title: Integration: End-to-End Auth Flow Testing
description:
Full end-to-end testing across all components. Start auth service (docker-compose), start loom serve --auth-url, test full flows. CLI auth is out of scope (ticket .14 is optional future work — do not gate E2E on it).

SECURITY TESTS: (1) OAuth state parameter — verify redirect URL contains non-empty state, verify callback rejects tampered state, verify callback rejects replayed state. (2) Redirect URI — verify callbackURL pointing to non-trusted origin is rejected. (3) Account linking — verify unverified GitHub email is NOT used for linking. (4) Session fixation — verify session token changes after successful OAuth sign-in. (5) JWT claims — verify issued JWT contains iss, aud, sub, email, jti claims with correct values. (6) Cross-system JWT confusion — send HS256 fleet JWT to ExtAuth → 401. Send RS256 user JWT to fleet auth → 401. (7) JWT in query param — send JWT in ?token= to regular API endpoint → rejected by middleware (only accepts from Authorization header). (8) Open mode — verify loom serve without --auth-url works with zero auth. (9) Auth service down — verify requests fail cleanly, no crash, no fallback to open. (10) Key rotation — rotate keys on auth service, verify Go cache refreshes. (11) JWKS kid storm — send 100 JWTs with random kid values, verify Go server does not make 100 JWKS fetches (cooldown enforced). (12) returnTo validation — verify sessionStorage returnTo with absolute URL is rejected. (13) Token exchange anti-leak — verify POST /api/auth/token response has Cache-Control: no-store. (14) SSE auth — verify GET /api/events without valid opaque token returns 401 when external auth enabled.

design: ## Summary Add a user menu to the header actions area (top-right of AppLayout) that shows the authenticated user's avatar and name, with a dropdown containing a Sign Out button. The menu is only rendered when `mode=external` and the user is authenticated (i.e., `useAuth()` returns `isAuthenticated=true` and `mode='external'`). In `mode=none`, the menu is omitted entirely — no placeholder, no empty space. After sign-out, the auth context clears the session and AuthGate automatically re-renders to show the LoginPage. ## Technical Approach ### Architecture The user menu lives in the **header actions area** of AppLayout (the `actions` prop slot, rendered top-right). It sits alongside ThemeToggle and ConnectionStatus in the `headerActions` div in App.tsx. This is the natural location — it's always visible, follows the standard SaaS convention of user menu in the top-right corner, and doesn't clutter the NavRail (which is for view switching, not user actions). ### Key Design Decisions 1. **Header actions area, not NavRail**. The task description says "NavRail or wherever the user menu will live." The NavRail is an icon-only vertical rail for view mode switching (kanban, list, terminal, settings). A user avatar/menu doesn't belong there — it's not a view mode. The header actions area (top-right) already has ThemeToggle and ConnectionStatus, making it the natural home for user identity. This follows the convention of GitHub, Linear, Slack, and virtually every SaaS app. 2. **New UserMenu component with dropdown**. A single component that renders: (a) a trigger button showing the user's avatar (image or initial) and name, and (b) a dropdown menu with a "Sign Out" option. The dropdown follows the existing pattern from PriorityDropdown/BackendSelectorDropdown (absolute positioning, `--z-dropdown`, keyboard nav, click-outside-to-close). This is a self-contained component — App.tsx just renders `` inside headerActions. 3. **Avatar handling: image URL with initial fallback, using shared colorUtils**. The `AuthUser` type from AuthContext (task .16) provides `image?: string` (the OAuth avatar URL from GitHub/Google). If present, render an `` tag. If absent or image fails to load (onError), fall back to an initial-letter avatar using `getAvatarColor` from `@/utils/colorUtils.ts`. This is the same shared utility already used by RepoBadge, AgentCard, AgentDetailPanel, and IssueCard — do NOT duplicate these functions. 4. **Conditional rendering via useAuth()**: The UserMenu component calls `useAuth()` internally. It returns `null` when `mode !== 'external'` or `!isAuthenticated`. This means App.tsx can always render `` — it self-gates. No conditional logic needed in App.tsx, keeping the integration minimal (just adding one component to headerActions). 5. **Single-device sign-out only**. The signOut() from AuthContext clears the local session, dispatches `CustomEvent('auth-sign-out')`, and clears the auth token. It does NOT invalidate sessions on other devices. After signOut() resolves, the auth context state changes → AuthGate detects !isAuthenticated → LoginPage renders. No manual redirect needed. 6. **Dropdown positioning: bottom-right aligned**. The trigger is in the top-right corner of the viewport. The dropdown opens downward, right-aligned with the trigger button (so it doesn't overflow off the right edge of the screen). Uses absolute positioning relative to the trigger wrapper. 7. **Click-outside and Escape to close**. Standard dropdown behavior: clicking outside the menu closes it, pressing Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger button. Uses a `useEffect` with `mousedown` event listener on `document` (same pattern as existing dropdowns in the codebase). 8. **No confirmation dialog for sign-out**. Sign-out is a low-risk, easily reversible action (user can just sign back in). Adding a confirmation modal would be friction without value. Click "Sign Out" → immediate sign-out. ### Component Structure ``` ├─

design:
## Summary

Comprehensive test coverage for the Better Auth integration frontend, spanning five unit test suites and one E2E Playwright suite. Unit tests cover appConfig.ts (config fetch/cache/error handling), authClient.ts (singleton lifecycle), AuthContext.tsx (providers, token sync, sign flows), AuthGate.tsx (rendering decisions, deep links, OAuth errors), and LoginPage.tsx (UI interactions, timeout, error states). E2E tests validate full browser flows for mode=open, mode=oidc, config errors (fail-closed), SSE token exchange, and multi-tab sign-out. Shared test utilities (mockAuthContext.ts, mockAuthClient.ts) eliminate duplication across consumer tests.

## Technical Approach

### Unit Test Strategy

All unit tests use Vitest with jsdom environment (@vitest-environment jsdom pragma). Auth module tests use vi.resetModules() + dynamic import in beforeEach to reset module-scoped singletons (config cache, auth client, pending refresh promises) between tests. Component tests mock useAuth() via vi.mock('@/contexts/AuthContext') and use @testing-library/react for rendering.

Key mock boundaries:
- appConfig.test.ts: mocks global.fetch directly (bare fetch, no API client)
- authClient.test.ts: mocks better-auth/react and better-auth/client/plugins via vi.doMock
- AuthContext.test.tsx: mocks @/api (setAuthToken, setAuthState, onAuthTokenExpired) and @/api/authClient (getAuthClient) — uses buildMockClient() helper (NOT createDefaultAuth)
- AuthGate.test.tsx: mocks @/contexts/AuthContext (useAuth) and @/components/LoginPage — uses createDefaultAuth from @/test-utils/mockAuthContext
- LoginPage.test.tsx: mocks @/contexts/AuthContext (useAuth) and @/hooks — uses createDefaultAuth from @/test-utils/mockAuthContext

The defaultAuth() consolidation targets exactly two files: AuthGate.test.tsx and LoginPage.test.tsx, which both import createDefaultAuth from @/test-utils/mockAuthContext. AuthContext.test.tsx is correctly excluded — it uses buildMockClient() because it tests the provider internals, not a consumer.

### E2E Test Strategy

E2E tests use Playwright with custom fixtures (tests/fixtures/base.ts) providing mockApi (ApiMockHandler) and mockSSE (SSEMockController). API mocking uses page.route() interceptors. The fixture includes mockConfig(), mockSession(), mockSseToken(), and mockAuth() helpers.

SSE mock gap addressed: all E2E tests in mode=open call mockApi.mockSseToken(null), which intercepts GET /api/workspaces/*/events/token and returns 404. This prevents SSE connection failures from polluting test results.

### Auth Mode Naming

The normalized field name is 'mode' (not 'auth_mode'). Values are 'open' (no auth) and 'oidc' (external auth). Tests use these exact values. The description's reference to 'auth_mode=none' is corrected to mode=open throughout.

### Fail-Closed Behavior

When /api/config returns an error (404, 500, timeout, non-JSON), fetchAppConfig() throws AppConfigError — it never falls back to {mode:'open'}. Tests verify this explicitly: 404 throws AppConfigError (not fallback to open), 500 throws, timeout throws, HTML response throws. E2E tests verify the BootError component renders with role=alert.

## Conventions Established

- Test utility imports: consumer component tests import from @/test-utils/mockAuthContext, not inline helpers
- Mock auth client: tests needing full auth client mock use createMockAuthClient from @/test-utils/mockAuthClient
- Module reset pattern: vi.resetModules() + dynamic import for any test file touching module-scoped singletons
- E2E fixture pattern: import { test, expect } from '../fixtures' (not @playwright/test directly)
- SSE token endpoint must always be mocked in E2E tests (null for 404, string for opaque token)

## Files to Create

None — all files exist.

## Files to Modify

None — all files are implemented. This design documents the existing test suite.

### Existing Files (Reference)

**Unit test files:**
1. src/api/__tests__/appConfig.test.ts — 10 tests: open response, oidc response, cache behavior, retry on failure, deduplication, network error, timeout, non-JSON, HTTP 500, unknown mode, missing auth_url, strips extra fields
2. src/api/__tests__/authClient.test.ts — 5 tests: client creation with correct config/plugins, singleton idempotency, getAuthClient returns singleton, getAuthClient throws when uninitialized, client has token method
3. src/contexts/__tests__/AuthContext.test.tsx — 12 tests: ExternalAuthProvider (token on active session, setAuthToken with JWT, no token while pending, null token on no session, authServiceDown on error, token failure handling, null token data). Sign flows (returnTo in sessionStorage, signIn.social call, signOut event dispatch, signOut clears token). NoAuthProvider (static context, no-op sign flows, no getAuthClient call). useAuth throws outside provider.
4. src/components/AuthGate/__tests__/AuthGate.test.tsx — 10 tests: returns null during loading, renders LoginPage when oidc + unauthenticated, renders children when authenticated, renders children in mode=open. OAuth error extraction from URL, URL cleanup after extraction, missing error param. Deep link restoration (valid path, rejects ://, rejects non-/ prefix, clears storage, handles storage errors, processes once).
5. src/components/LoginPage/__tests__/LoginPage.test.tsx — 10 tests: full-viewport dialog with aria, GitHub/Google buttons, title with aria-labelledby, all buttons type=button. Click calls signIn(provider), disables buttons during loading, shows Redirecting on clicked button. 10s timeout message, re-enables buttons after timeout. Error display (OAuth error, auth service down message, hides buttons when down, hides OAuth error when down, clears error on click).

**Test utilities:**
6. src/test-utils/mockAuthContext.ts — createDefaultAuth(), createAuthenticatedAuth(), createNoAuth() factories
7. src/test-utils/mockAuthClient.ts — createMockAuthClient() with MockAuthClient interface (state helpers: setAuthenticated, setUnauthenticated, setLoading, setError)

**E2E test files:**
8. tests/e2e/auth-integration.spec.ts — 11 tests across 5 describe blocks: mode=open (app loads, no auth requests, SSE without token), mode=oidc (login page unauthenticated, app renders authenticated, deep link restoration, OAuth error display), config errors (404 BootError, 500 BootError, HTML BootError, timeout BootError), SSE token exchange (opaque token in oidc, no token in open), multi-tab sign-out

**E2E infrastructure:**
9. tests/fixtures/base.ts — custom test fixture: mockApi, mockSSE, appPage fixtures
10. tests/helpers/api-mock.ts — ApiMockHandler with mockConfig, mockSession, mockSseToken, mockAuth, mockAll (includes config in mockAll)
11. tests/helpers/sse-mock.ts — SSEMockController for stream simulation

## Out of Scope

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. The smoke.spec.ts file imports from ../fixtures, ../helpers, and ../pages which all exist and work correctly. The mockAll() in api-mock.ts includes mockConfig as confirmed.

## Dependencies

- vitest + @testing-library/react + @testing-library/jest-dom (unit tests)
- @playwright/test (E2E tests)
- better-auth/react + better-auth/client/plugins (mocked in unit tests, route-intercepted in E2E)
- All auth source files: appConfig.ts, authClient.ts, AuthContext.tsx, AuthGate.tsx, LoginPage.tsx

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Module singleton leaks**: Each test using appConfig/authClient calls vi.resetModules() in beforeEach to prevent cached state from leaking. Failure to do this causes test order dependence.
2. **Fake timers + async**: appConfig timeout test uses vi.useFakeTimers() with vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(5001). The assertion promise must be registered BEFORE advancing timers to avoid unhandled rejection.
3. **sessionStorage SecurityError**: AuthGate deep link test verifies graceful handling when Storage.prototype.getItem throws SecurityError (private browsing mode).
4. **Re-render stability**: AuthGate test verifies returnTo is processed exactly once even across re-renders (via useRef guard).
5. **E2E mock ordering**: mockConfig must be registered BEFORE page.goto() — fetchAppConfig() fires immediately on boot. mockSseToken must be registered before the SSE mock's broader glob catches /api/events**.
6. **Multi-tab sign-out**: E2E test creates two pages in the same browser context, simulates sign-out on page1 via CustomEvent dispatch, changes session mock on page2 to return null, triggers focus event on page2 to simulate tab switch, and verifies LoginPage appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 5 unit test suites pass (appConfig, authClient, AuthContext, AuthGate, LoginPage)
2. auth-integration.spec.ts E2E suite passes in Playwright chromium project
3. fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on 404 (does NOT fall back to open mode)
4. fetchAppConfig throws AppConfigError on 500, timeout, non-JSON, unknown mode
5. AuthGate returns null (blank) during isLoading, LoginPage when unauthenticated in oidc mode, children when authenticated
6. AuthGate validates returnTo: rejects URLs containing :// or not starting with /
7. LoginPage disables both buttons during OAuth redirect loading
8. LoginPage shows timeout warning after 10 seconds of no redirect
9. LoginPage hides OAuth buttons when authServiceDown is true
10. ExternalAuthProvider calls authClient.token() to acquire JWT, not session cookie
11. signOut dispatches CustomEvent('auth-sign-out') for SSE/terminal cleanup
12. E2E: mode=open renders app without auth gate, makes no /api/auth/** requests
13. E2E: mode=oidc shows login page when session is null, renders app when session is valid
14. E2E: config errors (404, 500, HTML, timeout) all show BootError, never open mode
15. E2E: SSE uses opaque token in oidc mode, no token in open mode
16. mockAuthContext.ts provides createDefaultAuth imported by exactly AuthGate.test.tsx and LoginPage.test.tsx (not AuthContext.test.tsx)
17. mockAll() in api-mock.ts includes mockConfig

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests (vitest run):**
- Run all 5 test files via vitest run with jsdom environment
- Coverage: verify 80%+ line/branch/function coverage on auth source files
- Key scenarios: singleton caching, fail-closed errors, OAuth flow lifecycle, component rendering states, accessibility (aria attributes, focus trap)

**E2E tests (playwright test):**
- Run auth-integration.spec.ts in chromium project
- Uses page.route() for all API mocking — no real server needed
- Sanity gate: verify smoke.spec.ts still passes after any fixture changes
- Key scenarios: full boot sequence per auth mode, config error rendering, SSE token exchange, cross-tab sign-out propagation

**Manual verification:**
- Run loom serve with --auth-url to test real OAuth flow
- Verify login page renders, OAuth redirect works, deep link restores after login
- Open two tabs, sign out in one, verify other tab shows login page
- Test with network offline to verify fail-closed behavior
close_reason: All test files implemented and reviewed — design confirms no files to modify

comments.text:

title: Go: Extract isPublicRoute and extractToken into shared auth infrastructure
description: MUST be done BEFORE .8 (Remove API Key Auth). Extract isPublicRoute() and extractToken() from auth.go into a new file internal/webui/auth_routes.go. design:
## Summary

Extract the shared auth infrastructure functions — `isPublicRoute()`, `extractToken()`, and `stripWorkspacePrefix()` — from `internal/webui/auth.go` into a new file `internal/webui/auth_routes.go`, along with their corresponding tests into `internal/webui/auth_routes_test.go`. These functions are used by the current `NewAuthMiddleware` and will be needed by the future `NewExtAuthMiddleware`. Extracting them now ensures they survive the API key auth removal in ticket .8 without any risk of accidental deletion.

## Technical Approach

**Strategy**: Pure code-move refactor. Cut the three functions from `auth.go` and paste them into a new `auth_routes.go` file. Since both files are in the same `webui` package, no import changes or signature modifications are needed — all callers continue to reference the same unexported functions by name. This is the simplest possible approach: zero behavioral change, zero API surface change.

**Why `auth_routes.go`?**: The filename signals "route classification and token extraction for auth" — the shared infrastructure that any auth middleware (old API-key or new JWT/ExtAuth) depends on. This matches the task description's specified filename.

**What moves**: Exactly three functions plus their imports:
1. `isPublicRoute(method, path string) bool` — route classification (the critical safety function)
2. `stripWorkspacePrefix(path string) string` — helper used only by `isPublicRoute`
3. `extractToken(r *http.Request) string` — bearer/query-param token extraction

**What stays in `auth.go`**: Everything specific to the API-key auth system — `AuthConfig`, `NewAuthMiddleware`, `GenerateAPIKey`, `LoadOrCreateAPIKey`, `DefaultAPIKeyPath`, `handleAuthToken`, `handleAuthTokenDisabled`, and the `apiKeyLength` constant. These will be removed later by ticket .8.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/auth_routes.go`
New file containing the three extracted functions with their doc comments. Package `webui`. Imports needed: `"net/http"`, `"strings"`. The functions are copied verbatim — no modifications to logic or signatures.

Contents:
- `isPublicRoute(method, path string) bool` (lines 69-115 of current auth.go)
- `stripWorkspacePrefix(path string) string` (lines 117-135 of current auth.go)
- `extractToken(r *http.Request) string` (lines 137-153 of current auth.go)

### 2. `internal/webui/auth_routes_test.go`
New test file containing all tests for the three extracted functions. Package `webui`. Imports needed: `"net/http"`, `"net/http/httptest"`, `"testing"`.

Tests to move here:
- From `auth_test.go`: `TestIsPublicRoute` (line 237), `TestExtractToken_AuthorizationHeader` (line 295), `TestExtractToken_QueryParameter` (line 307), `TestExtractToken_MalformedAuthorizationHeader` (line 318), `TestExtractToken_NoAuth` (line 346), `TestExtractToken_HeaderTakesPrecedenceOverQuery` (line 357)
- From `auth_coverage_test.go`: `TestStripWorkspacePrefix_Various` (line 11), `TestIsPublicRoute_WorkspaceScoped` (line 199)

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/auth.go`
- **Remove** the `isPublicRoute` function (lines 69-115)
- **Remove** the `stripWorkspacePrefix` function (lines 117-135)
- **Remove** the `extractToken` function (lines 137-153)
- **Remove** `"strings"` from imports (only needed by the moved functions; the remaining code uses `crypto/subtle` for constant-time compare but does not use `strings`)
- Keep `"net/http"` in imports (still needed by `NewAuthMiddleware` and handler functions)
- All other code in `auth.go` remains unchanged

### 2. `internal/webui/auth_test.go`
- **Remove** `TestIsPublicRoute` (lines 236-291)
- **Remove** `TestExtractToken_AuthorizationHeader` (lines 293-303)
- **Remove** `TestExtractToken_QueryParameter` (lines 305-314)
- **Remove** `TestExtractToken_MalformedAuthorizationHeader` (lines 316-342)
- **Remove** `TestExtractToken_NoAuth` (lines 344-353)
- **Remove** `TestExtractToken_HeaderTakesPrecedenceOverQuery` (lines 355-365)
- **Remove** `"net/http/httptest"` from imports if no remaining tests use it (check: remaining tests like `TestNewAuthMiddleware_*` DO use `httptest`, so keep it)
- All `TestNewAuthMiddleware_*`, `TestGenerateAPIKey_*`, `TestLoadOrCreateAPIKey_*`, `TestHandleAuthToken*` tests remain

### 3. `internal/webui/auth_coverage_test.go`
- **Remove** `TestStripWorkspacePrefix_Various` (lines 9-51)
- **Remove** `TestIsPublicRoute_WorkspaceScoped` (lines 197-241)
- **Remove** `"testing"` from imports if no remaining tests need it (check: remaining `TestGenerateAPIKey_*` and `TestLoadOrCreateAPIKey_*` tests DO use `testing`, so keep it)
- All `TestGenerateAPIKey_*` and `TestLoadOrCreateAPIKey_*` tests remain

## Dependencies

- **No external packages** needed — the extracted functions only use stdlib (`net/http`, `strings`).
- **No internal module dependencies** — everything stays in the `webui` package.
- **No prerequisite tasks** — this is itself a prerequisite for .8 and .13.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Import cleanup**: After removing the three functions from `auth.go`, verify that `"strings"` is no longer needed there. If any remaining code in `auth.go` uses `strings`, keep the import. (Current analysis: `strings` is NOT used by any remaining functions in auth.go — `NewAuthMiddleware` calls `isPublicRoute` and `extractToken` which are moving, and the `handleAuthToken` function references `r.Header.Get` not `strings`.)

2. **Test helper `testHandler()`**: This helper is likely defined in a `_test.go` file in the `webui` package. Since test files in the same package share the test binary, `auth_routes_test.go` can call it without importing. Verify `testHandler()` is NOT needed by the moved tests (it's only used by `TestNewAuthMiddleware_*` tests which stay in `auth_test.go`). The moved tests only use `httptest.NewRequest` and direct function calls.

3. **`handlers_client_errors_test.go` and `handlers_csp_test.go`**: These files call `isPublicRoute()` directly in assertions (lines 210, 198 respectively). Since `isPublicRoute` stays in the same package, these require zero changes.

4. **No behavioral changes**: The refactor is purely structural. No function signatures, no logic, and no test assertions change. The invariant routes listed in the task description are exactly what `isPublicRoute` already enforces.

## Testing Strategy

### Automated Tests
Run after the refactor:
```bash
go test ./internal/webui/... -count=1
```
This verifies:
- All moved tests pass in their new file
- All remaining tests in `auth_test.go` and `auth_coverage_test.go` still compile and pass
- Tests in `handlers_client_errors_test.go` and `handlers_csp_test.go` that call `isPublicRoute` still work
- No import errors or undefined references

### Key Scenarios to Verify
1. **Build succeeds**: `go build ./cmd/loom/` — no compilation errors
2. **Vet passes**: `go vet ./internal/webui/...` — no issues
3. **All tests pass**: Full test suite for the webui package
4. **No duplicate definitions**: `grep -c 'func isPublicRoute' internal/webui/*.go` should return exactly 1 (in `auth_routes.go`)
5. **No duplicate definitions**: `grep -c 'func extractToken' internal/webui/*.go` should return exactly 1 (in `auth_routes.go`)
6. **No duplicate definitions**: `grep -c 'func stripWorkspacePrefix' internal/webui/*.go` should return exactly 1 (in `auth_routes.go`)

### Manual Verification
Not needed — this is a pure code-move refactor with no behavioral changes. The automated test suite provides full coverage.

design:
## Summary

This task removes all remaining API key auth configuration from the Go codebase after .8 (Go: Remove API Key Auth System) removes the middleware code. Specifically: ServerConfig struct fields (APIKey, AuthEnabled), CLI flags (--auth, --api-key), LOOM_WEBUI_API_KEY env var, DaemonSettings.APIKey/JWTKey, file management functions (GenerateAPIKey, LoadOrCreateAPIKey, DefaultAPIKeyPath), the serve.go plumbing that wires them together, and all related tests and documentation.

**BOUNDARY**: .8 removes middleware CODE (NewAuthMiddleware, handleAuthToken, handleAuthTokenDisabled, AuthConfig, /api/auth/token route, apiKey/authEnabled from setupRoutes, and the API key loading block in server.go). .27 removes CONFIG (struct fields, CLI flags, env vars, file management functions, daemon config, loom.yaml entries, documentation). .8 explicitly states "ServerConfig fields, CLI flags, env vars, and loom.yaml entries are NOT touched — those are owned by .27."

## Technical Approach

**Strategy**: After .8 removes all consumers of the auth config, ServerConfig.APIKey, ServerConfig.AuthEnabled, the --auth/--api-key flags, and the file management functions become dead code. This task sweeps all of them out.

**Post-.8 state**: After .8 merges, nothing in server.go reads ServerConfig.APIKey or AuthEnabled. serve.go still writes them (constructs the ServerConfig literal with these fields), the CLI flags still exist, the env var handling still runs — but it all feeds into struct fields that are never read. The file management functions (GenerateAPIKey, LoadOrCreateAPIKey, DefaultAPIKeyPath) in auth.go remain because .8 only deleted the middleware; their sole consumer was the API key loading block in server.go, which .8 removed.

**Post-.27 state**: ServerConfig has no auth fields. serve.go has no auth flags, env vars, or daemon config APIKey fallback. auth.go is deleted (empty after .8 removed middleware + .26 moved shared utilities to auth_routes.go + .27 removes file management). DaemonSettings has no APIKey/JWTKey. Related tests and docs are updated.

**Key decisions**:
1. **auth.go is DELETED** — after .8 removes middleware functions and .26 moves isPublicRoute/extractToken/stripWorkspacePrefix to auth_routes.go, only file management functions remain. This task removes those, leaving the file empty.
2. **auth_test.go is DELETED** — after .8 removes middleware tests, only GenerateAPIKey/LoadOrCreateAPIKey tests remain. This task removes those.
3. **auth_coverage_test.go is DELETED** — after .26 moves isPublicRoute/stripWorkspacePrefix tests to auth_routes_test.go, only GenerateAPIKey/LoadOrCreateAPIKey tests remain. This task removes those.
4. **DaemonSettings.JWTKey is also removed** — it was never consumed by any code (no reader of dc.Daemon.JWTKey exists). Dead config field.
5. **Frontend test helpers are OUT OF SCOPE** — the E2E helpers (helpers.ts, playwright.config.ts) read ~/.loom/webui-api-key and use LOOM_API_KEY. These should be updated when the frontend auth integration tasks (.11, .16, .17) land, not here.

## Conventions Established

- Follows .8/.27 boundary convention: .8 = middleware code, .27 = config layer
- After .27, no auth-related fields remain in ServerConfig or DaemonSettings (fleet auth fields FleetAPIKey/FleetJWTKey are a separate system and UNTOUCHED)

title: Frontend: Migrate direct getAuthToken consumers to fetchApi
description:
SECURITY PREREQUISITE — 5 files bypass fetchApi() and call getAuthToken() directly to build their own Authorization headers with raw fetch(). This means they miss the 401 interceptor and will not trigger re-auth on JWT expiry. They also will not respond to sign-out events that clear authToken. Until these are migrated, expiry and sign-out behavior is inconsistent across the frontend.

design:
## Summary

This is a normative decision task that resolves an inconsistency across the Better Auth JWT epic: the downstream tasks (.4, .5, .7) originally had conflicting algorithm specifications (EdDSA vs RS256 vs mixed). The decision is: **RS256 everywhere, no EdDSA**. This task documents the rationale, identifies the specific changes required in each downstream ticket's design, and confirms the Go ecosystem supports this cleanly.

## Decision: RS256 Only

**Algorithm:** RS256 (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 using SHA-256)
**Key type:** RSA (kty: RSA, with n/e fields in JWKS)
**Minimum key size:** 2048 bits

### Rationale

1. **golang-jwt/jwt/v5 native support** — RS256 is natively supported (already in go.mod v5.3.1). The existing fleet JWT code in jwt.go uses this library with HS256, so the team is familiar with it. EdDSA requires either golang.org/x/crypto (for ed25519) or lestrrat-go/jwx, adding new dependencies.

2. **Better Auth compatibility** — Better Auth's JWT plugin supports RS256 via keyPairConfig: {alg: 'RS256'}. RS256 is the default and best-tested path.

3. **JWKS simplicity** — RSA public keys in JWKS use kty: RSA with n (modulus) and e (exponent) fields, which are simple big-integer base64url values. EdDSA/OKP keys use a different structure (kty: OKP, crv: Ed25519, x field). Supporting only RSA means the JWKS parser is simpler and has less surface area for bugs.

4. **Industry standard** — RS256 is the most widely supported JWKS/JWT algorithm. Every JWKS consumer and producer supports it. EdDSA adoption is growing but not universal.

5. **No performance concern** — JWT verification is not on the hot path (one verify per request, cached JWKS keys). RS256 verification performance is more than adequate.

## Changes Required in Downstream Tasks

### Task .4 (Auth Service: JWT Plugin and JWKS Endpoint) — CONFIRMED CORRECT
The description already specifies RS256:
- keyPairConfig: {alg: 'RS256'} ✓
- JWKS returns RSA public keys (kty: RSA, n, e fields) ✓
- No changes needed to .4's description.
- **Design impact:** When .4 gets a design, it should NOT include any EdDSA/OKP configuration.

### Task .5 (Go: JWKS Cache Implementation) — DESIGN NEEDS UPDATE
The current design (in review) includes EdDSA/OKP support that must be removed:
- **Remove** OKP key type parsing (crv, x fields for Ed25519)
- **Remove** EdDSA from the cachedKey.Algorithm values
- **Remove** crypto/ed25519 import
- **Remove** TestJWKSCache_FetchAndLookup_EdDSA test case
- **Simplify** jwkKey struct: remove Crv and X fields (OKP-specific)
- **Simplify** parseJWK: only handle kty=RSA, return error for anything else
- **Simplify** GetKey signature: algorithm return value is always "RS256", but keep it for forward compatibility
- **Update** description to say "RSA public keys" not "RSA/EdDSA public keys"

### Task .7 (Go: External Auth JWT Verification Middleware) — DESIGN NEEDS UPDATE
The current design (in review) includes EdDSA acceptance that must be removed:
- **Remove** jwt.SigningMethodEdDSA case from the algorithm switch in keyfunc
- **Simplify** to: only jwt.SigningMethodRS256 is allowed, everything else returns error
- **Remove** TestExtAuth_EdDSA test cases (if any referenced in design)
- **Update** algorithm mismatch error: token algorithm must be RS256, key algorithm must be RS256
- **Update** comments referencing "RS256 or EdDSA" to just "RS256"

## Implementation Actions for This Task

This is a decision task — no code changes. The implementation actions are:
1. ✅ Document the RS256-only decision (this design field)
2. ⬜ Update .5's design to remove EdDSA references (to be done by reviewer or when .5 design is revised)
3. ⬜ Update .7's design to remove EdDSA references (to be done by reviewer or when .7 design is revised)
4. ⬜ Confirm .4's description is RS256-aligned (already confirmed above)

## Dependencies

- **Blocks:** .4, .5, .7 — these tasks cannot begin implementation until this decision is finalized
- **No code dependencies** — this is a design decision, not a code artifact

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

Not applicable — this is a decision task. Edge cases for RS256 implementation are covered in the downstream task designs (.5, .7).

## Testing Strategy

Not applicable — no code produced. Verification is:
1. Reviewer confirms RS256-only is correct
2. Reviewer ensures .5 and .7 designs are updated to remove EdDSA before those tasks are approved for implementation
close_reason: RS256 decision documented and verified. All downstream tasks (.4, .5, .7) already aligned: no EdDSA/OKP references remain in any design. .5 uses RSA-only jwkKey struct. .7 uses RS256 pointer identity check. .4 configures alg:RS256.

title: Go: JWKS Cache Implementation
description: Create internal/webui/jwks.go. JWKSCache fetches and caches RSA public keys from a JWKS endpoint. RS256 ONLY — no EdDSA, no EC keys. sync.RWMutex for concurrent reads (consistent with existing codebase patterns). Background goroutine refreshes every 5min. SECURITY — On-demand refresh protection: Use a SINGLE singleflight key ("jwks-refresh") for ALL on-demand refreshes, NOT per-kid. Add 10-second cooldown between on-demand refreshes. Add NEGATIVE CACHE for unknown kid values (30-second TTL). Cap maximum keys from JWKS to 10. SECURITY — Empty kid handling: try ALL cached keys, not just first. Add 24-hour max staleness bound. Gotchas: base64.RawURLEncoding for n/e fields, reject keys <2048 bits, empty JWKS retains cache, 64KB MaxBytesReader, safeDialContext for SSRF, TLS verification uses Go defaults. Create jwks_test.go with full coverage including cooldown, negative cache, kid storm, max keys, try-all-keys, staleness.
design:
## Summary

Implement a JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) cache for the Go WebUI server that fetches and caches RSA public keys from a remote JWKS endpoint. RS256 ONLY — no EdDSA, no EC keys. This is the foundation for external auth JWT verification — the downstream middleware (loomcli-laf73.7) will call into this cache to look up public keys by `kid` (Key ID) when validating Bearer JWTs from the Better Auth service. The cache must be safe for concurrent access, resilient to auth service outages, and protected against SSRF.

## Technical Approach

**Core type: `JWKSCache`** — a struct that holds cached public keys and manages background refresh. Uses `sync.RWMutex` for concurrent reads (consistent with existing codebase patterns in subscription.go, sse.go) rather than `atomic.Pointer` (not used elsewhere in this codebase). Background goroutine refreshes every 5 minutes. On-demand refresh with `singleflight.Group` using a SINGLE key `"jwks-refresh"` for ALL on-demand refreshes (NOT per-kid) — this prevents an attacker from triggering unbounded JWKS fetches with unique kid values. 10-second cooldown between on-demand refreshes. Negative cache for unknown kid values (30-second TTL). Cap max keys accepted from JWKS to 10. 24-hour max staleness bound.

**Key design decisions:**
- **No new dependencies** — uses `golang.org/x/sync/singleflight` (already available as transitive dep, or add if needed) for dedup. Standard `crypto/rsa` for key types.
- **RS256 only** — no EdDSA/OKP/Ed25519 support. Only RSA keys with RS256 algorithm are accepted.
- **Manual JWK parsing** — parse the JWKS JSON manually (it's a simple format: `{"keys": [{"kty","kid","n","e",...}]}`) rather than adding a heavy JWKS library. This keeps dependencies minimal and gives full control over validation (key size checks, algorithm restrictions).
- **SSRF protection** — reuse the existing `safeDialContext(false)` from `loom_proxy.go` for the HTTP transport.
- **Defensive caching** — empty JWKS response retains previous cache (prevents lockout if auth service returns empty during rotation). Malformed JSON or HTTP errors also retain cache.

**Interface contract for downstream (loomcli-laf73.7):**
```go
// GetKey returns the RSA public key for the given kid, or tries all keys if kid is empty.
// RS256 only — always returns *rsa.PublicKey.
func (c *JWKSCache) GetKey(kid string) (*rsa.PublicKey, error)
```

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/jwks.go`
The main JWKS cache implementation.

**Types:**
```go
// jwksResponse represents the JSON structure of a JWKS endpoint response.
type jwksResponse struct {
    Keys []jwkKey `json:"keys"`
}

// jwkKey represents a single JWK entry.
type jwkKey struct {
    Kty string `json:"kty"`  // Key type: "RSA"
    Kid string `json:"kid"`  // Key ID
    Alg string `json:"alg"`  // Algorithm: "RS256"
    Use string `json:"use"`  // Key use: "sig"
    N   string `json:"n"`    // RSA modulus (base64url)
    E   string `json:"e"`    // RSA exponent (base64url)
}

// JWKSCache fetches and caches public keys from a JWKS endpoint.
type JWKSCache struct {
    endpoint   string
    client     *http.Client
    logger     *slog.Logger

    mu         sync.RWMutex
    keys       map[string]*rsa.PublicKey  // kid → *rsa.PublicKey
    allKeys    []*rsa.PublicKey           // ordered list for kid-absent fallback
    lastFetch  time.Time                 // for max staleness bound (24h)

    refreshGroup singleflight.Group
    lastOnDemand time.Time               // for 10-second cooldown between on-demand refreshes
    negativeCache map[string]time.Time   // kid → expiry time for negative cache (30s TTL)

    done       chan struct{}
}
```

**Constructor:**
```go
func NewJWKSCache(endpoint string, client *http.Client, logger *slog.Logger) *JWKSCache
```
- If `client` is nil, creates one with `safeDialContext(false)` transport, 10s timeout, 64KB response body cap via `http.MaxBytesReader`.
- Performs initial synchronous fetch (logs warning on failure, doesn't fail startup).
- Starts background refresh goroutine (5-minute interval).

**Public methods:**
```go
// GetKey returns the RSA public key for the given kid.
// If kid is empty, tries ALL cached keys (not just first) — caller should attempt
// signature verification with each until one succeeds. Returns the list via iteration.
// If kid is not found in cache, checks negative cache (30s TTL), then triggers
// an on-demand refresh (with singleflight dedup, single key "jwks-refresh", 10s cooldown)
// and retries once. Returns error if key still not found after refresh.
func (c *JWKSCache) GetKey(kid string) (*rsa.PublicKey, error)

// Stop shuts down the background refresh goroutine.
func (c *JWKSCache) Stop()
```

**Internal methods:**
```go
// fetch retrieves and parses the JWKS from the endpoint.
// On success, updates the cache. On failure, retains existing cache and logs the error.
// Caps max keys accepted from JWKS response to 10.
func (c *JWKSCache) fetch(ctx context.Context) error

// parseJWK converts a single jwkKey into an *rsa.PublicKey.
// Validates: RSA keys must be >= 2048 bits. Only kty="RSA" is accepted.
// Uses base64.RawURLEncoding (NOT StdEncoding) for n/e fields.
func parseJWK(key jwkKey) (*rsa.PublicKey, error)

// refreshLoop runs the background refresh on a ticker.
func (c *JWKSCache) refreshLoop(interval time.Duration)
```

**Critical implementation details:**
- `base64.RawURLEncoding` for decoding `n`, `e` fields (JWKS standard uses unpadded base64url)
- RSA key size check: `pubKey.N.BitLen() < 2048` → reject with error
- `http.MaxBytesReader(nil, resp.Body, 64*1024)` to cap response body at 64KB
- Empty `keys` array in response → retain existing cache, log warning
- HTTP non-200 status → retain existing cache, log error with status code
- JSON decode error → retain existing cache, log error
- Cap max keys from JWKS response to 10 — skip additional keys with warning
- `singleflight.Group` with a SINGLE key `"jwks-refresh"` for ALL on-demand refreshes (NOT per-kid). This prevents kid-storm attacks where an attacker sends JWTs with unique kid values to trigger unbounded fetches.
- 10-second cooldown between on-demand refreshes — if last on-demand refresh was <10s ago, skip and return cache miss immediately
- Negative cache for unknown kid values — after an on-demand refresh, if kid is still not found, cache that miss for 30 seconds. Subsequent lookups for the same kid within 30s return error immediately without triggering another refresh.
- 24-hour max staleness bound — if `lastFetch` is older than 24 hours and JWKS endpoint is unreachable, reject cached keys (return error even if keys exist in cache)
- Empty kid handling: when kid is empty, try ALL cached keys (not just first). The caller iterates and attempts signature verification with each key until one succeeds. This is robust during key rotation when array order is unspecified.
- Background goroutine exits when `done` channel is closed (via `Stop()`)
- All logging via `*slog.Logger` (consistent with `ServerConfig.Logger` pattern)

### 2. `internal/webui/jwks_test.go`
Comprehensive tests using `httptest.Server` to mock the JWKS endpoint.

**Test setup:**
- Pre-generate RSA key pair (2048-bit) at package level using `crypto/rsa.GenerateKey`
- Helper function to create a valid JWKS JSON response from pre-generated keys
- Helper to create `httptest.Server` returning configurable JWKS responses

**Test cases:**
1. `TestJWKSCache_FetchAndLookup_RSA` — successful fetch, lookup by kid returns correct RSA key
2. `TestJWKSCache_KeyMiss_TriggersRefresh` — lookup unknown kid triggers on-demand refresh, new key found after server updates
3. `TestJWKSCache_KeyMiss_Cooldown` — second on-demand refresh within 10s is skipped, returns error immediately
4. `TestJWKSCache_NegativeCache` — unknown kid after refresh is cached as miss for 30s, subsequent lookups skip refresh
5. `TestJWKSCache_KidStormProtection` — 100 concurrent requests with unique kids result in only one JWKS fetch (singleflight with single key)
6. `TestJWKSCache_EmptyJWKS_RetainsCache` — server returns `{"keys":[]}`, existing cached keys preserved
7. `TestJWKSCache_MalformedJSON_RetainsCache` — server returns garbage, existing cache preserved
8. `TestJWKSCache_OversizedBody_Rejected` — server returns >64KB body, fetch fails gracefully
9. `TestJWKSCache_WeakRSAKey_Rejected` — 1024-bit RSA key in JWKS is skipped/rejected
10. `TestJWKSCache_MaxKeysEnforced` — JWKS with >10 keys only caches first 10
11. `TestJWKSCache_ConcurrentAccess` — multiple goroutines calling GetKey simultaneously with `-race` flag
12. `TestJWKSCache_Stop_HaltsBackground` — calling Stop() prevents further fetches
13. `TestJWKSCache_KidAbsent_TriesAllKeys` — GetKey("") tries all cached keys, not just first
14. `TestJWKSCache_HTTPError_RetainsCache` — server returns 500, cache preserved
15. `TestJWKSCache_Base64RawURL_Decoding` — verifies RawURLEncoding (no padding) works correctly
16. `TestJWKSCache_MaxStaleness` — cached keys older than 24h are rejected when endpoint is unreachable

**Test pattern:** Follow existing `jwt_test.go` style — table-driven where appropriate, direct assertions (`t.Errorf`/`t.Fatalf`), `httptest.NewServer` for mock endpoint.

## Files to Modify

None. This is a self-contained new module. The downstream task (loomcli-laf73.7) will wire it into the middleware and `ServerConfig`. The removal task (loomcli-laf73.8) will handle removing the old API key auth.

## Dependencies

**External packages (already in go.mod):**
- `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` — not directly used in this file, but the parsed keys will be consumed by jwt/v5's `ParseWithClaims` in the downstream middleware
- Standard library: `crypto/rsa`, `encoding/base64`, `encoding/json`, `net/http`, `sync`, `log/slog`, `math/big`, `time`

**May need to add to go.mod:**
- `golang.org/x/sync` — for `singleflight.Group`. Check if already a transitive dependency; if not, `go get golang.org/x/sync`.

**Internal dependencies:**
- `safeDialContext(false)` from `loom_proxy.go` — already in same package, no import needed

**Task dependencies:**
- No blocking dependencies — this task can be implemented independently
- Blocks: `loomcli-laf73.7` (JWT verification middleware uses `JWKSCache.GetKey()`)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Auth service down at startup** — initial fetch fails, cache is empty. GetKey returns error. Log warning but don't crash. Background refresh will retry.
2. **Auth service goes down after initial fetch** — cache retains last-known-good keys. Background refresh logs errors but doesn't evict cache. After 24 hours of unreachability, max staleness bound kicks in and keys are rejected.
3. **Key rotation** — new kid appears in incoming JWT. GetKey misses cache → checks negative cache → triggers on-demand refresh (subject to 10s cooldown) → picks up rotated keys from JWKS endpoint.
4. **Empty JWKS response** — `{"keys":[]}` is valid JSON but means "no keys." Retain previous cache (defensive). This handles the case where auth service is misconfigured during key rotation.
5. **Oversized response** — `MaxBytesReader` at 64KB prevents memory exhaustion from malicious endpoint.
6. **SSRF** — `safeDialContext(false)` prevents the JWKS fetcher from being pointed at internal services.
7. **Kid storm attack** — attacker sends JWTs with many unique kid values. `singleflight.Group` with single key `"jwks-refresh"` ensures only one fetch is in-flight regardless of how many different kids are requested. 10-second cooldown prevents rapid successive fetches. Negative cache prevents repeated lookups for the same unknown kid.
8. **Weak keys** — RSA <2048 bits rejected during parsing. Logged as warning, key skipped (not added to cache).
9. **Too many keys** — JWKS response with >10 keys only caches first 10. Prevents memory bloat from large JWKS responses.
10. **base64 encoding mismatch** — JWKS spec requires `base64.RawURLEncoding` (no padding). Using `StdEncoding` would silently produce wrong keys. Tests explicitly verify correct decoding.
11. **Context cancellation** — fetch uses context with 10s timeout. Background refresh uses `context.Background()` with the HTTP client timeout as the bound.
12. **Graceful shutdown** — `Stop()` closes the `done` channel, background goroutine exits. No leaked goroutines.
13. **Empty kid during key rotation** — when JWT has no kid header, try ALL cached keys. This is robust when key order in the JWKS array is unspecified.

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests (jwks_test.go):**
- All 16 test cases listed above
- Run with `go test -race ./internal/webui/ -run TestJWKS` to verify concurrent safety
- Pre-generated keys avoid slow key generation in CI (generate once at test package init)

**Manual verification:**
1. Start a local JWKS mock server (`httptest.Server` or standalone script)
2. Create `JWKSCache` pointing at mock server
3. Verify `GetKey(kid)` returns correct key type
4. Stop mock server → verify cache retains keys
5. Restart mock server with new keys → verify background refresh picks them up

**Integration (deferred to loomcli-laf73.22):**
- Full end-to-end with Better Auth service minting JWTs and Go server verifying them

design:
## Summary

Implement an HTTP middleware (`NewExtAuthMiddleware`) that validates Bearer JWT tokens from an external Better Auth service. The middleware extracts JWTs exclusively from the `Authorization` header, validates signatures against public keys from the JWKS cache (loomcli-laf73.5), enforces strict RS256-only algorithm restriction via pointer identity check, and injects a `UserIdentity` struct into the request context for downstream handlers. This is the core authentication gate for "external" auth mode — when `ExtAuthURL` is configured, every protected API request must carry a valid JWT.

Additionally, this task adds a defense-in-depth guard to `extractToken()` that rejects query-param tokens that look like JWTs, and implements `UserIdentity.String()` with PII redaction for safe logging.

## Technical Approach

**Middleware signature follows existing codebase convention:** `NewExtAuthMiddleware(cfg ExtAuthConfig) func(http.Handler) http.Handler` — same closure-returning pattern used by `NewAuthMiddleware` (auth.go:28), `NewCORSMiddleware` (cors.go:18), `NewSecurityHeadersMiddleware` (security.go:13), `NewFleetAuthMiddleware` (fleet_auth.go:18), and `NewRateLimitMiddleware` (ratelimit.go:54).

**Key design decisions:**

1. **Use `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` (already in go.mod)** — same library used by fleet JWT auth in `jwt.go`. Use `jwt.ParseWithClaims` with a custom `Keyfunc` that calls `JWKSCache.GetKey(kid)`. The `kid` is extracted from the token header inside the keyfunc.

2. **Algorithm restriction via pointer identity check** — inside the keyfunc, verify `token.Method == jwt.SigningMethodRS256` (pointer identity, NOT string comparison). RS256 ONLY — no EdDSA, no HS256. This prevents alg:none attacks, HMAC confusion attacks, and custom SigningMethod spoofing. Do NOT rely on parser options alone — the keyfunc is the authoritative check.

3. **Parser options** — use `jwt.WithExpirationRequired()`, `jwt.WithIssuedAt()`, `jwt.WithLeeway(5*time.Second)`, `jwt.WithIssuer(cfg.Issuer)`, `jwt.WithAudience(cfg.Audience)`. These enforce that `exp` and `iat` claims exist, clock skew is bounded (5s — NTP makes 30s unnecessary), and issuer/audience match configuration.

4. **Token size cap (8192 bytes)** — check `len(tokenStr) > 8192` before parsing. Prevents the JWT parser from spending CPU on pathologically large tokens. Return 400 (malformed) not 401 (auth failure).

5. **UserIdentity struct** — extracted from custom JWT claims (`sub`, `email`, `name`). NO OrgID — that is a follow-up epic (loomcli-1voxb). Stored in request context using an unexported context key (same pattern as `workerClaimsContextKey` in `fleet_auth.go:11`).

6. **UserIdentity.String() with PII redaction** — the `String()` method returns only the UserID, redacting email and name. Format: `UserIdentity{UserID: "user-abc123"}`. This ensures `fmt.Printf("%v", identity)` or `slog.Any("user", identity)` never leaks PII into logs. The description explicitly requires this.

7. **Required claim: `sub`** — if the parsed JWT lacks a `sub` claim, reject with 401. The `sub` is the user's unique ID from Better Auth. `email` and `name` are optional (may be empty).

8. **Public route and OPTIONS passthrough** — reuse `isPublicRoute()` from `auth_routes.go` (.26) for route exemptions. OPTIONS requests always pass through for CORS preflight.

9. **Own token extraction — NOT `extractToken()`** — the middleware extracts JWTs ONLY from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. It does NOT call `extractToken()` because that function has a query-param fallback intended for opaque tokens (SSE, terminal). The middleware has its own inline extraction logic that reads only the Authorization header.

10. **Defense-in-depth guard on `extractToken()`** — separately, this task modifies `extractToken()` in `auth.go` (or `auth_routes.go` if .26 has landed) to reject query-param tokens that look like JWTs: tokens containing two dots (`.`) and longer than 200 characters are rejected with empty string return. This prevents accidental JWT leakage into query strings even if a downstream handler calls `extractToken()`. The guard only applies to query-param tokens, not Authorization header tokens.

11. **Error response format** — use `respondError(w, status, message)` from `respond.go` (same as existing `NewAuthMiddleware`). Error messages are safe/generic — never include token contents or detailed crypto errors.

12. **Disabled mode** — if `cfg.JWKSCache` is nil (open mode), return a passthrough middleware. Same pattern as `NewAuthMiddleware` when `!config.Enabled`.

13. **Never log raw tokens** — error logging uses the logger from config but only logs the error classification, never the token string itself.

## Conventions Established

- **Context key pattern**: `type userIdentityContextKey struct{}` + `UserIdentityFromContext(ctx) (UserIdentity, bool)` — follows the established pattern from `workerClaimsContextKey` in fleet_auth.go and `workspaceContextKey` in workspace_context.go.
- **PII redaction**: `UserIdentity.String()` shows only UserID. All future identity types in this epic should follow the same redaction pattern.
- **JWT extraction for ExtAuth**: Authorization header only. Query-param tokens are never JWTs — they are opaque tokens validated by their respective handlers (sseAuth, terminalAuth).
- **Algorithm enforcement**: Pointer identity comparison (`token.Method == jwt.SigningMethodRS256`), not string comparison. This convention must be followed by any future code that validates JWTs in this codebase.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/ext_auth.go`

The external auth JWT verification middleware.

**Types:**

```go
// UserIdentity represents the authenticated user extracted from a JWT.
type UserIdentity struct {
    UserID string // JWT "sub" claim — unique user ID from Better Auth
    Email  string // JWT "email" claim (optional, may be empty)
    Name   string // JWT "name" claim (optional, may be empty)
}

// String returns a redacted representation safe for logging.
// Only UserID is included; Email and Name are omitted to prevent PII leakage.
func (u UserIdentity) String() string {
    return fmt.Sprintf("UserIdentity{UserID: %q}", u.UserID)
}

// userIdentityContextKey is the unexported context key for storing UserIdentity.
type userIdentityContextKey struct{}

// ExtAuthConfig holds configuration for the external auth middleware.
type ExtAuthConfig struct {
    JWKSCache *JWKSCache    // JWKS cache for public key lookup; nil = passthrough (open mode)
    Issuer    string        // Expected JWT issuer (validated against "iss" claim)
    Audience  string        // Expected JWT audience (validated against "aud" claim)
    Logger    *slog.Logger  // Structured logger (nil falls back to slog.Default())
}

// extAuthClaims extends jwt.RegisteredClaims with Better Auth custom fields.
type extAuthClaims struct {
    Email string `json:"email"`
    Name  string `json:"name"`
    jwt.RegisteredClaims
}
```

**Functions:**

```go
// NewExtAuthMiddleware creates a middleware that validates Bearer JWTs from an
// external auth service using cached JWKS public keys. When cfg.JWKSCache is nil,
// returns a passthrough middleware (open mode).
func NewExtAuthMiddleware(cfg ExtAuthConfig) func(http.Handler) http.Handler

// UserIdentityFromContext extracts UserIdentity from the request context.
// Returns zero-value UserIdentity and false if not present.
func UserIdentityFromContext(ctx context.Context) (UserIdentity, bool)
```

**Implementation details for `NewExtAuthMiddleware`:**

- If `cfg.JWKSCache == nil`, return passthrough (just calls `next.ServeHTTP`)
- Resolve logger: if `cfg.Logger == nil`, use `slog.Default()`
- For each request:
  1. If `r.Method == http.MethodOptions` → pass through (CORS preflight)
  2. If `isPublicRoute(r.Method, r.URL.Path)` → pass through
  3. Extract JWT from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header ONLY (inline extraction, NOT `extractToken()`). Case-insensitive "Bearer" prefix check per RFC 6750 (using `strings.EqualFold` on first 7 chars, matching the convention established by .26).
  4. If Authorization header is empty or missing Bearer prefix → `respondError(w, 401, "authentication required")`
  5. If `len(token) > 8192` → `respondError(w, 400, "malformed token")`
  6. Parse with `jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &extAuthClaims{}, keyfunc, parserOpts...)`
     - keyfunc: extract `kid` from `token.Header["kid"]`, call `cfg.JWKSCache.GetKey(kid)`, verify algorithm pointer identity
     - parserOpts: `jwt.WithExpirationRequired()`, `jwt.WithIssuedAt()`, `jwt.WithLeeway(5*time.Second)`, `jwt.WithIssuer(cfg.Issuer)`, `jwt.WithAudience(cfg.Audience)`
  7. If parse error → classify error and respond:
     - `jwt.ErrTokenMalformed` → `respondError(w, 400, "malformed token")`
     - All other errors (expired, wrong sig, bad claims) → `respondError(w, 401, "invalid or expired token")`
     - Log the error classification (NOT the token) at debug level
  8. Extract `sub` from `claims.Subject`. If empty → `respondError(w, 401, "invalid token claims")`
  9. Build `UserIdentity{UserID: claims.Subject, Email: claims.Email, Name: claims.Name}`
  10. Inject into context: `ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), userIdentityContextKey{}, identity)`
  11. Call `next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))`

**Algorithm verification in keyfunc (critical security logic):**
```go
func(token *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) {
    // Strict algorithm check: RS256 ONLY via pointer identity
    // This prevents alg:none, HMAC confusion, and custom SigningMethod spoofing
    if token.Method != jwt.SigningMethodRS256 {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported signing algorithm: %v", token.Method.Alg())
    }

    // Extract kid from header
    kid, _ := token.Header["kid"].(string)
    // GetKey handles kid="" by trying all keys, and triggers on-demand refresh for unknown kids
    key, err := cfg.JWKSCache.GetKey(kid)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("key lookup failed: %w", err)
    }

    return key, nil
}
```

### 2. `internal/webui/ext_auth_test.go`

Comprehensive test file following the patterns in `fleet_auth_test.go` and `jwt_test.go`.

**Test setup:**
- Pre-generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair at package test init: `rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)`
- Helper: `signExtAuthJWT(t, claims, key, kid, method)` — creates a signed JWT with the given claims, key, kid header, and signing method
- Helper: create a real `JWKSCache` backed by `httptest.Server` returning a JWKS JSON for the test RSA key. This tests the middleware + cache integration naturally.
- Note: The JWKS endpoint path used by the test server does not matter (it's just the httptest URL) — the real path `/api/auth/jwks` is configured at the wiring layer (.13).

**Test cases (19 tests):**

1. **TestExtAuth_Passthrough_WhenNilCache** — `ExtAuthConfig{JWKSCache: nil}` produces passthrough middleware; request with no auth header reaches inner handler.

2. **TestExtAuth_ValidJWT_InjectsIdentity** — Valid RS256 JWT with sub/email/name claims. Verify inner handler receives correct `UserIdentity` from context. Verify UserID, Email, and Name are all populated correctly.

3. **TestExtAuth_ExpiredJWT_Returns401** — JWT with `exp` in the past (beyond 5s leeway). Verify 401 response.

4. **TestExtAuth_WrongKey_Returns401** — JWT signed with a different RSA key than what JWKS serves. Verify 401.

5. **TestExtAuth_WrongIssuer_Returns401** — JWT with `iss` that doesn't match `cfg.Issuer`. Verify 401.

6. **TestExtAuth_WrongAudience_Returns401** — JWT with `aud` that doesn't match `cfg.Audience`. Verify 401.

7. **TestExtAuth_MissingSub_Returns401** — JWT with valid signature but empty/missing `sub` claim. Verify 401 with "invalid token claims".

8. **TestExtAuth_MissingExp_Returns401** — JWT without `exp` claim. Verify 401 (due to `WithExpirationRequired`).

9. **TestExtAuth_AlgNone_Returns401** — JWT with `alg: none` and no signature. Verify 401 (algorithm pointer identity check rejects it).

10. **TestExtAuth_HS256Confusion_Returns401** — JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the RSA public key as the HMAC secret (classic confusion attack). Verify 401 (pointer identity check rejects `*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC`).

11. **TestExtAuth_CustomSigningMethodSpoofing_Returns401** — Define a custom `SigningMethod` struct that returns "RS256" from `Alg()` but is a distinct type from `*jwt.SigningMethodRSA`. Sign a token with it. Verify 401 because pointer identity check (`token.Method != jwt.SigningMethodRS256`) catches this even though `Alg()` returns the right string.

12. **TestExtAuth_OversizedToken_Returns400** — Token string >8192 bytes. Verify 400 response with "malformed token" (not 401).

13. **TestExtAuth_MissingToken_Returns401** — Request with no Authorization header to a protected route. Verify 401 with "authentication required".

14. **TestExtAuth_OptionsPassthrough** — OPTIONS request to a protected route passes through without auth. Inner handler is called.

15. **TestExtAuth_KidAbsentFallback** — JWT without `kid` header field. Middleware calls `GetKey("")` which tries all cached keys. Verify successful auth.

16. **TestExtAuth_ClockSkewWithinLeeway_Accepted** — JWT that expired 3 seconds ago (within 5s leeway). Verify 200 (accepted).

17. **TestExtAuth_ClockSkewBeyondLeeway_Rejected** — JWT that expired 7 seconds ago (beyond 5s leeway). Verify 401 (rejected).

18. **TestExtAuth_PublicRoutePassthrough** — Request to `/health` without auth passes through. Inner handler is called.

19. **TestExtAuth_CrossSystem_FleetJWTAgainstExtAuth_Returns401** — Generate a valid HS256 fleet worker JWT using `GenerateWorkerToken()` from jwt.go with the fleet signing key. Send it to ExtAuth middleware as Bearer token. Verify 401 — the HS256 algorithm is rejected by the RS256 pointer identity check in the keyfunc. This prevents fleet-minted tokens from authenticating as user sessions.

20. **TestExtAuth_CrossSystem_UserJWTAgainstFleetAuth_Returns401** — Generate a valid RS256 user JWT (the kind ExtAuth would accept). Send it to `NewFleetAuthMiddleware` as Bearer token. Verify 401 — the RS256 algorithm is rejected by `ValidateWorkerToken()` which checks for `*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC` (fleet_auth uses HS256). This prevents user JWTs from authenticating as fleet workers.

21. **TestExtAuth_UserIdentityString_RedactsPII** — Create a `UserIdentity{UserID: "user-123", Email: "alice@example.com", Name: "Alice"}`. Call `.String()`. Verify output is `UserIdentity{UserID: "user-123"}` — email and name are NOT present in the string. This ensures `fmt.Sprintf`, `slog.Any`, etc. never leak PII.

22. **TestUserIdentityFromContext_NoClaims** — Empty context returns zero-value UserIdentity and false. (Follows `TestWorkerClaimsFromContext_NoClaims` pattern.)

23. **TestUserIdentityFromContext_WithClaims** — Context with injected UserIdentity returns correct values and true. (Follows `TestWorkerClaimsFromContext_WithClaims` pattern.)

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/auth.go` (or `auth_routes.go` if .26 has landed)

**Modification to `extractToken()`** — add a defense-in-depth guard that rejects query-param tokens that look like JWTs:

```go
func extractToken(r *http.Request) string {
    // Check Authorization header
    auth := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
    if auth != "" {
        const prefix = "Bearer "
        if strings.HasPrefix(auth, prefix) {
            return auth[len(prefix):]
        }
        return ""
    }

    // Fallback to query parameter (for WebSocket and EventSource opaque tokens)
    qp := r.URL.Query().Get("token")

    // Defense-in-depth: reject query-param tokens that look like JWTs.
    // JWTs have the format header.payload.signature (two dots) and are typically
    // >200 chars. Opaque tokens (API keys, HMAC tokens) don't match this pattern.
    // This prevents accidental JWT leakage into URLs (which may be logged in access
    // logs, browser history, or referrer headers).
    if len(qp) > 200 && strings.Count(qp, ".") == 2 {
        return ""
    }

    return qp
}
```

The change is a 4-line guard before the return. No behavioral change for opaque tokens (hex API keys, HMAC tokens) — they don't match the JWT pattern.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **Wiring into middleware chain** — handled by loomcli-laf73.13 (Wire ExtAuth Middleware and ServerConfig). This task creates the middleware; .13 creates the config flags, initializes JWKSCache, and inserts the middleware into `server.go`.
- **`isPublicRoute()` additions** — routes like `GET /api/events`, `POST /api/sessions/notify`, `/api/config`, `/api/internal/workers/*` are handled by loomcli-laf73.26 (auth_routes.go extraction). This task assumes `isPublicRoute()` already covers all exempt routes per the epic.
- **Token refresh / revocation** — follow-up concern. 15-min JWT TTL means revocation is eventual.
- **OrgID in UserIdentity** — follow-up epic loomcli-1voxb.

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. The `extractToken()` modification is the only cross-file change and it is in scope (per the description).

## Dependencies

**External packages (already in go.mod):**
- `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` — for `jwt.ParseWithClaims`, `jwt.RegisteredClaims`, parser options, signing method type assertions

**No new packages needed.**

**Internal dependencies (same package, no imports needed):**
- `JWKSCache` type and `GetKey(kid)` method from `jwks.go` (loomcli-laf73.5) — must be merged first
- `respondError()` from `respond.go`
- `isPublicRoute()` from `auth.go` (or `auth_routes.go` after .26 lands)

**Task dependencies:**
- **Depends on:** loomcli-laf73.5 (JWKS Cache) — provides `JWKSCache` type and `GetKey()` method
- **Depends on:** loomcli-laf73.26 (auth_routes.go) — provides `isPublicRoute()` in its final location (though the function already exists in auth.go)
- **Blocks:** loomcli-laf73.13 (Wire ExtAuth Middleware) — adds config flags and wires this middleware into `server.go`

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **JWKS cache empty at request time** — `GetKey(kid)` returns error. Middleware responds 401. This handles cold-start where the auth service was unreachable during JWKS cache initialization.

2. **Key rotation in progress** — Incoming JWT has a new `kid` not in cache. `GetKey(kid)` triggers on-demand refresh (handled by JWKS cache). If refresh succeeds, auth succeeds transparently.

3. **Algorithm confusion attacks** — `alg:none` is rejected because `jwt.UnsafeAllowNoneSignatureType` is not the `jwt.SigningMethodRS256` pointer. HMAC confusion is rejected because `*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC` is not the `jwt.SigningMethodRS256` pointer. Custom SigningMethod spoofing (returning "RS256" from Alg()) is rejected because pointer identity check catches it. RS256 ONLY.

4. **Cross-system token confusion** — Fleet HS256 JWTs sent to ExtAuth are rejected (wrong algorithm). RS256 user JWTs sent to fleet auth are rejected (fleet checks for `*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC`). Tests #19 and #20 verify both directions.

5. **Query param tokens that look like JWTs** — The `extractToken()` guard rejects query-param tokens with 2 dots and >200 chars. This prevents JWT leakage into URLs (logged in access logs, browser history, referrer headers). SSE opaque tokens and terminal HMAC tokens don't match this pattern so they are unaffected.

6. **Oversized token DoS** — 8192-byte cap checked before calling `jwt.ParseWithClaims`. Prevents the parser from allocating memory for pathologically large base64 payloads.

7. **Missing required claims** — `sub` is explicitly checked after parsing. Parser options enforce `exp` existence (`WithExpirationRequired`). `email` and `name` are optional — empty string is valid.

8. **Clock skew** — 5-second leeway via `jwt.WithLeeway(5*time.Second)` handles minor clock drift. Tests verify both within-leeway (3s, accepted) and beyond-leeway (7s, rejected) scenarios.

9. **Multiple audiences** — `jwt.WithAudience(cfg.Audience)` checks that the configured audience appears in the token's `aud` claim (which can be a string or string array per JWT spec).

10. **PII in logs** — Raw token strings are NEVER logged. `UserIdentity.String()` redacts email and name, logging only UserID. Error paths log error classification only.

11. **Concurrent requests** — The middleware is stateless per-request. The `JWKSCache` handles its own concurrency. No additional synchronization needed.

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests (ext_auth_test.go):**
- All 23 test cases listed above
- Use `httptest.NewServer` to mock JWKS endpoint with pre-generated RSA keys
- Create a real `JWKSCache` pointing at the mock server (tests middleware + cache integration)
- Use `httptest.NewRecorder` for HTTP response capture
- Run with `go test -race ./internal/webui/ -run TestExtAuth` to verify concurrent safety
- The JWKS mock endpoint is just an httptest URL — the real `/api/auth/jwks` path is configured at the wiring layer (.13), not here

**Test helpers:**
- `signExtAuthJWT(t, claims, key, kid, method)` — generates a JWT with explicit control over all parameters
- JWKS mock server that serves pre-generated RSA public key in JWKS format (matches the manual parsing format from .5: `{"keys": [{"kty":"RSA","kid":"...","alg":"RS256","use":"sig","n":"...","e":"..."}]}`)
- For cross-system tests (#19, #20): reuse `GenerateWorkerToken()` from jwt.go and `NewFleetAuthMiddleware()` from fleet_auth.go to test real cross-system rejection

**Manual verification (deferred to loomcli-laf73.22):**
1. Start Better Auth service → get a real JWT
2. Start loom with `--auth-url` pointing to auth service
3. Call a protected endpoint with the JWT → verify 200
4. Call without JWT → verify 401
5. Verify UserIdentity appears in handler context

## Summary

Remove the API key authentication middleware code from the Go backend. This removes `NewAuthMiddleware`, `AuthConfig`, `handleAuthToken`, `handleAuthTokenDisabled` from auth.go, the `/api/auth/token` route registration from routes.go, and the middleware wiring + API key loading block from server.go. File management utilities (`GenerateAPIKey`, `LoadOrCreateAPIKey`, `DefaultAPIKeyPath`) remain in auth.go for .27 to clean up. ServerConfig fields (`APIKey`, `AuthEnabled`), CLI flags (`--auth`, `--api-key`), env vars (`LOOM_WEBUI_API_KEY`), and loom.yaml entries are NOT touched — those are owned by .27.

**BOUNDARY: .8 removes middleware CODE (function definitions + their call sites). .27 removes CONFIG (struct fields, CLI flags, env vars, file management functions). Do not cross this boundary.**

## Technical Approach

**Strategy**: Surgical removal of the API key auth middleware and its consumers, leaving config-layer plumbing intact for .27.

**Prerequisite state**: This task assumes .26 (extract isPublicRoute/extractToken/stripWorkspacePrefix to auth_routes.go) and .13 (wire ExtAuth middleware) are already merged. After .13, server.go has conditional auth middleware logic: when `ExtAuthURL` is set, use `NewExtAuthMiddleware`; otherwise, use `NewAuthMiddleware` (old API key auth). Task .8 removes the old branch entirely.

**Key decisions**:
1. **auth.go is NOT deleted** — only the middleware functions are removed. The file management functions (`GenerateAPIKey`, `LoadOrCreateAPIKey`, `DefaultAPIKeyPath`, `apiKeyLength`) remain as live code until .27 removes them.
2. **auth_test.go is NOT deleted** — only middleware/handler tests are removed. Tests for `GenerateAPIKey` and `LoadOrCreateAPIKey` remain for .27.
3. **ServerConfig fields stay** — `APIKey` and `AuthEnabled` are still valid struct fields. After .8, nothing in server.go reads them, but serve.go still writes them. They compile fine as unused-but-set data. .27 removes them.
4. **serve.go is NOT modified** — CLI flags, env vars, daemon config fallback, and the ServerConfig literal construction all stay. .27 owns all of it.
5. **Test files that set `AuthEnabled: false`** in ServerConfig literals (server_test.go, server_lifecycle_test.go) are NOT modified — the field still exists.

- Follows .26 convention: shared auth utilities live in `auth_routes.go`
- Follows .8/.27 boundary: middleware code vs config code is the split line

None.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **setupRoutes parameter reordering**: Removing `apiKey` and `authEnabled` shifts all subsequent positional parameters left by 2. There are ~23 call sites across routes_test.go, embed_test.go, and server.go. Count parameters carefully at each call site. The 10th and 11th args (after mux, pool, multiPool, hub, getMutationsSince, termManager, termAuth, fleetStore, tokenCfg) are removed.

2. **isPublicRoute /api/auth/token entry**: Must be removed from auth_routes.go since the endpoint is gone. If left, it would silently mark a non-existent path as public — harmless but confusing for future maintainers.

3. **auth.go import cleanup**: After removing AuthConfig and NewAuthMiddleware, the imports `"crypto/subtle"` and `"net/http"` become unused. Go will refuse to compile with unused imports. Must remove them.

4. **auth_test.go import cleanup**: After removing middleware tests, `"encoding/json"`, `"net/http"`, and `"net/http/httptest"` become unused. Must remove them.

5. **Go unused variable**: After removing the consumers of `apiKey` in server.go (setupRoutes call and NewAuthMiddleware call), the `apiKey` variable from the loading block becomes unused. Go will refuse to compile. The entire loading block must be removed.

6. **embed_test.go /api/auth/token test cases**: These test general frontend handler behavior (404 for any /api/ path), not auth. Keep them — the path `/api/auth/token` is just an example of an API path.

7. **Conditional .13 code**: The exact shape of the conditional auth middleware code added by .13 is not yet finalized (task is in review). The implementer should read the actual code after .13 merges and remove the old-auth branch accordingly. The key outcome: only NewExtAuthMiddleware remains in the chain, no references to NewAuthMiddleware.

### Automated Tests
- `go build ./cmd/loom/` — verify full binary compiles with no unused imports/variables
- `go vet ./internal/webui/...` — no issues
- `go test ./internal/webui/... -count=1` — all remaining tests pass
- `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` — serve.go still compiles (it still sets APIKey/AuthEnabled in config)

### Key Scenarios to Verify
1. **No dangling references**: `grep -r "NewAuthMiddleware\|handleAuthToken\|handleAuthTokenDisabled\|AuthConfig" --include="*.go" internal/` should return zero results (excluding .beads/ and any comments)
2. **File management functions intact**: `grep -r "GenerateAPIKey\|LoadOrCreateAPIKey\|DefaultAPIKeyPath" --include="*.go" internal/webui/auth.go` should still find them
3. **Config fields intact**: `grep -r "APIKey\|AuthEnabled" --include="*.go" internal/webui/server_config.go` should still find them
4. **setupRoutes signature**: Verify the function no longer has apiKey/authEnabled params and all callers are updated

### Manual Verification
- Run `loom serve` — should start without auth middleware log messages
- `curl http://localhost:8080/api/auth/token` — should 404 (SPA catch-all, not a handler)
- `curl http://localhost:8080/api/health` — should succeed without Bearer token
- `curl http://localhost:8080/api/issues` — behavior depends on ExtAuth config (passthrough if no --auth-url)

title: withTx/RunInTransaction: COMMIT uses cancellable ctx and no reconnectMu lock
description: Two pre-existing robustness issues in third_party/beads/internal/storage/sqlite/{util.go,transaction.go}. 1) COMMIT uses caller's ctx (util.go:48). If ctx is cancelled between fn() returning nil and COMMIT, ExecContext fails immediately and the deferred ROLLBACK discards fully-applied work. Fix: commit on context.Background() with a short timeout. 2) withTx does not hold reconnectMu.RLock() around s.db.Conn(ctx) acquisition. If reconnect() swaps s.db mid-flight, the acquired conn belongs to the closed-out pool.
