title: V6 Kanban: Agent sidebar diff stat shows commit count not line count
description: V6 design shows '+366' on agent sidebar entries implying lines added. The live app shows '+198 +204' which appears to be commits ahead counts, not line diff stats. The design intends line-level diff stats per agent. Need to wire DiffStatResult.LinesAdded to the agent sidebar display.
design:
## Summary The AgentCard component in the V6 Kanban sidebar displays \`agent.ahead\` (commits ahead count, e.g., \"+198\") where the design intends line-level diff stats (e.g., \"+366 lines added\"). The fix requires: (1) adding a new backend endpoint \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` that returns line-level diff stats by agent name (mirroring the existing issue-scoped endpoint but without requiring an issue ID lookup), (2) creating a frontend hook \`useAgentDiffStat\` to poll this endpoint, and (3) updating AgentCard to display \`diffStat.added\`/\`diffStat.removed\` (lines) instead of \`agent.ahead\`/\`agent.behind\` (commits). ## Technical Approach **Why a new endpoint instead of reusing the issue-scoped one:** The existing \`GET /api/issues/{id}/git/diff-stat\` requires an issue ID, performs an RPC call to look up the assignee, then resolves the worktree. The AgentCard already knows the agent name — going agent→task→issue→assignee→worktree is a round-trip. A direct \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` skips the RPC and does \`ResolveAgentWorktree(wsID, name)\` → \`DiffStat(wt.Path, wt.DefaultBranch)\` directly. This is simpler, faster, and doesn't require agent-to-task mapping in the frontend. **Why a new hook instead of embedding in the agent poll:** The \`/api/status\` response that populates \`LoomAgentStatus\` comes from the loom monitor, which polls git metadata (ahead/behind/commits/changes) but intentionally does NOT run \`git diff --numstat\` (expensive). Adding diff stats to the monitor poll would slow down all agent status updates. A separate per-agent poll (60s interval) keeps the fast path fast. **Display change:** The commit counts section in AgentCard's meta column will be replaced with line diff stats. The commit ahead/behind counts move to the tooltip only. The \`changeCount\` variable (line 99) and \`changeBadge\` element will be removed — they conflate commits with uncommitted changes in a confusing way. The primary display becomes \`+N\` (green, lines added) and \`-N\` (red, lines removed). **Trade-offs considered:** - Embedding diff stats in the SSE/poll agent response: rejected (expensive on the backend, slows all polling) - Fetching via the issue endpoint with agentTasks mapping: rejected (requires issue ID, adds coupling, fails for agents without a current task) - Client-side aggregation from \`/diff/files\`: rejected (over-fetches, returns per-file data we don't need) ## Conventions Established - Agent-scoped git endpoints follow the pattern \`/api/agents/{name}/git/\` (consistent with existing \`/git/push\`, \`/git/status\`, etc.) - Diff stat polling hooks use 60s intervals (same as TaskRow's useIssueDiffStat) - Diff stat response shape: \`{ branch: string, added: number, removed: number }\` — reuses the existing \`DiffStatResponse\` struct and \`IssueDiffStat\` TS type ## Files to Create 1. **\`internal/webui/handlers_agent_diff_stat.go\`** — New handler for \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` - Resolves agent name to worktree via \`gitOps.ResolveAgentWorktree(wsID, name)\` - Calls \`gitOps.DiffStat(wt.Path, wt.DefaultBranch)\` - Returns \`DiffStatResponse{Branch, Added, Removed}\` (reuse existing struct from handlers_issue_diff_stat.go) 2. **\`internal/webui/handlers_agent_diff_stat_test.go\`** — Tests for the new handler - Happy path: agent exists, returns diff stats - Agent not found: returns 404 - Missing agent name: returns 400 - Workspace-scoped variant works correctly 3. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/useAgentDiffStat.ts\`** — React hook for polling agent diff stats - Mirrors \`useIssueDiffStat\` structure: options interface with \`workspaceId\`, \`agentName\`, \`enabled\`, \`pollInterval\` (default 60000) - Returns \`{ data: IssueDiffStat | null, isLoading, error }\` - Reuses existing \`IssueDiffStat\` type and \`get()\` client 4. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useAgentDiffStat.test.ts\`** — Tests for the new hook ## Files to Modify 1. **\`internal/webui/routes.go\`** — Register the new endpoint - Add after line 142 (under existing agent git endpoints): \`mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat", handleAgentDiffStat(gitOps))\` - Add workspace-scoped variant after line 327: \`wsMux.HandleFunc("GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat", handleAgentDiffStat(gitOps))\` 2. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/api/diff-stat.ts\`** — Add fetch function for agent diff stat - Add \`fetchAgentDiffStat(workspaceId: string, agentName: string): Promise\` that calls \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` (or workspace-scoped variant) - Reuses existing \`IssueDiffStat\` type (same response shape) 3. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/api/index.ts\`** — Export the new fetch function - Add \`export { fetchAgentDiffStat } from "./diff-stat"\` 4. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/index.ts\`** — Export the new hook - Add \`export { useAgentDiffStat } from "./useAgentDiffStat"\` - Add type exports for \`UseAgentDiffStatOptions\`, \`UseAgentDiffStatReturn\` 5. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.tsx\`** — Replace commit counts with line diff stats - Add import: \`import { useAgentDiffStat } from "@/hooks"\` - Add import: \`import { useWorkspaceContext } from "@/hooks/useWorkspaceContext"\` - Inside the component, add: \`const { workspaceId } = useWorkspaceContext()\` and \`const { data: diffStat } = useAgentDiffStat({ workspaceId, agentName: agent.name, pollInterval: 60000 })\` - Remove line 99: \`const changeCount = agent.ahead + (agent.changes?.length ?? 0)\` - Replace lines 157-174 (the commit counts \`
\`): show \`diffStat.added\`/\`diffStat.removed\` instead of \`agent.ahead\`/\`agent.behind\` - New display: \`\`\`tsx {diffStat && (diffStat.added > 0 || diffStat.removed > 0) && (
{diffStat.added > 0 && +{diffStat.added}} {diffStat.removed > 0 && -{diffStat.removed}}
)} \`\`\` - Remove lines 176-183 (the changeBadge element) — it conflates commits and uncommitted changes 6. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.module.css\`** — Update CSS classes - Rename/replace \`.commitCounts\` → \`.diffStats\` (same flex layout) - Rename/replace \`.commitCount\` → \`.linesAdded\` (keep green color \`var(--color-success)\`) - Rename/replace \`.behindCount\` → \`.linesRemoved\` (change to red: \`var(--color-danger, #ef4444)\`) - Remove \`.changeBadge\` class (no longer used) 7. **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/AgentCard/AgentCard.test.tsx\`** — Update tests - Mock \`useAgentDiffStat\` and \`useWorkspaceContext\` - Update "commit count" describe block → "diff stats" describe block - Test: shows \`+N\` when diffStat.added > 0 - Test: shows \`-N\` when diffStat.removed > 0 - Test: shows both when both > 0 - Test: hidden when diffStat is null (loading) - Test: hidden when both are 0 - Test: correct tooltip text - Remove "change badge" describe block entirely - Update "edge cases" large count test ## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task) - **\`AgentDetailPanel.tsx\` (lines 338-350):** Uses \`agent.ahead\`/\`agent.behind\` in the "Commit Status" section. This is CORRECT behavior — the detail panel intentionally shows commit-level info (with expandable commit list). No change needed. - **\`GitTab.tsx\` (lines 131-146):** Uses \`ahead\`/\`behind\` for branch sync status badges. This is CORRECT — the Git tab shows commit-level sync status. No change needed. - **\`AgentActivityPanel.tsx\` (line 75):** Uses \`agent.ahead > 0\` to compute \`needsPush\` summary count. This is CORRECT — it's about push status (commit-level), not line stats. No change needed. - **\`AgentStatusBadge.tsx\`:** Uses \`agent.ahead\`/\`agent.behind\` for display — not in scope for this bug since it's in the IssueDetailPanel, not the sidebar. - **\`third_party/beads/\` AgentCard:** Third-party code, not in scope. ## Dependencies - **Internal modules:** \`internal/webui\` (GitOps interface, DiffStatResponse, respondJSON, respondError, WorkspaceFromContext) - **External packages:** None new — all existing dependencies - **Task ordering:** No blockers. The existing \`GitOps.DiffStat()\` and \`GitOps.ResolveAgentWorktree()\` methods are already implemented. ## Edge Cases & Error Handling 1. **Agent has no worktree (recently removed):** \`ResolveAgentWorktree\` returns error → handler returns 404 → hook sets \`error\`, \`data\` stays null → AgentCard shows no diff stats (graceful degradation, no crash) 2. **Agent exists but has 0 lines changed:** \`DiffStat\` returns \`{0, 0, 0}\` → API returns \`{added: 0, removed: 0}\` → frontend condition \`diffStat.added > 0 || diffStat.removed > 0\` is false → nothing displayed. Correct. 3. **Network error / loom server down:** Hook catches error → data remains null → no diff stats shown. The AgentCard still renders all other info (name, status, role). No error UI needed in the card — errors are transient. 4. **Rapid agent name changes (user clicks through agents fast):** The hook should abort in-flight requests when agentName changes (use cleanup in useEffect). Pattern: copy from \`useIssueDiffStat\` which uses \`mountedRef\`. 5. **Workspace context not available (legacy mode):** \`workspaceId\` will be empty string → API URL uses non-workspace-scoped path → works correctly (existing pattern used by all other hooks). 6. **AgentCard rendered outside WorkspaceContext provider:** This would be a pre-existing bug if it happened. The AgentCard is only rendered inside MonitorDashboard which provides the context. If this somehow occurs, \`useWorkspaceContext\` will throw — abort and surface as React error boundary. Do NOT add a try/catch. 7. **Very large diff stats (e.g., +100000):** Display as-is. No abbreviation needed — the monospace font and tabular-nums handle large numbers. The design shows raw numbers. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. The AgentCard sidebar entry displays \`+N\` (lines added, green) and \`-N\` (lines removed, red) instead of commit ahead/behind counts 2. Hovering over the diff stats shows a tooltip like "366 lines added, 12 lines removed" 3. When an agent has 0 lines changed, no diff stat badge is shown 4. When the diff-stat API returns an error or is loading, the AgentCard renders without diff stats (no error state, no spinner) 5. The existing commit ahead/behind display in AgentDetailPanel (Info tab → "Commit Status" section) is UNCHANGED 6. The existing commit ahead/behind display in AgentDetailPanel (Git tab) is UNCHANGED 7. The changeBadge element (which conflated commits + uncommitted changes) is removed from AgentCard 8. \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` returns \`{"branch":"...","added":N,"removed":N}\` for valid agent names 9. \`GET /api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` returns 404 for unknown agent names 10. All existing tests continue to pass ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Tests (Frontend) - **useAgentDiffStat hook tests:** Mock \`fetchAgentDiffStat\`, test loading/success/error states, test polling behavior, test cleanup on unmount - **AgentCard tests:** Mock \`useAgentDiffStat\` to return controlled data, verify: - Renders \`+N\` for lines added - Renders \`-N\` for lines removed - Renders both when both > 0 - Renders nothing when data is null - Renders nothing when both are 0 - Tooltip text is correct - No changeBadge rendered ### Unit Tests (Backend) - **handleAgentDiffStat tests:** Use mock GitOps, test: - Happy path: returns correct JSON - Missing name: 400 - Agent not found: 404 - Workspace-scoped request: passes workspace ID correctly ### Manual Verification 1. Start loom server with agents that have commits 2. Open V6 Kanban view 3. Verify agent sidebar shows line counts (e.g., \"+366\") not commit counts (e.g., \"+198\") 4. Open AgentDetailPanel → Info tab → verify "Commit Status" still shows commit counts 5. Open AgentDetailPanel → Git tab → verify branch sync badges still show commit counts 6. Check browser DevTools network tab: confirm \`/api/agents/{name}/git/diff-stat\` is polled at ~60s intervals

(2) infra-isolation — rpc, sessions, lockfile, circuitbreaker, kv, configlock, usage, logrouter, atomicfile, workspace, debug, backend/beads, backend/fleet, backend/agentipc, events/otelexport must not import webui or cli. design:
## Summary

Add depguard linter rules to `.golangci.yml` that enforce the 4-repo module boundary DAG: sdk → infra → web → cli. These rules are **preventive gates** — they pass today (zero existing violations verified) and prevent future imports that would violate the boundary direction. This is Phase 1 of the repo-ready architecture epic: get the linter rules in place before any package moves happen.

## Technical Approach

Use golangci-lint v2's depguard linter (already enabled) to add 3 new rules alongside the existing `handler-layer-isolation` rule. Each rule targets one layer's source files via glob patterns and denies imports from layers above it in the dependency DAG.

**Dependency DAG** (lower imports upper only):
- **sdk** (bottom): imports nothing internal
- **infra**: imports sdk only
- **web**: imports sdk + infra
- **cli** (top): imports anything

Only 3 rules are needed since cli (top of DAG) has no restrictions.

**Layer → Package mapping (per approved plan purrfect-weaving-stream.md):**

| Layer | Packages |
|-------|----------|
| sdk | types, entity, backend (root only), backend/mapping, notify, agenterr, authmode, workspaceerrors, events (root only) |
| infra | rpc, sessions, lockfile, circuitbreaker, kv, configlock, usage, logrouter, atomicfile, workspace, debug, testutil, backend/beads, backend/fleet, backend/agentipc, events/otelexport |
| web | webui (all sub-packages) |
| cli | cli (all sub-packages), cmd/loom |

**Critical distinction from previous (rejected) design:** The previous design incorrectly placed atomicfile, circuitbreaker, debug, lockfile, logrouter, workspace, and testutil in the SDK layer. Per the approved plan, these 7 packages belong in the **infra** layer. This is verified by actual imports: `rpc` imports `debug` and `lockfile`, `kv` imports `circuitbreaker`, `configlock` imports `lockfile`, `usage` imports `lockfile`, `sessions` imports `lockfile`. These are all valid intra-infra imports that would be falsely blocked if these packages were misclassified as SDK-leaf.

**Rule structure:**

**Rule 1: `sdk-leaf`** — SDK leaf packages must not import ANY internal package. Uses a blanket deny on the entire `internal` prefix. This is simpler and stricter than listing each forbidden package individually.

Note: `backend/mapping` is SDK-layer but NOT a leaf (it imports `backend` and `entity`, both SDK). It is intentionally excluded from `sdk-leaf` via the non-recursive glob `**/internal/backend/*.go`. Since it only imports other SDK packages, it already respects the boundary and doesn't need a deny rule. If someone later adds an infra/web/cli import to it, that would be caught by code review. The `internal/ops` package (created by loomcli-rir82.2) is included preventively — it doesn't exist yet but will be a zero-import SDK leaf.

**Rule 2: `infra-isolation`** — Infra packages must not import webui or cli. Uses two specific deny entries.

Note: The 7 previously-misclassified packages (atomicfile, circuitbreaker, debug, lockfile, logrouter, workspace, testutil) are correctly placed here. Even though some are zero-import leaves today, they belong in infra per the plan. Placing them in `infra-isolation` (rather than `sdk-leaf`) allows them to import other infra packages in the future without violating boundary rules — e.g., `rpc` already imports `debug` and `lockfile`.

Also includes `backend/mapping` in the files list since it should also be prevented from importing webui/cli. (backend/mapping imports backend+entity, both SDK — no violations today.)

**Rule 3: `webui-isolation`** — All webui packages must not import cli.

**Rule naming:** Follows the plan's convention: `sdk-leaf`, `infra-isolation`, `webui-isolation`. The existing `handler-layer-isolation` rule is a finer-grained intra-web-layer rule and remains unchanged.

**depguard file-matching approach:**

depguard's `files` field takes glob patterns matched against source file paths. Using `list-mode: lax` (same as existing rule), only denied packages are blocked; all others are allowed.

- **sdk-leaf**: Each true-leaf SDK package gets an explicit glob entry. For `backend` root and `events` root (which have sub-packages in infra), use non-recursive globs: `**/internal/backend/*.go` and `**/internal/events/*.go`.
- **infra-isolation**: Glob each infra package explicitly, including the 7 packages that were previously misclassified (atomicfile, circuitbreaker, debug, lockfile, logrouter, workspace, testutil) plus backend/mapping.
- **webui-isolation**: Single glob `**/internal/webui/**` covers all webui sub-packages.

**Prefix matching in deny lists:** depguard treats `pkg: foo/bar` as matching `foo/bar` and all sub-packages (`foo/bar/baz`). So `pkg: .../internal/webui` blocks both `internal/webui` and `internal/webui/daemon`, etc.

## Conventions Established

- **Layer naming**: `sdk`, `infra`, `web`, `cli` — matching the plan's 4-repo model
- **Rule naming pattern**: `sdk-leaf`, `infra-isolation`, `webui-isolation` — each name describes its scope
- **File glob pattern**: Use `**/internal/<pkg>/**` for recursive matching, `**/internal/<pkg>/*.go` for root-only matching when sub-packages belong to a different layer
- **Deny description pattern**: `"SDK-layer packages must not import other internal packages"` (sdk-leaf), `"Infra packages must not import webui/cli"` (infra-isolation), `"WebUI must not import cli"` (webui-isolation) — matching the plan's exact descriptions
- **Future packages**: `internal/ops` is included preventively in sdk-leaf (created by .2). The implementer should add a YAML comment noting that new packages must be added to the appropriate rule

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### `.golangci.yml`
Add 3 new depguard rules under `linters.settings.depguard.rules`, after the existing `handler-layer-isolation` rule:

**Rule 1: `sdk-leaf`**
```yaml
sdk-leaf:
  list-mode: lax
  files:
    - "**/internal/types/**"
    - "**/internal/entity/**"
    - "**/internal/backend/*.go"       # root only — sub-packages are infra
    - "**/internal/notify/**"
    - "**/internal/agenterr/**"
    - "**/internal/authmode/**"
    - "**/internal/workspaceerrors/**"
    - "**/internal/events/*.go"        # root only — otelexport is infra
    - "**/internal/ops/**"             # future: created by loomcli-rir82.2
  deny:
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal
      desc: "SDK-layer packages must not import other internal packages"
```

**Rule 2: `infra-isolation`**
```yaml
infra-isolation:
  list-mode: lax
  files:
    - "**/internal/rpc/**"
    - "**/internal/sessions/**"
    - "**/internal/lockfile/**"
    - "**/internal/circuitbreaker/**"
    - "**/internal/kv/**"
    - "**/internal/configlock/**"
    - "**/internal/usage/**"
    - "**/internal/logrouter/**"
    - "**/internal/atomicfile/**"
    - "**/internal/workspace/**"
    - "**/internal/debug/**"
    - "**/internal/testutil/**"
    - "**/internal/backend/mapping/**"
    - "**/internal/backend/beads/**"
    - "**/internal/backend/fleet/**"
    - "**/internal/backend/agentipc/**"
    - "**/internal/events/otelexport/**"
  deny:
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui
      desc: "Infra packages must not import webui"
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli
      desc: "Infra packages must not import cli"
```

**Rule 3: `webui-isolation`**
```yaml
webui-isolation:
  list-mode: lax
  files:
    - "**/internal/webui/**"
  deny:
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli
      desc: "WebUI must not import cli"
```

The existing `handler-layer-isolation` rule remains unchanged.

Add a YAML comment above the new rules block:
```yaml
# Module boundary rules — dependency direction: sdk → infra → web → cli
# When adding new internal packages, add them to the appropriate rule below.
# See /Users/tyson/.claude/plans/purrfect-weaving-stream.md for layer definitions.
```

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **`third_party/beads/.golangci.yml`** — separate Go module with its own linter config; has no depguard rules and no loomcli internal imports. Not relevant.
- **Makefile** — references depguard in a display string only (line 166 `[4/9] Go: lint (golangci-lint + depguard)`). No changes needed.
- **`cmd/loom/main.go`** — cli-layer (top of DAG), no restrictions needed.
- **`internal/ops/` creation** — tracked by loomcli-rir82.2. The glob is included preventively in sdk-leaf.
- **Moving events/otelexport classification** — tracked by loomcli-rir82.3. Already classified correctly as infra in this design's infra-isolation rule.
- **`backend/mapping` has no dedicated deny rule** — it's SDK-layer but not a leaf (imports backend+entity). It IS included in infra-isolation to prevent webui/cli imports. It cannot import infra packages though — there's no rule for this specific case. Accepted gap: backend/mapping currently imports only SDK packages and is unlikely to add infra imports. If the team wants tighter enforcement, a separate `sdk-non-leaf` rule could be added later.

## Dependencies

- **golangci-lint v2** (already installed, version 2.9.0)
- **depguard linter** (already enabled in `.golangci.yml`)
- No external packages needed
- No other tasks must be completed first — the rules pass today with zero violations

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **`**/internal/backend/*.go` glob matching**: This non-recursive glob matches only files directly in `internal/backend/` (errors.go, issuebackend.go, types.go, errors_test.go, types_test.go), NOT files in sub-directories like `backend/beads/`, `backend/fleet/`, `backend/agentipc/`, or `backend/mapping/`. **Verification step**: After adding the rules, run `golangci-lint run` — if it reports violations from `backend/mapping/mapper.go`, the glob is matching too broadly. Fall back to listing specific files: `**/internal/backend/errors.go`, `**/internal/backend/issuebackend.go`, `**/internal/backend/types.go`. Expected: `*.go` is non-recursive in standard glob semantics.

2. **`**/internal/events/*.go` glob matching**: Same pattern — root `events` package is SDK, `events/otelexport` is infra. `*.go` must NOT match files in `events/otelexport/`. Same fallback approach if it does.

3. **Test files**: depguard rules apply to test files (`_test.go`) too. This is correct — test files should also respect module boundaries. The `**/internal/backend/*.go` glob WILL match `errors_test.go` and `types_test.go` in the backend root, which is correct (they're SDK leaf tests).

4. **New packages added later**: A new `internal/foo/` package won't be covered by any boundary rule until explicitly added. This is acceptable for a preventive gate. Add a YAML comment documenting this expectation so implementers of new packages know to update the rules.

5. **Rule ordering / overlap**: depguard applies all matching rules to a file. Files in `internal/backend/*.go` match sdk-leaf only. Files in `internal/backend/beads/**` match infra-isolation only. Files in `internal/webui/**` match BOTH webui-isolation AND handler-layer-isolation (for `**/handler/**` files). This is correct — the rules are additive (all deny lists apply). No conflicts.

6. **`backend/mapping` in infra-isolation**: This package is SDK-layer but is included in infra-isolation to get the webui+cli deny protection. The infra-isolation deny list only blocks webui and cli imports — it does NOT block other infra imports. So technically `backend/mapping` could import `rpc` or `kv` without a violation. This is a minor over-permission (sdk should not import infra), but the risk is low: backend/mapping is a small pure-converter package. Accepted trade-off vs. creating a 4th rule for one package.

7. **Prefix matching scope**: `pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal` in sdk-leaf matches ALL imports starting with this prefix, including `internal/types`, `internal/entity`, etc. This means sdk-leaf packages cannot import OTHER sdk-leaf packages either. **This is correct**: all current sdk-leaf packages have zero internal imports. The only sdk package with intra-sdk imports (backend/mapping) is intentionally excluded from the sdk-leaf files list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `golangci-lint run` passes with zero new depguard violations (confirming rules match current import graph)
2. Adding `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/rpc"` to `internal/types/types.go` causes a depguard error mentioning "SDK-layer packages must not import other internal packages"
3. Adding `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui"` to `internal/rpc/client.go` causes a depguard error mentioning "Infra packages must not import webui"
4. Adding `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli"` to `internal/rpc/client.go` causes a depguard error mentioning "Infra packages must not import cli"
5. Adding `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli"` to any file in `internal/webui/` causes a depguard error mentioning "WebUI must not import cli"
6. Files in `internal/cli/` can still import from any internal package without depguard errors
7. `backend/mapping/mapper.go` is NOT flagged by sdk-leaf (the `**/internal/backend/*.go` glob must not match sub-directories)
8. `events/otelexport/exporter.go` is NOT flagged by sdk-leaf (the `**/internal/events/*.go` glob must not match sub-directories)
9. The existing `handler-layer-isolation` rule continues to work unchanged
10. Test files (`_test.go`) are covered by the boundary rules
11. Intra-infra imports are allowed: `rpc` importing `debug` and `lockfile` must NOT trigger any violation

## Testing Strategy

### Automated verification
1. Run `golangci-lint run` — must pass clean with zero depguard violations
2. Run `make gate` or `make check-go` — must pass

### Manual verification (boundary violation detection)
For each of the 3 rules, temporarily add a forbidden import to a file in that layer and confirm golangci-lint catches it:

1. **SDK-leaf test**: Add `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/rpc"` to `internal/types/types.go`, run `golangci-lint run ./internal/types/...`, confirm depguard error. Revert.
2. **Infra-isolation test (webui)**: Add `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui"` to `internal/rpc/client.go`, run `golangci-lint run ./internal/rpc/...`, confirm depguard error. Revert.
3. **Infra-isolation test (cli)**: Add `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli"` to `internal/lockfile/lockfile.go`, run `golangci-lint run ./internal/lockfile/...`, confirm depguard error. Revert.
4. **WebUI-isolation test**: Add `import _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli"` to `internal/webui/server.go`, run `golangci-lint run ./internal/webui/...`, confirm depguard error. Revert.
5. **No false positives on cli**: Confirm `internal/cli/serve.go` (which imports webui) has no depguard errors.
6. **No false positives on intra-infra**: Confirm `internal/rpc/` (which imports debug, lockfile, types) has no depguard errors.
7. **No false positives on intra-sdk**: Confirm `internal/backend/mapping/` (which imports backend, entity) has no depguard errors — it's not in sdk-leaf files.

### Glob edge case verification
8. **backend root vs sub-package**: Confirm that `internal/backend/types.go` is covered by sdk-leaf but `internal/backend/beads/beads.go` is NOT covered by sdk-leaf (it should be covered by infra-isolation instead).
9. **events root vs otelexport**: Confirm that `internal/events/event.go` is covered by sdk-leaf but `internal/events/otelexport/exporter.go` is NOT (it should be covered by infra-isolation).

title: Phase 7: Add check-import-fanout.sh — max 10 internal imports per package, hard fail
description: Create scripts/check-import-fanout.sh. Uses go list to count internal/loomcli imports per package. Fails with exit 1 if any package exceeds threshold (default: 10). No allowlist. Wire as new step in make check-go. This prevents wiring packages from accumulating cross-cutting dependencies. After the god package splits, all packages should be at 3-10 internal imports. Plan: /Users/tyson/.claude/plans/purrfect-weaving-stream.md
design:
## Summary

Create `scripts/check-import-fanout.sh` — a shell script that uses `go list` to count how many module-internal packages each Go package under `internal/` imports. Fails with exit 1 if any package exceeds a configurable threshold (default: 10). No allowlist. Wire it into `make check-go` as a new step after the package size check (added by sibling .9). Update all step labels from `[N/10]` to `[N/11]`.

This gate prevents packages from accumulating cross-cutting dependencies. After the Phase 3 god-package splits, all packages should import 3–10 internal siblings. A package importing 11+ internal packages is a sign it needs to be split or its responsibilities narrowed.

## Technical Approach

**Counting method: `go list` (not filesystem-based)**

The task description explicitly says "Uses go list to count internal/loomcli imports per package." This is the right tool because:
- Import fanout is a semantic property of the code (what a package actually imports), not a filesystem property
- `go list` resolves all imports transitively through build constraints, correctly handling `_test.go` exclusion (non-test imports only by default)
- It works at the package granularity we need

**Command**: For each package, run `go list -f '{{range .Imports}}{{.}}\n{{end}}' ./internal/...` and count lines matching the module prefix (`github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/`), excluding self-imports.

Optimized approach — single `go list` invocation for all packages:

```bash
MODULE=$(go list -m)
go list -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{join .Imports ","}}' ./internal/... 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r line; do
    pkg="${line%% *}"
    imports="${line#* }"
    count=$(echo "$imports" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -c "^${MODULE}/" || true)
    # Subtract 1 if the package appears in its own import list (it doesn't in Go, but be safe)
    echo "$count $pkg"
done
```

Then filter for packages exceeding the threshold.

**Scope**: Only packages under `internal/`. The `go list ./internal/...` pattern naturally scopes this. No need for separate exclusion of `cmd/`, `third_party/`, etc. — `go list ./internal/...` doesn't traverse those.

**What counts as "internal import"**: Any import whose path starts with the module path (`github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/`). This includes imports from `internal/`, `cmd/`, or any other module-local package. Self-imports are excluded (a package doesn't import itself in Go, but the script should be defensive).

**Exit codes**: 0 = pass, 1 = violation found, 2 = usage error (invalid threshold or `go list` failure).

**Failure mode if `go list` fails**: If `go list ./internal/...` exits non-zero (e.g., broken build), the script must abort with exit 2 and a clear error message. Do NOT silently pass — a broken build hiding import violations defeats the purpose. Capture `go list` output to a temp file and check the exit code before processing.

## Conventions Established

- **`go list`-based scripts**: Unlike the filesystem-based `.9` (check-package-size.sh), this script uses `go list` because it measures a semantic property (imports). Future scripts measuring semantic Go properties (e.g., cyclomatic complexity) should follow this pattern.
- **Module-prefix filtering**: Internal imports are identified by grepping for the module path from `go list -m`. This is portable across forks/renames.
- **No allowlist, ever**: Consistent with `.9` — if a package has too many internal imports, restructure it.
- **Makefile step numbering**: After `.9` adds package-size check (step `[6/10]`), this task adds import-fanout check as step `[7/11]`, shifting exec guard to `[8/11]`, log.Printf guard to `[9/11]`, test to `[10/11]`, coverage to `[11/11]`.

## Files to Create

1. **`scripts/check-import-fanout.sh`** — The main script. Uses `go list` to count module-internal imports per package under `internal/`. Exits 1 if any exceeds threshold.

2. **`scripts/check-import-fanout_test.sh`** — Test script following the `check-loc-stale_test.sh` / `check-coverage_test.sh` pattern. Creates a mock `go` binary that simulates `go list` output, then verifies the script's behavior across scenarios.

## Files to Modify

1. **`Makefile`** — In the `check-go` target:
   - **Prerequisite**: `.9` will have already renumbered steps to `[N/10]` and added `[6/10] Go: package size check`. This task assumes `.9` is implemented first.
   - Insert new step after `[6/10]` (package size check): `@echo "=== [7/11] Go: import fanout check ==="` followed by `@./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 10`
   - Renumber all steps from `[N/10]` to `[N/11]`:
     - `[1/10]` → `[1/11]` (format check)
     - `[2/10]` → `[2/11]` (vet)
     - `[3/10]` → `[3/11]` (build)
     - `[4/10]` → `[4/11]` (lint)
     - `[5/10]` → `[5/11]` (LOC check)
     - `[6/10]` → `[6/11]` (package size check — from .9)
     - NEW `[7/11]` (import fanout check)
     - `[7/10]` → `[8/11]` (exec.Command guard)
     - `[8/10]` → `[9/11]` (log.Printf guard)
     - `[9/10]` → `[10/11]` (test with race detector)
     - `[10/10]` → `[11/11]` (coverage threshold)

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **`scripts/check-package-size.sh`** (loomcli-rir82.9) — Separate Phase 7 sibling. Filesystem-based file counting. Must be implemented first since this task's Makefile wiring assumes `.9` is done.
- **`scripts/check-dir-size.mjs`** (loomcli-rir82.11) — Frontend equivalent. Different language, different tool.
- **`cmd/loom/main.go`** — Outside `internal/`, naturally excluded by `go list ./internal/...`.
- **`third_party/beads/`** — Has its own module, not traversed by `go list ./internal/...`.
- **TestImports / XTestImports** — The script counts `.Imports` only (non-test imports). Test imports (`_test.go`) are excluded. This is intentional: test files may import more broadly for test utilities. If test-import fanout becomes a problem, it should be a separate gate.

## Dependencies

- **Go toolchain**: `go list` and `go list -m` must be available. Already guaranteed by the `check-go` target (Go build/vet run earlier).
- **No external packages**: Pure bash + go list + grep + awk.
- **Task loomcli-rir82.9**: Must be implemented first — this task's Makefile changes build on `.9`'s step numbering. (Already declared as dependency in the beads issue.)
- **Does NOT depend on Phase 3 splits**: The script will correctly identify `internal/cli` (21 internal imports) and `internal/webui` (20 internal imports) as violations today. That's expected and correct — the gate exists to motivate the splits.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **`go list` fails (broken build)**: Abort with exit 2 and message "go list failed — fix build errors first". Do NOT silently pass. Check `go list` exit code explicitly.
2. **Package with zero internal imports**: Will have count 0. Not a violation. Correct.
3. **Nested packages**: `internal/webui/server/middleware` is separate from `internal/webui`. Each is counted independently. `go list ./internal/...` handles this correctly.
4. **Self-import**: Go packages don't import themselves. The script should be defensive and exclude the package's own import path from the count, but this edge case won't occur in practice.
5. **Threshold of 0 or non-integer**: Reject with exit 2 and usage message. Validate with the same regex as `.9`: `^[1-9][0-9]*$` (positive integer only). Threshold 0 is rejected — every package would violate it, which is meaningless.
6. **No packages under `internal/`**: `go list ./internal/...` returns nothing → no violations → exit 0. Correct.
7. **Package with only test files**: `go list` still lists the package but `.Imports` will be empty (only test imports exist). Count = 0, not a violation. Correct.
8. **Circular imports**: Go doesn't allow circular imports, so this can't happen. Not an edge case.
9. **Vendor mode**: `go list` respects `-mod=vendor` if set. The script doesn't set it, so it uses the default module mode. This is correct for our repo.
10. **`go list -m` returns unexpected output**: If the module path is empty or multi-line, the grep filter will silently pass everything. Validate that `MODULE` is non-empty; abort with exit 2 if not.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Running `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 10` in the current repo exits 1 and lists `internal/cli` (21 internal imports) and `internal/webui` (20 internal imports) as violations.
2. Running `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 25` in the current repo exits 0 (no packages exceed 25 internal imports).
3. Running `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh` (no argument) uses default threshold of 10.
4. Running `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh abc` exits 2 with a usage message.
5. Running `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 0` exits 2 (invalid — must be positive integer).
6. If `go list ./internal/...` fails, the script exits 2 with "go list failed" message (not silent pass).
7. Only module-internal imports are counted (imports starting with module path from `go list -m`).
8. Self-imports are excluded from the count.
9. Test file imports (`.Imports` excludes test files by default in `go list`) are NOT counted.
10. `make check-go` includes the new step labeled `[7/11] Go: import fanout check` and invokes `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 10`.
11. All existing `check-go` step labels are updated from `[N/10]` to `[N/11]`.
12. The script does NOT have an allowlist mechanism.
13. Output lists violations sorted by import count descending, with the count and package path (relative to module root). Example output:
    ```
    Import fanout violations (threshold: 10):
    21  internal/cli
    20  internal/webui
    ```
14. Package paths in output are displayed as relative paths (e.g., `internal/cli` not `github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli`).
15. `scripts/check-import-fanout_test.sh` exists and passes.

## Testing Strategy

### Automated tests (`scripts/check-import-fanout_test.sh`)

Follow the `check-coverage_test.sh` mock pattern — create a mock `go` binary that intercepts `go list` commands and returns controlled output.

**Mock `go` binary**:
- Intercepts `go list -m` → returns `example.com/testmod`
- Intercepts `go list -f '...' ./internal/...` → returns pre-configured package/import lines
- Falls through to real `go` for anything else (not needed, but safe)

**Test cases**:
1. **Under threshold**: 3 packages each importing 3 internal packages → exit 0
2. **Over threshold**: 1 package importing 15 internal packages (threshold 10) → exit 1 with correct output
3. **Multiple violations**: 2 packages over, 1 under → exit 1, both listed in descending order
4. **Custom threshold via `$1`**: threshold=3 with a 5-import package → exit 1
5. **Default threshold**: no arg → uses 10
6. **Self-import excluded**: package imports itself in mock output → count excludes it
7. **Invalid threshold**: `abc` → exit 2
8. **Zero threshold**: `0` → exit 2
9. **`go list` failure**: mock `go` exits 1 → script exits 2 with error message
10. **Relative path output**: violations show `internal/foo` not full module path

### Manual verification

1. Run `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 10` and verify it lists `internal/cli` (21) and `internal/webui` (20)
2. Run `./scripts/check-import-fanout.sh 25` and verify it passes
3. Run `make check-go` and verify the new step appears at position `[7/11]`
4. Verify all other steps are renumbered correctly

### Script structure reference

The script should follow this skeleton (matching `.9`'s conventions):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-import-fanout.sh — Prevent packages from accumulating cross-cutting deps.
# Counts module-internal imports per Go package under internal/.
# Fails with exit 1 if any package exceeds the threshold.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
THRESHOLD="${1:-10}"

# Validate threshold
if ! [[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "Usage: check-import-fanout.sh [THRESHOLD]" >&2
    echo "  THRESHOLD must be a positive integer (default: 10)" >&2
    exit 2
fi

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# Get module path
MODULE=$(go list -m 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Error: go list -m failed" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -n "$MODULE" ]] || { echo "Error: empty module path" >&2; exit 2; }

# Get imports for all internal packages
GOLIST_OUTPUT=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$GOLIST_OUTPUT"' EXIT

if ! go list -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{join .Imports ","}}' ./internal/... > "$GOLIST_OUTPUT" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Error: go list failed — fix build errors first" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# Count module-internal imports per package
violations=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
    pkg="${line%% *}"
    imports="${line#* }"
    # Count imports matching module prefix, excluding self
    count=0
    if [[ "$imports" != "$pkg" ]]; then  # has imports
        count=$(echo "$imports" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -c "^${MODULE}/" || true)
        # Exclude self-import if present
        if echo "$imports" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -qx "$pkg"; then
            count=$((count - 1))
        fi
    fi
    if (( count > THRESHOLD )); then
        rel="${pkg#"${MODULE}/"}"
        violations+=("$(printf '%d\t%s' "$count" "$rel")")
    fi
done < "$GOLIST_OUTPUT"

if [[ ${#violations[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "Import fanout violations (threshold: $THRESHOLD):" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "${violations[@]}" | sort -rn >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

title: Phase 7: Add check-dir-size.mjs — max 15 frontend files per directory, hard fail, no allowlist
description: Create frontend scripts/check-dir-size.mjs. Counts .ts/.tsx files per src/ directory (excluding __tests__, test-utils, node_modules, dist). Fails with exit 1 if any directory exceeds 15 files. No allowlist. Wire into npm run check:arch. Mirrors the existing check-loc.mjs pattern but checks directory breadth instead of file length. Plan: /Users/tyson/.claude/plans/purrfect-weaving-stream.md
design:
## Summary

Create `internal/webui/frontend/scripts/check-dir-size.mjs` — a Node ESM script that walks `internal/webui/frontend/src/` recursively, counts `.ts`/`.tsx` files at depth 1 of every directory, and fails with exit 1 if any directory exceeds 15 files. No allowlist. Wire it into `npm run check:arch` (which is invoked from `make check-frontend` step `[4/6] architectural checks`). This is the final frontend "directory breadth" gate that mirrors the Go-side `check-package-size.sh` (`.9`) and prevents frontend domain directories from re-accumulating into god-dirs after the Phase 6 splits (`.6`, `.7`, `.26`, `.27`) land.

## Technical Approach

### Counting method: recursive filesystem walk, per-directory depth-1 count

Walk `src/` recursively. For every directory encountered (including `src/` itself, plus every nested directory), count the number of direct-child files whose name ends in `.ts` or `.tsx`. Files in nested sub-directories do NOT roll up into the parent — each directory is evaluated on its own immediate contents. This is what makes the gate force *splitting*: a parent directory with 20 files can only pass by moving files into a new sub-directory, which the parent then does not see.

Why recursive (not just one level under `src/`): without recursion, a developer could evade the gate by creating `src/hooks/x/` and dumping 30 files there. By checking every directory, that sub-dir is itself gated.

### Directory exclusions (whole-subtree, not walked into)

The walker prunes these directory basenames and does **not** descend into them:

- `__tests__` — test files are organized by their own convention, not the dir-size budget
- `test-utils` — test helpers, out of scope for architectural metrics
- `generated` — machine-produced code (e.g. `src/types/generated/openapi.ts`). Explicit requirement from the epic notes: "Generated code directories (src/types/generated/, src/api/generated/) must be EXCLUDED from the 15-file dir-size check. Generated code is machine-produced and its count is driven by the OpenAPI spec, not developer discipline. The check-dir-size.mjs script should skip directories named 'generated'. This is not an allowlist — it's a categorical exclusion for machine output, same as excluding node_modules or dist."
- `node_modules` — third-party, never counted
- `dist` — build output, never counted

Implementation detail: the walker checks the directory's basename. If the basename matches any of the excluded names, the walker does NOT descend AND the directory itself is NOT added to the list of directories to measure. (A directory named `__tests__` must not itself be flagged for having 20 test files.)

### File counting rule (no file-level filtering)

At each non-excluded directory, count every file with extension `.ts` or `.tsx`. **No file-level exclusions** — in particular:

- `.test.ts` / `.test.tsx` / `.spec.ts` / `.spec.tsx` files that live next to source files (e.g. `src/hooks/useSort.test.ts`, `src/api/client.test.ts`) **ARE counted**.
- `.d.ts` files are counted (this affects exactly one file, `src/vite-env.d.ts`, in a directory of 5 — a no-op).
- `TestFixtures.tsx` is counted.

Rationale for including co-located test files: the Phase 6 split task descriptions use the raw `.ts/.tsx` count as their headline ("Split src/hooks (82 files)" — verified: 82 includes 15 co-located `.test.ts` files; only 67 are source). The split tasks are sized against the raw count, so the gate must measure the raw count. Filtering out test files would silently allow `7 source + 15 tests = 22 files` in a single directory while still passing, which contradicts the split tasks' own arithmetic.

This diverges from `check-loc.mjs`'s `shouldSkip` (which excludes test files because LOC is a per-file bloat metric, not a per-directory breadth metric). That divergence is intentional and documented in the script header comment.

### Threshold

Hardcoded constant at the top of the file: `export const DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD = 15;`. No CLI argument for threshold — this is a hard rule, not a configurable knob. Tests parametrize the threshold by calling `checkDirSize(root, { threshold })` directly.

**"Exceeds 15" semantics**: a directory with exactly 15 files passes. A directory with 16 files fails. Implemented as `count > threshold`.

### Output format

On pass: `✓ All directories within 15-file limit (N directories scanned)` to stdout, exit 0.

On failure: list each violating directory with its file count, sorted descending by count, path relative to the frontend dir. Follows the `check-loc.mjs` output style:

```
  82	src/hooks
  41	src/components/TerminalView
  34	src/components/IssueDetailPanel
  34	src/api
  20	src/types
  16	src/components/WorkspaceTree

✗ 6 directory(ies) exceed 15-file limit
```

Violations are written to stderr. Exit code 1.

### Exit codes

- `0` — all directories pass
- `1` — one or more violations
- `2` — setup error (src/ directory not found, not a directory, or walker I/O error)

### Module structure (mirrors `check-loc.mjs`)

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Check that no directory under frontend src/ contains more than 15 .ts/.tsx files at depth 1.
// Generated, __tests__, test-utils, node_modules, dist directories are excluded entirely.
// Test files (.test.ts/.test.tsx) ARE counted — the gate measures directory breadth, not file bloat.
// No allowlist: if a directory is too full, split it into sub-dirs.

import { readdirSync, statSync } from "fs";
import { join, relative, sep } from "path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";

export const DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD = 15;

export const EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES = new Set([
  "__tests__",
  "test-utils",
  "generated",
  "node_modules",
  "dist",
]);

export function shouldSkipDir(basename) { /* ... */ }
export function isCountableFile(name) { /* extension === .ts || .tsx */ }
export function walkDirs(rootDir) { /* returns array of { dirPath, fileCount } for every non-excluded dir under rootDir, including rootDir itself */ }
export function checkDirSize(frontendDir, srcDir, opts = {}) { /* returns { violations, scannedCount } or { error, exitCode } */ }

function main() { /* resolves frontendDir + srcDir from import.meta.url, calls checkDirSize, prints + exits */ }

const isMainModule = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
if (isMainModule) { main(); }
```

`walkDirs` is a single recursive function:
1. Read the directory's entries.
2. Count direct-child files where `isCountableFile(entry.name)` is true.
3. Append `{ dirPath, fileCount }` for this directory (unless the directory is src/'s excluded parent — src/ itself is always included).
4. Recurse into each sub-directory whose basename is NOT in `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES`.

`checkDirSize` post-filters the walk output: keep only entries where `fileCount > DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD`, sort descending, return.

### Why this approach

- **Consistent with `check-loc.mjs`**: same file layout, same `isMainModule` idiom, same `checkX(root, srcDir, opts)` + `main()` split, same export-for-testability pattern. Eases maintenance.
- **Pure Node, no dependencies**: uses `fs`, `path`, `url`. No glob libraries, no external tools. Matches all existing frontend scripts.
- **Fail-closed by default**: any I/O error aborts with exit 2 and a clear message. Missing `src/` is a hard failure (not a pass-with-zero-violations).

## Conventions Established

1. **`per-directory breadth` gates count raw `.ts/.tsx` including tests.** New convention specific to this task. Rationale: upstream split task descriptions size their work against the raw count. Applies to any future frontend "directory budget" script. Documented in the script header comment.
2. **Excluded-directory basename set is a module-level `Set`**, not a helper function. Easy to read, easy for tests to verify.
3. **Threshold is a module-level `export const`**, not a CLI arg. Consistent with `check-loc.mjs`'s `THRESHOLD_TS`/`THRESHOLD_TSX`. Test overrides are passed through an `opts` object to `checkDirSize`, not via env var or CLI.
4. **No allowlist** — consistent with sibling Phase 7 tasks `.9` and `.10` (both of which explicitly established the "no allowlist" convention for the package-size / import-fanout gates). The task description is explicit: "No allowlist — if a directory is too big, split it."
5. **Output format** — `count\tpath` lines, descending sort, trailing `✗ N directory(ies) exceed ...` summary. Matches `check-loc.mjs`'s violation-listing style so CI log readers see a consistent format across arch gates.
6. **Wiring into `check:arch`** — appended at the end of the existing pipeline (`check:loc && check:no-raw-fetch && check:no-hardcoded-urls && check:boundaries && check:dir-size`). Order is not load-bearing; placing it last keeps the newest gate at the bottom of the pipeline so cached-pass gates run first.

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/scripts/check-dir-size.mjs` (new)

The main script, ~120 lines. Structure:

- Header comment explaining: purpose, the `count test files` divergence from `check-loc.mjs`, no-allowlist rule, 15-file threshold.
- Constants: `DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD = 15`, `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` Set.
- `shouldSkipDir(basename)` — returns true if basename is in the excluded set.
- `isCountableFile(name)` — returns true if name ends in `.ts` or `.tsx`.
- `walkDirs(rootDir)` — recursive walker, returns `Array<{ dirPath, fileCount }>` for every non-excluded directory under (and including) `rootDir`.
- `checkDirSize(frontendDir, srcDir, { threshold = DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD } = {})` — returns either `{ error, exitCode }` on setup failure or `{ violations, scannedCount }` on success.
  - `violations` is a sorted-descending array of `{ relPath, fileCount, threshold }`.
  - `scannedCount` is the number of directories that were walked (for the success message).
- `main()` — resolves `scriptDir = fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url))`, computes `frontendDir = join(scriptDir, "..")`, `srcDir = join(frontendDir, "src")`, calls `checkDirSize`, prints, exits.
- `isMainModule` guard, identical to `check-loc.mjs:174-180`.

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/scripts/__tests__/check-dir-size.test.mjs` (new)

Vitest test suite mirroring `check-loc.test.mjs`. Structure and coverage:

- **`shouldSkipDir` unit tests**: each excluded name (`__tests__`, `test-utils`, `generated`, `node_modules`, `dist`) returns `true`; ordinary names (`hooks`, `components`, `api`) return `false`.
- **`isCountableFile` unit tests**: `.ts` → true, `.tsx` → true, `.js` → false, `.css` → false, `.md` → false, `.d.ts` → true (ends in `.ts`).
- **`walkDirs` unit tests** (temp-dir-based):
  - Empty dir → `[{ dirPath: root, fileCount: 0 }]`
  - Dir with 5 `.ts` files → `fileCount: 5` for root, one entry
  - Dir with a sub-dir → walker returns both root and sub-dir entries
  - Dir with a `__tests__` sub-dir containing 30 files → `__tests__` is not walked, not listed in results; parent's fileCount is unaffected
  - Dir with a `generated` sub-dir containing 50 files → same exclusion behavior
  - Dir with `test-utils`, `node_modules`, `dist` sub-dirs → all excluded
  - Dir with mixed `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.md`, `.css` files → only `.ts` and `.tsx` counted
  - `.test.ts` and `.spec.tsx` files **ARE counted** (explicit negative regression test for the file-filtering divergence from `check-loc.mjs`)
- **`checkDirSize` unit tests** (temp-dir-based):
  - Empty `src/` → `violations: []`, `scannedCount: 1`
  - `src/` with 10 files → no violation
  - `src/` with exactly 15 files → no violation (boundary: 15 passes)
  - `src/` with 16 files → exactly 1 violation, `fileCount: 16`
  - Nested violation: `src/hooks/` with 20 files, `src/` empty → 1 violation for `src/hooks`
  - Multiple violations sort descending: create dirs with 18, 22, 16 files → order is 22, 18, 16
  - `__tests__` sub-dir with 30 files does NOT produce a violation
  - `generated/` sub-dir with 50 files does NOT produce a violation
  - `.test.ts` files next to source DO count toward the parent's total (explicit check: put 8 source + 8 `.test.ts` files → total 16 → violation)
  - Custom threshold override via opts: threshold=10 with a 12-file dir → violation
  - Missing `srcDir` → `{ error: /not found/, exitCode: 2 }`
  - `srcDir` is a file, not a directory → `{ error: /not a directory/, exitCode: 2 }`
  - `relPath` in violations is frontend-relative using forward slashes (normalize `sep` → `/` — same as `check-loc.mjs:118`)
- **Constants tests**:
  - `DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD === 15`
  - `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` is a `Set` and contains all 5 expected names (and no more)
- **Subprocess integration tests** (using `execFileSync("node", ["--input-type=module", "-e", inlineScript])` pattern from `check-loc.test.mjs:88-102`):
  - Empty project dir → exit 0, stdout contains `within 15-file limit`, contains `1 directories scanned`
  - 16-file dir → exit 1, stderr contains `16` and `src/fat`
  - Multiple violations → exit 1, stderr output order is descending (verified by parsing line-leading counts)
  - Summary line exact format: `✗ N directory(ies) exceed 15-file limit`
  - Pass summary exact format: `✓ All directories within 15-file limit (N directories scanned)`

Use the same `makeTmpProject` / `writeFile` helpers from `check-loc.test.mjs:34-50`. Do not share code between the two test files — duplicate the helpers inline to keep the test file self-contained, matching the pattern used by the other `__tests__/check-*.test.mjs` files.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/package.json`

Two edits (lines 15-19):

1. Add a new `"check:dir-size"` entry after `"check:boundaries"` (between current lines 18 and 19):
   ```json
   "check:boundaries": "node scripts/check-component-boundaries.mjs",
   "check:dir-size": "node scripts/check-dir-size.mjs",
   ```
2. Extend the `"check:arch"` pipeline to chain `check:dir-size` at the end:
   ```json
   "check:arch": "npm run check:loc && npm run check:no-raw-fetch && npm run check:no-hardcoded-urls && npm run check:boundaries && npm run check:dir-size",
   ```

No other files need changes:
- **`Makefile` is NOT touched**: `make check-frontend` step `[4/6]` already invokes `npm run check:arch`, which transitively calls the new script.
- **`eslint.config.js` is NOT touched**: eslint has no awareness of this gate.
- **No CI workflow files**: CI runs `make check` which runs `make check-frontend` which runs `npm run check:arch`. Transitive.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

Running the neighborhood scan — repo-wide search for directories currently violating the 15-file limit — surfaced 6 directories:

- **`src/hooks` (82 files)** — will be split by sibling task `loomcli-rir82.6`. Listed as a dependency of this task. Not touched here. This gate will fail on `src/hooks` until `.6` lands.
- **`src/components/TerminalView` (41 files)** and **`src/components/IssueDetailPanel` (34 files)** — will be split by sibling task `loomcli-rir82.7`. Listed as a dependency. This gate will fail on both until `.7` lands.
- **`src/types` (20 files)** — will be split by sibling task `loomcli-rir82.26`. Listed as a dependency. This gate will fail until `.26` lands.
- **`src/components/WorkspaceTree` (16 files)** — will be split by sibling task `loomcli-rir82.27`. Listed as a dependency. This gate will fail until `.27` lands.
- **`src/api` (34 files)** — this is the tricky one. Task `.8` ("Split frontend src/api into domain sub-dirs") was **closed as superseded** with reason: "Superseded by Phase 4 OpenAPI generation (.15-.18). Hand-written src/api/ will be replaced by generated client from openapi.yaml, not manually split into sub-dirs." However, the hand-written files still exist at `src/api/` depth 1 (26 source + 8 co-located `.test.ts` = 34 files). Phase 4 (.15-.21) is marked complete in the epic, but the old hand-written files have not been removed. **This is an unresolved gap in the Phase 4 → Phase 7 hand-off.** It is explicitly out of scope for this task — the script will correctly flag `src/api` as a violation, and the resolution requires either (a) re-opening a replacement for `.8` to remove or decompose the hand-written api files, or (b) filing a follow-up task to complete the migration to the generated client. **Before this task's implementation is merged, a decision must be made — either re-open the split work, file a follow-up, or confirm with the human reviewer that the gate is expected to fail on `src/api` until the migration completes.** The planner flags this explicitly so the implementation agent does not attempt to solve it silently.

Other directories at or near the limit (all currently passing):
- `src/components/AgentDetailPanel` (15 files) — exactly at threshold, passes, but has zero headroom. Not in scope.
- `src/utils` (14 files), `src/views` (10 files), etc. — all under threshold.

Neighborhood scan — scripts with similar shape that were inspected to confirm the pattern:
- `scripts/check-loc.mjs` — matched: ESM + export helpers + `isMainModule` main() + tmpdir-based tests. Copied structure.
- `scripts/check-component-boundaries.mjs` — matched: same module layout, same test-file sibling convention.
- `scripts/check-no-raw-fetch.mjs`, `scripts/check-no-hardcoded-urls.mjs`, `scripts/check-openapi-staleness.mjs` — same module layout. No code needs to be modified in any of these; they are reference patterns only.

## Dependencies

- **No new npm packages.** The script uses only `fs`, `path`, `url` from Node stdlib — same as `check-loc.mjs`.
- **Hard task dependencies** (listed on the BD task, must land before this task's implementation makes CI green):
  - `loomcli-rir82.6` (hooks split)
  - `loomcli-rir82.7` (TerminalView + IssueDetailPanel split)
  - `loomcli-rir82.26` (types split)
  - `loomcli-rir82.27` (WorkspaceTree split)
- **Soft dependency** (not on the BD task, but needed for the gate to actually pass): a resolution for the `src/api` 34-file overflow — see Out of Scope. The implementation agent must NOT attempt to fix this; they must surface the issue in a bd comment or loom complete note so the human can decide.
- **No ordering constraint** with sibling `loomcli-rir82.12` (eslint-plugin-boundaries) — disjoint concerns, can land in either order.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Empty `src/` directory**: `walkDirs` returns `[{ dirPath: srcDir, fileCount: 0 }]`. No violations. Success message: "1 directories scanned". **Expected behavior**: pass.
2. **`src/` does not exist**: `statSync` throws. `checkDirSize` returns `{ error: "Error: src/ directory not found at <path>", exitCode: 2 }`. `main()` prints to stderr and exits 2. **No fallback pass** — a missing `src/` is treated as a configuration error, not an empty-repo pass.
3. **`src/` is a file, not a directory**: `statSync(srcDir).isDirectory() === false`. `checkDirSize` returns `{ error: "Error: <path> is not a directory", exitCode: 2 }`. Exit 2.
4. **Directory with exactly 15 files**: passes. Strict `>` comparison.
5. **Directory with exactly 16 files**: fails. Violation entry: `{ relPath: "...", fileCount: 16, threshold: 15 }`.
6. **Nested excluded directory**: e.g. `src/components/Foo/__tests__/nested.ts`. `__tests__` is skipped at every depth — the walker never descends into any directory named `__tests__` regardless of where it appears in the tree.
7. **A `generated/` directory at any depth**: not walked. So `src/types/generated/` is excluded AND `src/api/generated/` (if it existed) would also be excluded AND `src/components/Foo/generated/` (hypothetical future) would also be excluded. The rule is name-based, not path-based.
8. **A directory with only `.js` files and no `.ts`/`.tsx`**: `fileCount: 0`. Not a violation, but still added to the walker output (so `scannedCount` reflects all walked dirs). **Do NOT early-return a zero-count directory** — the success message prints the scanned count, which is useful telemetry.
9. **A directory named `__tests__` at `src/__tests__/`**: Not walked, not measured, even if it has 100 files. Same rule as (6).
10. **`.ts`/`.tsx` file at `src/` root**: counted against `src/`. Currently 5 files (App.tsx, TestFixtures.tsx, main.tsx, router.tsx, vite-env.d.ts) → under threshold.
11. **Symbolic links**: `readdirSync` returns them with `entry.isDirectory()` following the symlink. If a symlinked dir points into `node_modules`, the walker prunes on basename (won't match `node_modules` at the link's *parent* name necessarily). **Decision**: accept symlink-follow behavior. If a symlink to something unexpected gets added, the implementer can file a follow-up. No defensive `lstat` check — over-engineering.
12. **Walker I/O error** (e.g. permission denied reading a sub-dir): the uncaught exception propagates out of `walkDirs`. `main()` does NOT catch it — the script crashes with a stack trace. **Decision**: this is OK, matches `check-loc.mjs` behavior. Permission errors in `src/` are a system-level configuration problem and a stack trace is the right feedback.
13. **Case-sensitivity of excluded names**: `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` is checked with exact-string `.has(basename)`. A directory named `__Tests__` or `Generated` would NOT be skipped. **Decision**: accept. The project's convention is lowercase `__tests__`/`generated`; any deviation is a naming error and should be surfaced by the gate.
14. **Race condition — a file is deleted between `readdirSync` and `statSync`**: not possible because we don't `statSync` individual files, we only check extension. No race risk.
15. **`TestFixtures.tsx` at `src/` root**: counted (unlike `check-loc.mjs`, which skips it). `src/` has only 5 files, so this is a no-op currently. Documented in the header comment to pre-empt confusion.
16. **A directory has a file named `.ts` or `.tsx` with no basename** (e.g. `foo/.tsx`): `isCountableFile` checks the name ends with `.ts` or `.tsx`, so `.tsx` would match. **Decision**: accept. These files don't exist in practice and adding a check adds complexity for zero benefit.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Script behavior:**

1. Running `node internal/webui/frontend/scripts/check-dir-size.mjs` with the real repo today exits with code `1` and lists exactly these 6 directories as violations in descending order: `src/hooks (82)`, `src/components/TerminalView (41)`, `src/components/IssueDetailPanel (34)`, `src/api (34)`, `src/types (20)`, `src/components/WorkspaceTree (16)`. (The ordering between the two `34`-count entries is implementation-defined; either is acceptable as long as both are listed.)
2. The script exits with code `0` when every directory under `src/` has ≤15 `.ts`/`.tsx` files at depth 1.
3. A directory with exactly 15 files passes (boundary).
4. A directory with 16 files fails (boundary).
5. No allowlist mechanism exists: there is no `ALLOWLIST` export, no config file, no env var, no CLI flag that can exempt a directory from the check.
6. `__tests__`, `test-utils`, `generated`, `node_modules`, `dist` directories are never walked into and are never listed as violations, regardless of their contents.
7. `.test.ts` / `.test.tsx` / `.spec.ts` / `.spec.tsx` files that live at depth 1 of a directory ARE counted toward that directory's total. (Regression test against the `check-loc.mjs`-style "skip tests" convention.)
8. The script crashes-loud with exit code `2` and a "not found" error message if `src/` does not exist.

**Output format:**

9. On failure, each violation is printed as `  <count>\t<path>` on stderr, with `<path>` relative to the frontend directory and using forward slashes (even on Windows).
10. On failure, the summary line `✗ N directory(ies) exceed 15-file limit` appears on stderr after the violation list.
11. On success, the summary line `✓ All directories within 15-file limit (N directories scanned)` appears on stdout.
12. Violations are sorted by file count in descending order.

**Wiring:**

13. `package.json` has a new `"check:dir-size"` script entry that invokes `node scripts/check-dir-size.mjs`.
14. `package.json`'s `"check:arch"` script chains `check:dir-size` at the end of the `&&` pipeline.
15. Running `npm run check:arch` in `internal/webui/frontend/` invokes the new script as the final step.
16. Running `make check-frontend` at the repo root invokes `npm run check:arch`, which transitively invokes the new script. (The existing Makefile step `[4/6] Frontend: architectural checks` now covers dir-size implicitly — no Makefile edit required.)

**Tests:**

17. `internal/webui/frontend/scripts/__tests__/check-dir-size.test.mjs` exists and passes via `npm run test:unit` (vitest).
18. Test count is ≥20 cases covering: `shouldSkipDir`, `isCountableFile`, `walkDirs`, `checkDirSize` (direct), and subprocess integration.
19. An explicit regression test asserts that a directory with 8 source + 8 `.test.ts` files (total 16) produces exactly 1 violation with `fileCount: 16`. (Pins the "count tests" convention.)
20. An explicit regression test asserts that a directory with 30 files inside a `__tests__/` sub-dir and 5 files at depth 1 produces 0 violations. (Pins the `__tests__` exclusion.)
21. An explicit regression test asserts that the boundary case (15 passes, 16 fails) is correct.

**Negative cases:**

22. No file named `check-dir-size.sh` or any other shell-script variant is created. The script is Node ESM, matching the `.mjs` convention of other frontend scripts.
23. No changes to `Makefile`. (The script is wired purely through `package.json`.)
24. No changes to `eslint.config.js`. (eslint has no awareness of this gate.)
25. No `ALLOWLIST` export, no `IGNORE_DIRS` env var, no `--allow` CLI flag. The only configurability is the `opts.threshold` argument to `checkDirSize` for testing purposes; the public CLI has no args.
26. No helper function named `shouldSkipFile` or similar — there is no file-level skip logic (the divergence from `check-loc.mjs` is enforced by omission).
27. The script does NOT import from `check-loc.mjs` — the two scripts are independent, even where they have similar helpers. Independence is intentional so a future change to `check-loc.mjs`'s `shouldSkip` cannot accidentally change `check-dir-size.mjs`'s semantics.

## Testing Strategy

### Automated tests (`scripts/__tests__/check-dir-size.test.mjs`)

Follow the `check-loc.test.mjs` layout — vitest, `mkdtempSync`, `describe`/`it`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach`, direct function tests + subprocess integration tests. Specific suites:

1. **`shouldSkipDir`** — 5 positive cases (each excluded name), 3 negative cases (`hooks`, `components`, `api`).
2. **`isCountableFile`** — `.ts` yes, `.tsx` yes, `.d.ts` yes (ends in `.ts`), `.js` no, `.css` no, `.md` no, file with no extension no.
3. **`walkDirs`** — temp-dir-based. Verify recursion, exclusion of each excluded name, counting of mixed extensions.
4. **`checkDirSize`** — temp-dir-based. Cover all edge cases from the "Edge Cases" section.
5. **Constants** — `DIR_SIZE_THRESHOLD === 15`, `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES.size === 5` with exact membership.
6. **Subprocess integration** — spawn `node --input-type=module -e <inline>` that imports `checkDirSize` from the real script and runs it against a temp project. Follows `check-loc.test.mjs:88-102`. Verify exit codes (0, 1, 2), stdout/stderr content, sort order.

### Manual verification

After implementation:

1. `cd internal/webui/frontend && node scripts/check-dir-size.mjs` — verify exit code 1 and that the 6 expected violations are listed in descending order.
2. `cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run check:dir-size` — same result via the new package.json script.
3. `cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run check:arch` — verify pipeline runs all previous checks first, then hits `check:dir-size` last and fails there (or passes entirely if all prerequisite splits are done).
4. `cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run test:unit -- check-dir-size` — verify the new test file passes.
5. Create a temp dir outside the repo, drop 16 .ts files in it, run `node /path/to/check-dir-size.mjs` with that as cwd (won't work directly — the script resolves src/ via `import.meta.url`). Instead: create `tmp/src/overflowing/` with 16 files under the actual repo (in a branch), run the script, verify the new dir is flagged. Delete tmp/ before committing.
6. Verify `make check-frontend` invokes the new check transitively: grep the Makefile's `check-frontend` target output for the new step. (No explicit step label — it runs under `[4/6] architectural checks`.)
7. Verify no regressions in other gates: all of `check:loc`, `check:no-raw-fetch`, `check:no-hardcoded-urls`, `check:boundaries` still behave identically.

The script correctly flags 2 current violations: src/api (34 files, blocked on loomcli-0vopm) and src/utils (16 files, blocked on new followup loomcli-984yn). title: Phase 7: Add eslint-plugin-boundaries for frontend layer DAG enforcement
description: Install eslint-plugin-boundaries. Configure strict layer DAG in eslint.config.js: views → components, hooks, stores, api, utils, types. components → components, hooks, utils, types (NO api — must go through hooks). hooks → hooks, api, stores, utils, types. stores → api, utils, types. api → utils, types. utils → types. types → nothing. Audit current imports for violations, fix them before enabling as error. This prevents components from accumulating data-fetching logic. Plan: /Users/tyson/.claude/plans/purrfect-weaving-stream.md
design:
## Summary

Install `eslint-plugin-boundaries` v6 and configure a strict layer DAG for `internal/webui/frontend/src/` that prevents cross-cutting architecture drift — in particular, stopping components from accumulating direct data-fetching logic. Each source file is classified into exactly one architectural layer by path pattern; the `boundaries/dependencies` rule (v6's replacement for the deprecated `element-types`) enforces the allowed edges. Type-only imports are allowed across otherwise-forbidden edges so that shared DTOs don't force runtime coupling. Before the rule is enabled at error severity, all existing runtime violations are fixed in-repo (no allowlist). This task is the final Phase 7 linter gate for the frontend; together with `.9` (Go package size), `.10` (Go import fanout), and `.11` (frontend dir size) it locks in the Phase 3–6 refactor.

## Technical Approach

### Plugin and rule choice (v6)

Use `eslint-plugin-boundaries@^6.0.2`. The v6 API consolidates the old `element-types`, `no-private`, `entry-point`, and `external` rules into a single `boundaries/dependencies` rule. Design against `boundaries/dependencies` only — do **not** use `element-types` (deprecated/removed in v6).

Key v6 feature we rely on: `dependency.kind: "type" | "value" | "typeof"` on `allow`/`disallow` selectors. This lets us express "components may import **types** from api, but not **values**" as a first-class rule, without allowlist workarounds or `ignoreMatches` hacks.

### Layer DAG (settled)

The task description lists views/components/hooks/stores/api/utils/types. Current `src/` also contains `contexts/`, `styles/`, `test-utils/`, and four loose root files (`App.tsx`, `main.tsx`, `router.tsx`, `TestFixtures.tsx`). The design assigns each to a layer to avoid "unknown file" failures:

| Layer | Pattern | Allowed imports from |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | `src/*.{ts,tsx}` (App, main, router, TestFixtures) | `views`, `components`, `contexts`, `hooks`, `stores`, `api`, `utils`, `types` |
| `views` | `src/views/**` | `components`, `contexts`, `hooks`, `stores`, `api`, `utils`, `types` |
| `contexts` | `src/contexts/**` | `hooks`, `stores`, `api`, `utils`, `types` |
| `components` | `src/components/**` | `components`, `contexts`, `hooks`, `utils`, `types` (NO api, NO stores, NO views) |
| `hooks` | `src/hooks/**` | `hooks`, `contexts`, `stores`, `api`, `utils`, `types` (NO components, NO views) |
| `stores` | `src/stores/**` | `api`, `utils`, `types` |
| `api` | `src/api/**` | `utils`, `types` |
| `utils` | `src/utils/**` | `types` |
| `types` | `src/types/**` | nothing (generated files live under `src/types/generated/**`, intra-layer) |
| `styles` | `src/styles/**` | `types` (in practice, CSS only; `.ts` files in styles are the tokens barrel) |

Element patterns use `mode: "file"` so `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx` files are classified by their own path (so tests under `src/components/Foo/Foo.test.tsx` still resolve to `components`). `__tests__/` subdirectories inherit the parent layer via the same micromatch patterns. `test-utils/**` is excluded via `boundaries/ignore` — test helper code is not subject to the DAG.

**Decisions and their rationale (so edge cases don't get re-decided by the implementer):**

1. **`contexts` is placed between `views` and `hooks`.** Contexts provide app-wide state; they may call hooks and api directly to bootstrap. They may NOT import `components` (today there are 2 type-only violations — both must be fixed by relocating the types). They are importable by `views`, `components`, and `app` (components currently reach into contexts via `useContext(AuthContext)`-style patterns — 8 such imports today, all legal under this DAG).

2. **`app` is the top-level layer** for `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/router.tsx`, `src/TestFixtures.tsx`. These four files wire everything together and may import from anywhere. Without this layer they'd be "unknown files" and fail `no-unknown-files`.

3. **`components → views` is forbidden.** A component must never reference a page.

4. **`components → stores` is forbidden.** Stores are accessed via hooks. Current code already follows this (zero violations today).

5. **`hooks → components` is forbidden.** This has 9 type-only violations today (e.g., `import type { ColumnDef } from "@/components/table/columns"`). Fix by moving the affected types into `src/types/`.

6. **Type-only imports are globally allowed across forbidden edges.** Implemented via a second rule entry with `allow: { dependency: { kind: "type" } }` that covers every `from` type. Justification: the goal of the DAG (per the task description) is "prevents components from accumulating **data-fetching logic**". Data fetching is a runtime concern; `import type { Foo }` is erased at compile time and introduces no runtime coupling. Forbidding all type-only cross-layer imports would require mass-relocating DTOs to `src/types/` and is explicitly out of scope for this task.

7. **`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` is added as `"error"`** so that the type-only escape hatch can actually be trusted. Without this rule, developers could write `import { Foo } from "@/api/foo"` and TS would erase it at runtime anyway, bypassing the value-import ban entirely. Enforcing `import type { Foo }` ensures runtime-vs-type intent is explicit in source.

8. **No allowlist.** Consistent with sibling tasks `.9` and `.10` (`no-allowlist` was the explicit convention those tasks established). Every current violation is either fixed in-repo or is a legitimate type-only import.

9. **`default: "disallow"`.** Any edge not explicitly listed is forbidden. This is stricter than `default: "allow"` and matches the "strict DAG" language of the task.

### Import-resolution settings

`boundaries/elements` only classifies files; the plugin still relies on an import resolver to follow `@/` path aliases. Configure:

```js
settings: {
  "import/resolver": {
    typescript: { project: "./tsconfig.json" }
  },
  "boundaries/elements": [ /* patterns below */ ],
  "boundaries/ignore": [
    "src/test-utils/**",
    "src/**/__tests__/**",
    "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}",
    "src/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}",
    "src/vite-env.d.ts"
  ]
}
```

Tests are ignored to keep the DAG enforced only on production code. The frontend already has `test-utils/` and `__tests__/` conventions; tests legitimately reach across layers (e.g., a `views` test imports mocks from `test-utils/` which in turn imports `api` fixtures).

`eslint-import-resolver-typescript` must be added as a devDependency so the `@/*` → `src/*` alias resolves. Without it, cross-layer imports via `@/` silently fall through and the rule short-circuits to "unresolved, skip". This is a common v6 footgun and must be wired correctly for the gate to have teeth.
