design:
## Summary

Update the local dev experience to reflect the Phase 5 decoupling (`.19` removes `//go:embed` + `--dev` flag, `.20` adds `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `.28` deletes `frontend-ensure` + rebuilds the release pipeline). Post-.19 the Go server is a pure API, so the whole "loom-served UI with frontend dist watcher" story (`scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh`, `make dev-loom`, `--dev` in `.air.toml`) is obsolete — there is nothing to watch-rebuild dist for. This task consolidates all dev paths into a single `make dev` that runs the Go server on `:8080` and the Vite dev server on `:3000` in parallel, fixes `.air.toml` so `air` no longer passes the removed `--dev` flag (and adds `--frontend-url http://localhost:3000` so cross-origin modes also work), refreshes the docs (`README.md`, `docs/testing/test-infrastructure.md`), updates the Go test (`makefile_test.go:TestMakeDryRun_Dev`) that still asserts the old script, adds a one-command `docker-compose.dev.yml` at the repo root that brings up the API + frontend (via `deploy/` images) with an optional `fleet` profile for Redis, and deletes `scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` + `scripts/dev_test.sh` (the latter only tests a script that is being renamed/deleted — it is replaced by an updated suite for the single remaining `dev.sh`).

This is the dev-half of Phase 5. Sibling `.19` covers server decoupling, `.20` covers frontend decoupling, `.28` covers build/release/deploy. The remaining Phase 5 child epic parent-work becomes "developer runs `make dev`, gets two hot-reloading processes, same as before".

## Technical Approach

### Strategy: one dev path, not three

Pre-Phase-5 there were three overlapping targets:

| Target | Script | What it did |
|---|---|---|
| `make dev` | `run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` | air + `npm run build --watch` (Loom-served UI) |
| `make dev-loom` | `run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` | same as `dev` |
| `make dev-vite` | `dev.sh` | air + `npm run dev` (Vite HMR on :3000) |

Post-.19 there is **no Loom-served UI**, so `run-web-ui-with-loom.sh`'s entire premise (keep `dist/` fresh so `//go:embed` serves it) is gone. The only shape that survives is the `dev-vite` shape: Go API server + Vite dev server, two ports.

We collapse to one target:

| Target | Script | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `make dev` | `scripts/dev.sh` | air (Go server on :8080) + Vite dev server on :3000 in parallel |

`make dev-loom` and `make dev-vite` become **deprecated aliases** that print a one-line warning and forward to `make dev`. This preserves muscle memory for one release cycle. A follow-up task will delete the aliases (flagged in Out of Scope).

### Fixing `.air.toml`

`.air.toml` currently has:
```toml
args_bin = ["serve", "--dev", "--no-daemon"]
```

After `.19` lands, `--dev` is an unknown flag and `air` will crash-loop. We change to:
```toml
args_bin = ["serve", "--no-daemon", "--frontend-url", "http://localhost:3000"]
```

Why `--frontend-url http://localhost:3000`? Two modes to support in local dev:
1. **Default (Vite dev proxy)** — `VITE_API_BASE_URL` unset. Frontend issues relative `/api/...` URLs, Vite dev proxy forwards `/api` → `:8080`. CORS is never exercised (browser sees same-origin `:3000`). `--frontend-url` is a no-op in this mode.
2. **Cross-origin dev** — developer sets `VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080` (or an ngrok URL). Frontend issues absolute requests from `http://localhost:3000`. CORS preflights hit the Go server, which must have `http://localhost:3000` in its allow-list. The flag enables this mode.

Passing the flag unconditionally is safe (it is inert in mode 1) and is the minimum code change that makes both modes work. This matches the `.env.example` note that already tells developers to set `--frontend-url` to `http://localhost:3000` in cross-origin dev.

### Refactoring `scripts/dev.sh`

The current `scripts/dev.sh` already does the right shape (air + Vite in parallel). Minor polish:

1. Pre-flight: print both URLs up front (already does) and note that `/api/*` is proxied through Vite (documentation-only echo line).
2. No functional flag changes needed — `air` picks up `args_bin` from `.air.toml`, so fixing `.air.toml` is enough.
3. Keep `bd daemon` auto-start (useful for local dev).
4. Keep existing `node_modules` auto-install.
5. Update the header comment to reflect the new mental model ("Go API + Vite dev server, same as pre-decoupling dev-vite, now the only dev path").
6. Add one-line sanity check: warn if `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is set but does not include `localhost` and the developer did not pass `--frontend-url` explicitly. Skipped for now — over-engineering. Just noted in the comment header.

### Deleting `scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh`

This script is a dead end post-.19:
- It does `npm run build --watch` into `dist/` so `//go:embed` can pick it up. Embed is gone.
- It runs `air` which invokes `loom serve --dev`. Flag is gone.
- It has zero reason to exist.

Strategy: **delete the file** (consistent with `.19`'s "delete, don't deprecate" stance for the pre-v2-cut branch).

Downstream cleanup (same PR):
- `makefile_test.go:TestMakeDryRun_Dev` (lines 195–205) asserts `make -n dev` contains `./scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh`. Update to assert `./scripts/dev.sh` instead.
- `docs/testing/test-infrastructure.md` section `### scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` (lines 112–120) is deleted. Section `### scripts/dev.sh` is updated to describe the single dev path.
- `README.md:265–273` "Development" section is rewritten to show `make dev` only.

`third_party/beads/scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` is the vendored beads copy — **not touched** (vendored code is frozen per CLAUDE.md).

### `docker-compose.dev.yml` at the repo root

Distinct from `deploy/docker-compose.yml` (from `.28`, which is the production reference with nginx reverse-proxying same-origin). The dev compose is a **smoke-test-the-whole-stack in one command** file, not the primary dev loop. Day-to-day dev is still `make dev` with native tools because native `air` + native Vite dev are faster and simpler than containerized equivalents.

Shape:

```yaml
# docker-compose.dev.yml — one-command local stack smoke test
# NOTE: day-to-day dev should use `make dev` (native air + vite, faster).
# This file is for (a) smoke-testing the containerized stack end-to-end,
# (b) running the fleet-db/Redis path locally without a native install.
#
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml --profile fleet up --build
services:
  server:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: deploy/server/Dockerfile
    environment:
      LOOM_FRONTEND_URL: "http://localhost:3000"
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    restart: unless-stopped

  frontend:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: deploy/frontend/Dockerfile
      args:
        VITE_API_BASE_URL: "http://localhost:8080"
    ports:
      - "3000:80"
    depends_on:
      server:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    profiles: ["fleet"]
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    restart: unless-stopped
```

Key differences vs. `deploy/docker-compose.yml`:

| | `deploy/docker-compose.yml` (.28) | `docker-compose.dev.yml` (.29) |
|---|---|---|
| Location | `deploy/` | repo root |
| API port | only exposed internally | `8080:8080` (direct access) |
| Frontend port | `8080:80` (same-origin via nginx) | `3000:80` (distinct) |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `""` (relative, nginx proxies) | `http://localhost:8080` (cross-origin, exercises CORS) |
| `LOOM_FRONTEND_URL` | `"http://localhost"` (no-op) | `"http://localhost:3000"` (real) |
| Redis | absent | present under `fleet` profile |
| Purpose | production reference | dev smoke test |

The CORS-exercising choice is deliberate: it's the exact shape a real cross-origin deployment will take, which makes this a useful smoke test rather than a second copy of the production compose.

Redis is behind a **compose profile** (`profiles: ["fleet"]`) so it is opt-in: `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml --profile fleet up`. Without the profile flag, Redis does not start and developers who do not use fleet pay zero setup cost.

Reuses the Dockerfiles from `.28`. If `.28` has not landed at merge time, this task has a hard build dependency — flagged below.

### `loom serve --dev` auto-starting Vite — NOT pursued

Task description says "Consider: 'loom serve --dev' flag that auto-starts Vite dev server as a child process for single-command DX (optional, nice-to-have)."

**Decision: Out of Scope.** Three reasons:
1. `.19` explicitly removes `--dev` and adopts a "delete, don't deprecate" stance. Re-introducing a `--dev`-style flag on the Go binary directly contradicts the in-flight direction.
2. `make dev` already provides the single-command DX (one target, two processes). Adding a Go-side child-process spawner duplicates existing functionality.
3. Spawning Node from Go portably (SIGCHLD handling, cleanup on crash, cross-platform pipe/tty wiring) is surprisingly thorny for a "nice-to-have". The bash script does it better.

Flagged in Out of Scope with the justification so future planners can see the decision was intentional, not an oversight.

## Conventions Established

- **`make dev` is the single canonical dev entry point.** It starts Go server on `:8080` (via `air`) and Vite dev server on `:3000` (via `npm run dev`). Previous targets (`dev-loom`, `dev-vite`) become deprecated aliases that forward to it with a one-line warning.
- **Dev ports are fixed: API `:8080`, frontend `:3000`.** The task description mentioned `:5173` (Vite default), but the existing `vite.config.ts` already pins `:3000` with `strictPort: true`. Keep the pin; changing it would ripple through `.env.example`, Playwright projects, and the dev proxy for no gain.
- **`.air.toml` passes `--frontend-url http://localhost:3000` unconditionally.** Safe in same-origin mode (inert), required in cross-origin mode (`VITE_API_BASE_URL` set).
- **`scripts/run-web-ui-with-loom.sh` is deleted, not deprecated.** Matches sibling `.19`'s "delete, don't deprecate" stance for pre-v2-cut cleanup.
- **`scripts/dev.sh` is the single dev script** — one file, one target, one orchestration.
- **`docker-compose.dev.yml` lives at the repo root** (not under `deploy/`) to distinguish it from the production compose. Profiles gate optional services (`fleet` for Redis).
- **Deprecated aliases live for exactly one cleanup pass.** A follow-up task (flagged under Out of Scope) removes `dev-loom`/`dev-vite` once external users (if any) have migrated.

## Files to Create

### `docker-compose.dev.yml` (repo root, new file, ~55 lines)
Defines three services: `server` (built from `deploy/server/Dockerfile`, exposes `:8080`, `LOOM_FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:3000`), `frontend` (built from `deploy/frontend/Dockerfile` with `VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080`, exposes `:3000`), and `redis` (image `redis:7-alpine`, under profile `fleet`, exposes `:6379`, healthcheck on `redis-cli ping`). Server has a healthcheck on `/health`; frontend `depends_on` server being healthy. All restart `unless-stopped`. Top comment explains the file's purpose vs. `deploy/docker-compose.yml` and native `make dev`.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **`make dev` on a host with `air` installed but missing `node_modules`** — `dev-check` verifies `air`, `node`, `npm` exist. `scripts/dev.sh` auto-installs `node_modules` if missing. Expected: succeeds.

2. **`make dev` when `bd daemon` is not running** — `scripts/dev.sh` auto-starts `bd daemon` and records that it did, so cleanup stops it on exit. Expected: no change from today.

3. **Port conflict on `:8080` or `:3000`** — `air` fails immediately with a port-in-use error. `vite` is configured `strictPort: true` so it fails fast rather than silently rebinding. Both cases propagate to the top-level script. Expected: explicit error; developer frees the port and retries. Do not silently fall back to a different port.

4. **`vite dev` fails to start (e.g., corrupt `node_modules`)** — `wait "$AIR_PID" "$VITE_PID"` returns; the `trap cleanup EXIT` kills `air` so the Go server does not linger. Expected: clean exit.

5. **Developer sets `VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080` and `.air.toml` still has `--frontend-url http://localhost:3000`** — Vite dev server runs on `:3000`, frontend bundles absolute URLs to `:8080`, browser makes cross-origin requests from `:3000` → `:8080`, CORS preflight hits Go server, server allows `http://localhost:3000`. Expected: works.

6. **Developer sets `VITE_API_BASE_URL` to something not `:3000` (e.g., `https://my-tunnel.ngrok.io`)** — `.air.toml`'s `--frontend-url http://localhost:3000` does not cover this origin. Expected: CORS fails; developer must override by passing `--frontend-url https://my-tunnel.ngrok.io` to `loom serve` directly (bypassing `air`) or by editing `.air.toml` temporarily. Document the override pattern in the `.env.example` — already present. Not this task's problem.

7. **`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up` without `.28` merged** — the `deploy/server/Dockerfile` path does not exist. Compose fails at build time with a clear `Dockerfile not found` error. Expected: developer notices `.28` has not landed, waits, or sets up the dependency ordering correctly. This is why `.28` is a hard dependency.

8. **`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up` with Redis absent** — without `--profile fleet`, the `redis` service does not start. Server still starts, but any fleet-db code path that tries to reach `redis://localhost:6379` will fail at runtime. Expected: developers who do not test fleet paths are unaffected; developers who do test fleet paths pass `--profile fleet`.

9. **`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --profile fleet` on a host with port `:6379` already bound** — Redis container fails to bind. Compose fails fast. Expected: developer frees the port or changes the host port mapping. Acceptable.

10. **`make dev-loom` invoked by an in-flight script** — prints "deprecated, use `make dev`" to stderr then forwards to `./scripts/dev.sh`. The developer's script gets the new behavior (two processes, :8080 + :3000) instead of the old (one process, :8080). This is a **behavior change** that will break any script that assumed `:8080` serves the UI. Flag prominently in the PR description.

11. **`make dev-vite` invoked on a CI runner without air installed** — `dev-check` fails with "air not found. Install: go install github.com/air-verse/air@latest". Same as today. No regression.

12. **Developer runs `make dev` but then kills only the Vite process (Ctrl-C in the Vite pane of a multiplexer)** — `scripts/dev.sh` uses `wait "$AIR_PID" "$VITE_PID" 2>/dev/null` which returns when either exits, then the trap kills the survivor. Expected: clean full shutdown. This is today's behavior — no regression.

13. **Fresh checkout with no `dist/`** — `scripts/dev.sh` does NOT try to build `dist/`. Good — `dist/` is no longer needed for dev (Vite serves from source). Even `check-deps` should not touch dist. Expected: works from a clean `git clean -fdx`.

14. **`.air.toml` parsed by an old version of `air`** — `air` versions before v1.40 may not recognize trailing arguments after `--no-daemon`. We verify the pinned air version in the install hint (`go install github.com/air-verse/air@latest` — latest is safe). If a developer is on an older pinned version, they get a clear flag-parse error from `air`. Not this task's concern.

15. **`deploy/server/Dockerfile` entrypoint uses `--frontend-url http://localhost`** (from `.28`'s default) — overridden by `docker-compose.dev.yml`'s `environment: LOOM_FRONTEND_URL: "http://localhost:3000"`. Environment variable takes precedence over the hardcoded default? No — `LOOM_FRONTEND_URL` is only read as the *default value* of `--frontend-url` when the flag is absent. The compose file passes the env var but does not override the `CMD` in the Dockerfile, which still has `--frontend-url http://localhost` as an explicit arg. **Fix**: in `docker-compose.dev.yml`, override the `command:` field to `["serve", "--port", "8080", "--frontend-url", "http://localhost:3000"]`. Document this in the compose file comment.

16. **`docker-compose.dev.yml` rebuilds slowly because `deploy/frontend/Dockerfile` does `npm ci` from scratch** — expected; this is a smoke-test, not an interactive dev loop. Note in the compose file header.

17. **`docker-compose.dev.yml` on macOS with port 6379 bound by a native Redis (via Homebrew)** — same as edge case 9. Developer chooses one.

18. **`make dev` when `pre-push` hook is not yet installed** — `dev: dev-check .git/hooks/pre-push` still has the hook prerequisite. `make hooks` installs it. Expected: no change.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Testing Strategy

### Unit tests to update

**`makefile_test.go:TestMakeDryRun_Dev`** — update the assertion from the old script path to `./scripts/dev.sh`. One-line change plus doc comment.

title: Phase 2: Move events/otelexport to infra layer (keep events/ in sdk)
description: events/ (parent) stays in sdk — stdlib only, pure event types. events/otelexport/ moves to infra classification — it imports 13 external OTel SDK packages (otlpmetrichttp, otlptracehttp, sdk/metric, sdk/trace, etc.). No file move needed. Update depguard rules to classify events/otelexport under infra-isolation (must not import webui/cli). This keeps loom-sdk dependency-light — consumers who just want types don't pull in OTel. Plan: /Users/tyson/.claude/plans/purrfect-weaving-stream.md
design:
## Summary

Classify \`internal/events/otelexport\` as infra-layer in depguard linter rules, enforcing that it must not import \`webui\` or \`cli\` packages. The \`events/\` parent package remains SDK-layer (stdlib only, pure event types). This is a **preventive gate** — \`events/otelexport\` already respects the boundary today (imports only \`internal/events\` + external OTel SDK packages). The rule prevents future regressions that would drag heavy OTel SDK dependencies into the wrong layer.

No file moves or code changes are needed. The only change is to \`.golangci.yml\`.

## Technical Approach

Add a depguard rule to \`.golangci.yml\` that targets files in \`internal/events/otelexport/\` and denies imports of \`webui\` and \`cli\` packages.

**Coordination with loomcli-rir82.1 (depguard boundary rules):**
The sibling task .1 designs a comprehensive set of 3 boundary rules (\`sdk-boundary\`, \`infra-boundary\`, \`web-boundary\`). Its \`infra-boundary\` rule already includes \`**/internal/events/otelexport/**\` in the files list. If .1 has already been implemented when this task runs:
- **Verify** that \`events/otelexport\` appears in the \`infra-boundary\` rule's \`files\` list
- **Verify** that \`events/otelexport\` does NOT appear in the \`sdk-boundary\` rule's \`files\` list
- **Done** — no additional changes needed

If .1 has NOT been implemented yet (the \`infra-boundary\` rule doesn't exist in \`.golangci.yml\`):
- Add a targeted \`otelexport-infra-isolation\` rule that blocks \`events/otelexport\` from importing webui or cli
- This rule will be superseded by .1's broader \`infra-boundary\` rule when .1 lands. The implementation agent for .1 should remove this targeted rule and absorb it into \`infra-boundary\`.

**Rule definition (if .1 hasn't landed):**
\`\`\`yaml
otelexport-infra-isolation:
  list-mode: lax
  files:
    - "**/internal/events/otelexport/**"
  deny:
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui
      desc: "Infra-layer (events/otelexport) must not import web; dependency direction: sdk → infra → web → cli"
    - pkg: github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli
      desc: "Infra-layer (events/otelexport) must not import cli; dependency direction: sdk → infra → web → cli"
\`\`\`

**Why not also restrict events/otelexport from importing other infra packages?**
The task scope is infra-isolation (must not import webui/cli). events/otelexport currently only imports \`internal/events\` (sdk-layer). Future imports of other infra packages (e.g., \`rpc\`, \`sessions\`) would be valid for an infra-layer package. Over-restricting would create false positives.

**Why a separate rule instead of adding to existing \`handler-layer-isolation\`?**
Different scope — \`handler-layer-isolation\` targets handler files within webui. The otelexport rule targets a completely different package with different boundary concerns.

## Conventions Established

- **Targeted depguard rule naming**: When a task adds a depguard rule ahead of a broader boundary task (like .1), name it \`<package>-<boundary>-isolation\` (e.g., \`otelexport-infra-isolation\`) so it's clearly a subset of the eventual boundary rule and easy to find/remove.
- **Conditional implementation pattern**: Check if a broader rule from a sibling task exists before adding a narrow one. Prefer verifying existing rules over creating duplicates.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### \`.golangci.yml\`
**If .1's \`infra-boundary\` rule already exists:**
- No changes needed — verify that \`**/internal/events/otelexport/**\` is in its \`files\` list.

**If .1's rules do NOT exist yet:**
- Add the \`otelexport-infra-isolation\` rule under \`linters.settings.depguard.rules\` (alongside the existing \`handler-layer-isolation\` rule).

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **\`internal/cli/daemon_config.go\` — \`OTelDaemonConfig\` struct duplication**: The cli layer defines \`OTelDaemonConfig\` with the same fields as \`otelexport.Config\`. This duplication is intentional — it avoids making \`daemon_config.go\` import the \`otelexport\` package (which would transitively pull 11 OTel SDK packages into every file that imports daemon config). The field-by-field copy in \`initOTelExporter\` is the correct pattern. Not a cleanup target.
- **Other infra packages' depguard rules** — Handled by loomcli-rir82.1 (the full boundary rule set).
- **SDK-layer rule for \`events/*.go\` (root)** — Also handled by loomcli-rir82.1. The events parent already imports nothing internal; the sdk-boundary rule will formalize this.

## Dependencies

- **No external packages needed**
- **No code changes required in any Go source files**
- **Soft dependency on loomcli-rir82.1**: If .1 has landed, this task reduces to verification only. If not, a standalone rule is added. Either way, the task is independently implementable.
- **golangci-lint v2** (already installed, version 2.9.0)
- **depguard linter** (already enabled in \`.golangci.yml\`)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Merge conflict with .1**: If both .1 and .3 are implemented on separate branches and both modify the \`depguard.rules\` section of \`.golangci.yml\`, there will be a merge conflict. **Expected behavior**: The merge resolver should keep .1's broader rules and drop .3's narrow rule if .1 fully subsumes it. If .3 lands first, .1's implementer should notice the narrow rule and absorb it.

2. **Test files**: depguard rules apply to test files (\`_test.go\`). The test files in \`events/otelexport/\` import \`internal/events\` and OTel SDK test packages — all allowed. They do NOT import webui or cli. No false positives.

3. **golangci-lint glob matching for \`**/internal/events/otelexport/**\`**: This glob matches all files in the \`otelexport/\` directory recursively. Since there are no sub-packages under otelexport, this is equivalent to \`**/internal/events/otelexport/*.go\`, but the recursive glob is future-proof. If someone adds a sub-package under otelexport, it would also be classified as infra (correct behavior).

4. **No-op when rule is already present**: If the implementation agent finds that .1's rules exist and \`events/otelexport\` is already classified, the entire task is a verification. The implementation agent should still: (a) run \`golangci-lint run ./internal/events/otelexport/...\` to confirm zero violations, (b) check that the package is NOT in the sdk-boundary files list.

design:
## Summary

Split `internal/cli/` (153 non-test Go source files, 155 test files) into **13 sub-packages plus root**, bringing every package under the 25-file hard limit. This revision addresses two major issues from the previous design: (1) daemon/ was 29+ files exceeding the limit, and (2) root remainder was 56 unmatched files, not ~25 as claimed.

The split uses Go's **composition-root pattern**: the root package (`cli/`) retains shared infrastructure (25 files), sub-packages import root for shared types and export their Cobra commands, and `cmd/loom/main.go` triggers sub-package registration via blank imports. `cli/config/` is a **true leaf** (zero imports of cli root) — it holds only type definitions and loading functions, never Cobra commands.

## Technical Approach

### Pattern: Composition Root with init() Registration

**Current state:** All 153 files share `package cli` and use package-level singletons (`defaultDeps`, `trackerInst`, `rootCmd`). Cobra commands register via `rootCmd.AddCommand()` in `init()` functions scattered across files.

**After split:**
1. `internal/cli/` (root) retains shared infrastructure: Deps, Backend interface/registry, lock management, issue backend singletons, fleet mode detection, worktree resolution, daemon runtime detection, config command registration.
2. `internal/cli/config/` is a **true leaf** — it holds type definitions (LoomConfig, DaemonConfig, AgentEntry, RoleConfig, Checkpoint, SecretBackend), config loading functions (LoadConfig, LoadDaemonConfig), validation, and secret resolution. It imports **only** external packages (atomicfile, configlock, yaml, backend, lockfile) — never cli root.
3. Each sub-package registers Cobra commands via `init()`:
   ```go
   // cli/daemon/cmd.go
   package daemon
   import "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli"
   func init() { cli.RegisterCommand(NewDaemonCmd()) }
   ```
4. `cmd/loom/main.go` blank-imports all sub-packages to trigger registration.
5. Root exports `RegisterCommand(cmd *cobra.Command)` which appends to a pending slice. `Execute()` calls `rootCmd.AddCommand(pendingCmds...)` before executing.

### Handling `defaultDeps`

36 files currently reference `defaultDeps` directly. After the split:
- `defaultDeps` stays in root as the package-level singleton
- Sub-packages access it via `cli.GetDeps(cmd)` (Cobra context extraction, already used by many files)
- Functions that receive `*Deps` as parameter continue to do so
- `secrets.go` currently falls back to `defaultDeps` when deps is nil — this fallback **must be removed** so secrets.go can live in cli/config/ without importing root. The only caller (`daemon_run_helpers.go`) already provides Deps at construction time.

### Handling cross-package unexported symbols

After the split, functions/types used across the new package boundaries must be **exported** (capitalized). The compiler catches all violations exhaustively — any unexported cross-reference is a compile error. Key examples:
- `runGit()` in cli/git/ → `RunGit()` (called from cli/workspace/, cli/monitor/)
- `collectMonitorData()` in cli/monitor/ → `CollectMonitorData()` (called from cli/serve/)
- `resolveDaemonPath()` in cli/daemon/ → `ResolveDaemonPath()` (called from cli/serve/)
- `filterEnv()`/`FilteredEnv()` in root → already exported or stays in root
- `worktreeCompletion()` in root → `WorktreeCompletion()` (used as Cobra ValidArgsFunction by sub-packages)
- `isFleetMode()` in cli/config/ → `IsFleetMode()` (called from root, daemon, doctor, etc.)
- `LoadDaemonConfig()` in cli/config/ → already exported ✓
- All Checkpoint functions in cli/config/ → already exported ✓

### Import DAG (acyclic — verified)

```
cmd/loom/main.go
  → cli/ (root)
  → cli/config/, cli/migrate/
  → cli/daemon/, cli/serve/, cli/agent/, cli/automode/, cli/backends/,
    cli/monitor/, cli/hooks/, cli/cleanup/, cli/git/, cli/workspace/, cli/doctor/

cli/ (root) → cli/config/

cli/config/    → (external only: atomicfile, configlock, yaml, backend, lockfile) — TRUE LEAF
cli/migrate/   → cli/, cli/config/

cli/daemon/    → cli/, cli/config/
cli/serve/     → cli/, cli/config/, cli/daemon/ (for resolveDaemonPath)
cli/agent/     → cli/, cli/config/
cli/automode/  → cli/, cli/config/
cli/backends/  → cli/
cli/monitor/   → cli/, cli/config/, cli/git/
cli/hooks/     → cli/, cli/config/
cli/cleanup/   → cli/, cli/config/
cli/git/       → cli/, cli/config/
cli/workspace/ → cli/, cli/config/, cli/git/
cli/doctor/    → cli/, cli/config/
```

**No cycles.** cli/config/ is a true leaf within the cli hierarchy. Root imports only cli/config/. All other sub-packages import root and/or cli/config/ but never each other in a circular way. cli/serve/ → cli/daemon/ is one-directional (daemon never imports serve). cli/workspace/ → cli/git/ is one-directional (git never imports workspace). cli/monitor/ → cli/git/ is one-directional.

### Key architectural decisions

1. **cli/config/ is a true leaf** — Config types (LoomConfig, DaemonConfig, AgentEntry, RoleConfig), config loading (LoadConfig, LoadDaemonConfig), validation, secrets, and checkpoint types live here. Cobra command registration files (config_cmd.go, migrate_cmd.go) do NOT go here because they reference rootCmd, which would create a cycle. config_cmd.go stays in root; migrate_cmd.go goes to cli/migrate/.

2. **daemon/ solved by extracting config + moving IPC client + ensure functions** — The original 29 daemon_* files + daemon.go + concurrency.go = 31 exceeded the limit. Solution: move 4 config-related files (daemon_config.go, daemon_config_display.go, daemon_queue.go, daemon_repos.go) to cli/config/, move daemon_ipc_client.go to root (used by root's ipc_issue_backend.go), move daemon_ensure.go to root (used by serve/ and workspace/). Daemon keeps all 16 files with Daemon receiver methods + 9 other daemon-specific files = 25.

3. **backend.go (registry) stays in root** — deps.go references RegisterBackend, SetBackend, InvokeAgent, etc. directly. Sub-packages in cli/backends/ register themselves via init() calling cli.RegisterBackend().

4. **process_guard.go → cli/backends/** — Used exclusively by backend_claude.go, backend_codex.go, backend_external.go, backend_opencode.go. Not daemon-related.

5. **issue_text.go → cli/agent/** — Only consumed by recover_helpers.go (also in agent/).

6. **checkpoint.go → cli/config/** — Pure data struct with only stdlib imports. Used by both agent/ and daemon/ — both import config/.

## Conventions Established

- **Package naming:** Sub-packages use short, descriptive names: `daemon`, `serve`, `config`, `migrate`, `agent`, `git`, `workspace`, `doctor`, `hooks`, `cleanup`, `automode`, `backends`, `monitor`
- **Command export pattern:** Each sub-package with Cobra commands exports `NewXxxCmd() *cobra.Command` and registers via `init() { cli.RegisterCommand(NewXxxCmd()) }`
- **Root registration API:** `cli.RegisterCommand(cmd)` appends to a pending list; `Execute()` adds them all to rootCmd before running
- **Backend registration:** Sub-packages call `cli.RegisterBackend(b)` in init()
- **Deps passing:** Sub-packages always receive Deps via `cli.GetDeps(cmd)` or explicit parameter — never reference `cli.defaultDeps` directly
- **Config access:** All sub-packages import `cli/config` for configuration types, not root
- **File renaming in config/:** daemon_config.go→project.go, daemon_config_display.go→display.go, daemon_queue.go→queue.go, daemon_repos.go→repos.go
- **Leaf invariant:** cli/config/ MUST NOT import cli/ root. All Cobra command files stay outside config/.

## Files to Create

### `internal/cli/register.go`
New file in root (~15 lines). Exports `RegisterCommand(cmd *cobra.Command)` and an internal `pendingCmds` slice. Called by sub-package `init()` functions. `Execute()` calls `registerPendingCommands()` which does `rootCmd.AddCommand(pendingCmds...)`.

### Sub-package directories (13 new directories)
Each directory contains moved/renamed files from cli root:
- `internal/cli/config/` — type definitions, loading, validation, secrets, checkpoint
- `internal/cli/daemon/` — daemon supervisor, IPC server, lifecycle, control
- `internal/cli/serve/` — loom serve, server wiring, ops implementations, worker, logging
- `internal/cli/migrate/` — fleet migration command and implementation
- `internal/cli/agent/` — plan, task, agent commands, prompts, recovery
- `internal/cli/automode/` — automode loop, poller, tmux, event emission
- `internal/cli/backends/` — backend implementations, process guard
- `internal/cli/monitor/` — monitor dashboard, data collection, display
- `internal/cli/hooks/` — hook types, parsing, dispatch, installation
- `internal/cli/cleanup/` — cleanup events, sessions, usage commands
- `internal/cli/git/` — git operations, push, pull, merge, PR, sync, reset, conflicts
- `internal/cli/workspace/` — workspace commands, init, setup, worktree management, status
- `internal/cli/doctor/` — doctor checks, stale detection, fleetdb diagnostics

### `internal/cli/agent/prompts/`
Move the `prompts/` embedded .md files directory alongside prompts.go. The `//go:embed prompts/*.md` directive uses relative paths and must stay adjacent to its source file.

## Files to Modify

### `cmd/loom/main.go`
Add blank imports for all 13 sub-packages plus config:
```go
import (
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/agent"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/automode"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/backends"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/cleanup"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/daemon"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/doctor"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/git"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/hooks"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/migrate"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/monitor"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/serve"
    _ "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli/workspace"
)
```
(config/ has no init() registration — it is a pure-type leaf.)

### Unexported symbols that cross new boundaries must be exported

- `collectMonitorData()` in cli/monitor/ → `CollectMonitorData()` (called from serve/)

### Minor refactoring: Remove defaultDeps fallback from secrets.go

```

```

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

1. **cli/data/ package (thin HTTP client commands)** — Tracked by loomcli-rir82.24. Depends on OpenAPI Go client generation (.21) and HTTP endpoint additions (.22, .23). This task splits existing files; .24 creates new thin-client replacements.

2. **Depguard rule updates** — After the split, depguard rules (loomcli-rir82.1) may need updated file globs to match the new sub-package paths. Coordinate when both land.

3. **cli/httpclient/ already exists** — 4 files (client.go, device_flow.go, token_cache.go, client_test.go). Already a sub-package. No changes needed from this task.

4. **testdata/ directory** — Contains test fixtures. Stays in root for integration tests.

5. **sessions/ directory** — Contains session log data files (not Go code). Stays in root.

## Dependencies

- **No external packages needed** — purely internal reorganization
- **Depends on loomcli-rir82.2 (ops migration)** being completed first ✓ (already done). After .2 landed, `gitops_impl.go` and `backendops_impl.go` import `ops` instead of `webui`. This simplifies the serve/ sub-package imports.
- **Blocks loomcli-rir82.9 (check-package-size.sh)** and **.10 (check-import-fanout.sh)** — Those linters enforce limits this task achieves.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **init() ordering:** Go guarantees init() functions within a package run in source-file order, but cross-package init() order follows import dependency order. Since sub-packages don't import each other cyclically, their init() registration order is determined by blank-import order in main.go. Cobra command ordering is unaffected — Cobra sorts help output alphabetically. **Expected behavior:** All commands appear in `loom --help` in the same groups as before.

2. **Test file circular imports:** Test files in root (`package cli`) can access unexported root symbols. Test files in sub-packages (`package daemon`) can access unexported symbols in their sub-package only. Tests that exercise cross-package interactions MUST stay in root. 25 E2E/integration/smoke test files stay in root, ~130 unit test files move with their source.

3. **Build tag files:** `signal_dir_unix.go` (build tag `!windows`) and `signal_dir_windows.go` stay in root. They are only used by lock.go (also in root).

4. **Embedded prompts directory:** `prompts.go` uses `//go:embed prompts/*.md`. After moving prompts.go to cli/agent/, the `prompts/` directory must also move to `cli/agent/prompts/`. The embed directive's relative path remains unchanged. **Expected behavior:** `//go:embed prompts/*.md` in agent/prompts.go resolves to agent/prompts/*.md. If the build fails, the implementation agent must verify the directory was moved.

5. **Package-level var initialization order:** `defaultDeps` in root calls `DefaultDeps()` which calls `resolveIssueBackendType()` and `newCliBeadsAdapter()` — all in root. No change. `LoadDaemonConfig()` moves to config/ but is called by daemon/ and serve/ at runtime, not at init time. **Expected behavior:** No initialization order issues.

6. **Cobra PersistentPreRunE inheritance:** Set on rootCmd in root. Sub-package commands are children of rootCmd via RegisterCommand/AddCommand. PersistentPreRunE inheritance travels the command tree regardless of which Go package defined the command. **Expected behavior:** All commands receive Deps injection via context.

7. **defaultDeps references in test files:** ~36 source files reference defaultDeps, and many test files do too. Test files that move to sub-packages and reference defaultDeps need refactoring to use `cli.GetDeps(nil)` or create test-local Deps. The compiler catches these exhaustively. **Expected behavior:** All test files compile. Implementation agent must grep `defaultDeps` across ALL test files in each sub-package.

8. **Concurrent daemon access:** The daemon uses mutex-protected shared state (agents map, reconcile lock). All daemon files with Daemon methods stay in cli/daemon/. Unexported mutex fields remain accessible within the package. **Expected behavior:** No behavioral change to daemon concurrency.

9. **LoomConfig type references in root:** worktree_resolve.go (in root) references `LoomConfig` which moves to cli/config/. After the move, root imports cli/config/ and references `config.LoomConfig`. Use an import alias if needed: `import cfgpkg "...cli/config"`. **Expected behavior:** Compile succeeds; type usage is unchanged.

10. **secrets.go defaultDeps removal:** After removing the `defaultDeps` fallback, if any code path calls `Resolve()` on a `OnePasswordBackend` with nil deps, it will get an explicit error instead of silently using the global singleton. **Expected behavior:** No runtime change (the only caller provides deps), but future nil-deps bugs are caught early.

11. **daemon_queue.go references to daemon_config types:** daemon_queue.go uses `DaemonConfig`, `AgentEntry`, `RoleConfig`, `LoadDaemonConfig`, `mergeRoleConfig`. After the split, these types are in cli/config/. daemon_queue.go moves to cli/daemon/ and imports cli/config/ for these types. **Expected behavior:** Clean compilation. daemon/ already imports config/ for other types.

12. **serve/ cross-package calls:** serve_observability.go calls `resolveDaemonPath()` from daemon_state.go (now in cli/daemon/). serve_workspace.go calls `ensureDaemonForWorkspace()` from workspace_init.go (now in cli/workspace/). Both must be exported. serve/ imports both daemon/ and workspace/. This is legal — the DAG remains acyclic (neither daemon nor workspace imports serve). **Expected behavior:** serve_observability.go calls `daemon.ResolveDaemonPath()`. serve_workspace.go calls either `cli.EnsureDaemonForWorkspace()` (since daemon_ensure.go is in root) or `workspace.EnsureDaemonForWorkspace()` depending on final placement. Since daemon_ensure.go is in root, serve/ calls `cli.EnsureDaemonForWorkspace()` — no extra imports needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `go build ./...` succeeds with zero errors
2. `go test ./...` passes — all 155 test files pass (whether in root or sub-packages)
3. `go vet ./...` passes
4. Every Go package under `internal/cli/` has ≤ 25 non-test `.go` files
5. Every Go package under `internal/cli/` has ≤ 10 internal imports (verify with `go list -json ./internal/cli/... | jq '.Imports | map(select(startswith("github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal"))) | length'`)
6. `cli/config/` does NOT import `cli/` (it is a leaf — verify with `go list -json ./internal/cli/config | jq '.Imports | map(select(contains("internal/cli"))) | map(select(. == "github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/cli")) | length'` = 0)
7. No sub-package imports another sub-package in a cycle (the import DAG is acyclic — Go compiler rejects cycles)
8. `cmd/loom/main.go` has blank imports for all 12 command-registering sub-packages
9. `loom --help` displays all commands organized in the same groups as before
10. `make check-go` passes (golangci-lint, go vet, go test, LOC limits)
11. `loom serve`, `loom daemon`, `loom plan`, `loom task`, `loom monitor`, `loom doctor` all work correctly (manual smoke test)
12. The `prompts/` embedded directory is accessible from cli/agent/ (prompt templates render correctly)
13. No files remain in `internal/cli/*.go` root that belong in a sub-package — root has exactly 25 files as listed
14. `secrets.go` in cli/config/ has no reference to `defaultDeps` or any cli/ root import

## Testing Strategy

### Test file migration (~155 test files)

**Unit tests (~130 files) — move with source:**
Each test file moves to the same sub-package as its source file. Example: `daemon_test.go` → cli/daemon/, `config_test.go` → cli/config/, `backend_claude_test.go` → cli/backends/.

Tests that access unexported symbols that now live across a package boundary must be rewritten to use exported APIs. The compiler catches these exhaustively — any unexported cross-reference is a compile error.

**Integration/E2E tests (25 files) — stay in root:**
Tests that exercise cross-package interactions stay in `internal/cli/` root:
- E2E tests: automode_e2e, config_cmd_e2e, daemon_e2e, doctor_e2e, hooks_e2e, init_e2e, plan_task_e2e, recover_e2e, serve_e2e, sessions_cmd_e2e, status_e2e, usage_cmd_e2e, workspace_cmd_e2e
- Smoke tests: daemon_planner_smoke, plan_smoke
- Integration: integration_test, backend_pty_integration, blocker_resolution_parity, session_echo
- Test utilities: testmain, testutil, testutil_helpers, testenv, testenv_echo
- Mocks: mock_issue_backend

Integration tests access sub-package functionality through **exported APIs only**. They test the full command lifecycle via Cobra command execution.

### Verification steps (run in order)

1. `go build ./...` — all packages compile
2. `go vet ./...` — no vet errors
3. `go test ./internal/cli/...` — all tests pass recursively across sub-packages
4. `go test ./...` — full test suite passes
5. `make check-go` — full Go quality gate passes (lint, vet, test, LOC)
6. Manual smoke test: `loom plan --help`, `loom daemon --help`, `loom serve --help`, `loom monitor --help`
7. Verify package sizes: `for d in internal/cli internal/cli/*/; do count=$(find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.go' ! -name '*_test.go' 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$d: $count"; done` — all ≤ 25
8. Verify import fan-out: `go list -json ./internal/cli/... | jq -r '.ImportPath as $pkg | (.Imports // []) | map(select(startswith("github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal"))) | "\($pkg): \(length)"'` — all ≤ 10
9. Verify config/ is a leaf: `go list -json ./internal/cli/config | jq '.Imports[]' | grep internal/cli$` — should produce no output

design:
## Summary

Split the 115-file webui root package into domain-scoped sub-packages plus a 21-file root, bringing every package under the 25-file hard limit. This is a **revision** addressing three feedback items: (1) explicit fleet file package rename work (package webui → package fleet), (2) explicit assignment of three orphaned test files, and (3) explicit acknowledgment that *_module.go files must change their package declarations.

**Pre-requisite note**: Task .2 is marked closed but internal/ops/ does not exist on this branch — GitOps, BackendOps, FileOps interfaces remain in webui root. This design works with the **current code state**: those interface files stay in root. If .2's code lands later, the interface files simply delete from root (no circular dependency impact since no sub-package imports them from root).

## Technical Approach

### The Circular Dependency Problem

The naïve split (move handlers to sub-packages, keep shared utilities in root) creates a cycle: root imports handler sub-packages for module constructors, handler sub-packages import root for respondJSON/respondError.

**Solution — three-layer import DAG:**

```
server/handler  → service/  (shared HTTP utilities, no root import)
service/        → (external only)  (interfaces + result types, no root import)
handlers/*      → server/handler, service/, terminal/ (NO root import)
terminal/       → service/, server/realtime, tabmeta/ (NO root import)
hooks/          → terminal/, coordinator/, daemon/, fleet/ (NO root import)
subscription/   → server/realtime, daemon/ (NO root import)
log/            → server/handler, server/middleware (NO root import)
fleet/ (ext.)   → server/handler, server/middleware (NO root import)
root            → ALL of the above (wiring layer)
```

No sub-package imports root. Root imports all sub-packages. Zero cycles.

### Module Registration: Structural Interface Matching

Each handler sub-package defines its own Module struct with Register(mux *http.ServeMux). This structurally satisfies the webui.Module interface (defined in root's module.go) without importing root. Root's buildModules() imports handler sub-packages and constructs module instances.

**Package declaration changes** (feedback item #3): Every *_module.go file currently declares `package webui`. When moved to a sub-package, each must change its package declaration:
- fleet_module.go: `package webui` → `package fleet`
- issue_module.go: `package webui` → `package issues`
- issue_tab_module.go: `package webui` → `package issues`
- session_module.go: `package webui` → `package issues`
- terminal_module.go: `package webui` → `package terminal` (handlers/terminal/)
- terminal_tab_module.go: `package webui` → `package terminal` (handlers/terminal/)
- git_module.go: `package webui` → `package git`
- file_module.go: `package webui` → `package misc`
- log_module.go: `package webui` → `package log` (the log/ sub-package)
- sse_module.go: `package webui` → `package subscription`
- workspace_ops_module.go: stays `package webui` (remains in root)

Every non-module source file moving to a sub-package must also change its package declaration from `package webui` to the target sub-package name. This is a mechanical find-and-replace on the first line of each file.

### Service Interfaces: Move to service/, Impls Stay Separate

AgentService, TerminalService, DiffService, FileService, SessionService interfaces + their result types move to service/ (alongside existing IssueService, WorkspaceService). This lets handler sub-packages import service types without touching root.

Implementations stay where their dependencies live:
- terminal_service_impl.go + terminal_service_tabs.go → terminal/ (needs TerminalManager, ScrollbackBuffer)
- agent_service_impl.go → root (references types from multiple sub-packages)
- diff_service_impl.go → root (references GitOps which stays in root)
- file_service_impl.go → root (references FileOps which stays in root)
- session_service_impl.go → root (references SessionsStore, sessionhistory)

### Fleet File Migration (Feedback Item #1)

Moving fleet_*.go (8 files, currently `package webui`) into existing webui/fleet/ (currently `package fleet`) requires:

1. **Package declaration change**: Each moved file changes `package webui` → `package fleet` (first line of file).

2. **Unexported symbol resolution**: The fleet_*.go files use unexported webui-root symbols that must be replaced:
   - `respondJSON(w, status, v)` → `handler.WriteJSON(w, status, v)` (import server/handler)
   - `respondError(w, status, msg)` → `handler.WriteJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})`
   - `maxRequestBody` → `handler.MaxRequestBody` (already exported in server/handler)
   - `logger` → `slog.Default()` or accept `*slog.Logger` as constructor parameter

3. **Type visibility**: All exported types in fleet_*.go (FleetRegisterConfig, FleetClaimRequest, FleetClaimResponse, FleetDoneRequest, FleetDoneResponse, HeartbeatRequest, HeartbeatResponse, FleetRateLimiter, FleetModule, TokenConfig, WorkerClaims) keep their names. Unexported types (workerClaimsContextKey, fleetClaimClient, fleetClaimPoolGetter, fleetClaimPoolAdapter, fleetDoneStore, heartbeatStore, workerRegistrar) keep their names — they're package-internal to fleet/ now.

4. **Caller updates**: Root files that reference fleet types must update:
   - server.go: `TokenConfig` → `fleet.TokenConfig`, `FleetRegisterConfig` → `fleet.RegisterConfig` (drop "Fleet" prefix to avoid stutter: `fleet.FleetRegisterConfig` → `fleet.RegisterConfig`)
   - server_config.go: same type updates
   - server_app.go: same type updates
   - server_modules.go: `NewFleetModule(...)` → `fleet.NewFleetModule(...)` (already imports fleet/)

5. **fleetWSHandler extraction**: fleetWSHandler() is defined in routes.go but is fleet-specific. Move it to fleet/ as an exported function FleetWSHandler(). Root's routes.go doesn't call it directly (it's only used in FleetModule.Register), so this is a clean extraction. Update fleet_ws_handler_test.go to test the fleet package function.

6. **jwt.go migration**: jwt.go (TokenConfig, WorkerClaims, GenerateWorkerToken, ValidateWorkerToken) is entirely fleet-specific. It moves to fleet/ with `package fleet`. Since it was already `package webui` and fleet/ already exists, this is a package rename + move.

### Shared HTTP Utilities: Leverage Existing server/handler/

server/handler/ already has WriteJSON (same as respondJSON), ReadJSON, HandleServiceError, MaxRequestBody, MaxListLimit, ParseListOpts. The root's respond.go, handlers.go, handlers_params.go contain duplicates or unexported versions:

- `respondJSON` = `handler.WriteJSON` (same implementation) — delete respond.go, root files switch to handler.WriteJSON
- `respondError` = inline `handler.WriteJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})` — no separate function needed
- `MaxListLimit` = `handler.MaxListLimit` — delete root copy
- `maxRequestBody` = `handler.MaxRequestBody` — delete root copy
- `writeIssuesError` — move to handlers/issues/ as unexported writeIssuesError (only used by issues handlers)
- `IssuesResponse` — move to handlers/issues/ (only used by issues handlers)
- `splitAndTrim` — move to server/handler/ as exported SplitAndTrim (used by handlers/issues/ via handlers_issues_parse.go and the root handlers_params.go's parsers)
- `parseStringParam`, `parseBoolParam`, `parseIntParam`, `parseArrayParam`, `parseDateParams` — move to server/handler/ as exported functions (used by handlers/issues/, handlers/git/, handlers/misc/)

After these moves, respond.go and handlers.go are deleted (empty). handlers_params.go is deleted (content moved to server/handler/).

### Package-Level Logger

log.go (the logger singleton, 8 lines) stays in root. All sub-packages that need logging use slog.Default() or accept *slog.Logger as constructor parameter. The sub-package log/ (log streaming) is distinct from the logger.

### External Callers

cli/daemon_logs_cmd.go imports webui.ReadLastNLines which moves to webui/log. Update import: webui.ReadLastNLines → webuilog.ReadLastNLines (import path webui/log aliased as webuilog to avoid stdlib collision).

## Conventions Established

- **Handler sub-package pattern**: Each handlers/* package exports handler factory functions (HandleXxx(deps) http.HandlerFunc) and a Module struct. Modules satisfy webui.Module structurally (no root import).
- **Shared HTTP utilities**: server/handler/ is the canonical location for WriteJSON, HandleServiceError, parameter parsing, JSON body reading, error mapping. All handler sub-packages import it. Root's respondJSON/respondError are deleted.
- **Service interface location**: All service interfaces live in service/. Implementations live where their dependencies are (root, terminal/, etc.).
- **Export naming**: When moving a handler function from root to a sub-package, capitalize: handleListIssues → HandleListIssues. Internal helpers stay unexported.
- **File renaming**: When moving handlers_issues.go to handlers/issues/, strip the prefix: handlers_issues.go → issues.go. Module files become module.go. Fleet files strip fleet_ prefix: fleet_auth.go → auth.go.
- **Package declaration**: Every moved file changes its package declaration from webui to the target sub-package name. This is non-negotiable — Go requires all files in a directory to share one package name.
- **Fleet type renaming**: Types with "Fleet" prefix drop it when inside the fleet package to avoid stutter: FleetRegisterConfig → RegisterConfig, FleetModule → Module (but FleetClaimResponse etc. keep "Fleet" prefix because they're domain identifiers, not package prefixes).
- **Logger access**: Sub-packages use slog.Default() or accept *slog.Logger. Never import root for the logger.
- **Test organization**: Unit tests move with their source. Integration/E2E/cross-cutting tests stay in root.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Unexported symbols crossing new boundaries**: Every moved handler file currently uses unexported functions from the same package. After the split, cross-package references must be exported. The implementation agent must:
   - Grep for every unexported symbol defined in a moved file
   - Check if it's referenced from a file now in a different package
   - Export it (capitalize) if so, update all call sites

2. **Package-level variables**: logger (in log.go) is used by ~50 files throughout root. It stays in root. Sub-packages use slog.Default() or accept *slog.Logger as a constructor parameter. Do NOT import root for the logger. Abort compilation if any sub-package references the root logger.

6. **WorkspaceOpsModule handler function migration**: WorkspaceOpsModule calls handler functions from 4 different handler sub-packages (issues, workspace, git, misc). Expected: ~8 internal imports (4 handler sub-packages + service + coordinator + daemon + fleet) — within limit.

9. **FleetModule's fleetWSHandler**: fleetWSHandler is defined in routes.go (root) but is fleet-specific. Move it to fleet/ as exported FleetWSHandler(). It uses respondJSON (replace with handler.WriteJSON) and middleware.WorkspaceFromContext (importable from fleet/ without cycle). The fleet_ws_handler_test.go moves with it.

10. **Test file import updates**: ~79 unit test files move with their source. Each needs: package declaration change, import updates for relocated types. ~35 integration/E2E test files stay in root. Root test files that reference types now in sub-packages need import updates (e.g., service.AgentService, terminal.TerminalManager).

11. **handlers_test.go (1963 lines)**: This mega test file primarily tests handlers that move to handlers/issues/ (issue CRUD, ready, blocked, deps, comments) and handlers/git/ (handleBlocked is tested here but defined in handlers_graph.go). Strategy: move to handlers/issues/ since the majority of tests are issue-related. Any test functions that test handlers in other sub-packages must be split out to their respective sub-package test files. The implementation agent should grep for function names in handlers_test.go and match each to its source handler's destination sub-package.

12. **metrics_test.go**: Tests handleMetrics which is in handlers_health.go (moves to handlers/misc/). However, metrics_test.go imports fleet.ClaimMetrics and realtime.Hub — it's a cross-cutting integration test. Keep in root.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `go build ./...` succeeds — zero compile errors
2. `go test ./internal/webui/...` passes — all test files pass recursively across sub-packages
3. Every Go package under internal/webui/ has ≤ 25 non-test .go files (verified by: find <pkg> -maxdepth 1 -name '*.go' ! -name '*_test.go' | wc -l)
4. No circular imports — go build implicitly verifies this

No sub-package under handlers/, terminal/, hooks/, subscription/, log/ imports internal/webui root — verified by: grep -r '"github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui"' internal/webui/handlers/ internal/webui/terminal/ internal/webui/hooks/ internal/webui/subscription/ internal/webui/log/ returns empty

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (~79 files): Move with source
Each test file follows its source to the new sub-package. Package declaration changes from webui to target sub-package. Tests accessing unexported symbols across the new package boundary must be rewritten to use exported APIs.

for d in internal/webui internal/webui/handlers/issues internal/webui/handlers/workspace internal/webui/handlers/terminal internal/webui/handlers/git internal/webui/handlers/misc internal/webui/terminal internal/webui/hooks internal/webui/subscription internal/webui/log internal/webui/fleet internal/webui/service internal/webui/server/handler; do

design:
## Summary

Split `internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/` (currently 82 .ts/.tsx files at directory root, exceeding the upcoming Phase 7 max-15-files-per-directory gate) into 6 domain sub-directories: `terminal/`, `workspace/`, `issues/`, `agents/`, `ui/`, and `common/`. Each sub-dir gets a barrel `index.ts`. The root `src/hooks/index.ts` is preserved as a thin re-export aggregator over the sub-barrels so the dominant `import { ... } from "@/hooks"` call sites do not need to change. Direct file imports (`@/hooks/useFoo`) — which break when files move — are rewritten to point at the sub-barrel (`@/hooks/<domain>`) or new file path. Co-located inline tests (15 files at root) and tests under `hooks/__tests__/` (45 files) are moved into per-subdir `__tests__/` folders alongside their hooks. After this lands, `src/hooks/` will contain only 1 file (the root barrel) plus 6 sub-dirs, each at or below the 15-file limit, unblocking task `loomcli-rir82.11`.

## Technical Approach

**Why 6 sub-dirs and not more / fewer:** The 65 hook files (82 minus 15 inline tests, minus `index.ts`, minus `logTypes.ts`) cluster naturally around the product's domain entities and the UI substrate. The breakdown below was driven by (a) keeping each sub-dir at ≤14 files so future hooks have headroom under the 15-file gate, (b) keeping the import graph acyclic (sub-dirs only depend on `common/` peers, not on each other), and (c) matching the entity language used by the rest of `src/` (`workspace`, `issues`, `agents`, `terminal` already exist as sibling concepts in `components/`, `stores/`, `api/`).

**Why keep the root barrel:** 111 files import from `@/hooks` today, the vast majority via the named-aggregator form `import { useFoo, useBar } from "@/hooks"`, often importing 5+ symbols across 3+ would-be sub-domains in a single statement. Forcing those to split into 3 import statements per call site would multiply churn for zero architectural benefit — `eslint-plugin-boundaries` (task `.12`) treats `hooks` as a single layer in the DAG, not per-domain, so sub-paths gain nothing for boundary enforcement. The root barrel is one file in `src/hooks/`, well under the 15-file gate. Direct `@/hooks/<file>` imports MUST be updated regardless because the file moved, so we update those to the sub-barrel form (`@/hooks/<domain>`) which both compiles after the move and surfaces the new domain organization.

**Why we update internal hook→hook and hook→non-hook imports:** Hooks today use relative paths like `import x from "../api/sse"`. After moving into a subdir, that breaks. We rewrite hook-internal imports to `@/...` alias form (`@/api/sse`, `@/types/session`, `@/stores/issueStore`, `@/utils/focusUtils`, `@/components/BackendSelectorDropdown/backendDefaults`) so depth changes don't cascade. We also rewrite hook→hook relative imports (e.g., `useTaskLogPolling` importing `LogChunk` from `./logTypes`) to use the new sub-barrel path.

**Trade-off — sub-barrel vs no sub-barrel:** Sub-barrels add one file per sub-dir but make `@/hooks/issues` a stable surface and let the root barrel be a clean one-line-per-domain re-export. Worth the file. The task description explicitly requires sub-barrels.

## Conventions Established

This is the first sub-dir split for `src/hooks/`. Conventions to follow (and that future Phase 6 tasks `.7`, `.26`, `.27` should mirror unless they have a stated reason to diverge):

1. **Sub-barrel pattern:** Each sub-dir has `index.ts` re-exporting the same symbols (and types) the root barrel currently exports for that file. Use `export { useFoo } from "./useFoo"; export type { UseFooReturn } from "./useFoo";` form — preserve the value/type distinction the root barrel uses today. No default exports.
2. **Root barrel is a re-aggregator:** `src/hooks/index.ts` becomes a chain of `export * from "./terminal"; export * from "./workspace"; ...`. No direct `./useFoo` references. Keep alphabetized by sub-dir name.
3. **Internal hook imports use `@/...` aliases, not relative paths:** When moving a hook, replace any `../api/...`, `../stores/...`, `../types/...`, `../utils/...`, `../components/...` imports with their `@/api/...`, `@/stores/...`, etc. equivalents. Reason: depth-independent so future moves don't cascade.
4. **Hook→hook references go through the sub-barrel of the target domain:** `useTaskLogPolling` importing from sibling `logTypes` becomes `from "./logTypes"` (same dir, fine), but if a hook in `agents/` needs a hook in `common/`, it imports `from "@/hooks/common"` (sub-barrel), not `from "../common/useFoo"`.
5. **Test co-location:** Each sub-dir has its own `__tests__/` folder containing the tests for its hooks. No tests at sub-dir root (i.e., no `terminal/useTerminalFont.test.ts` next to `terminal/useTerminalFont.ts`) — uniformly use `__tests__/` so the `check-dir-size.mjs` exclusion (which excludes only `__tests__`, not files matching `*.test.*`) works without surprises. This unifies the two patterns currently in use (15 inline tests at root + 45 in `hooks/__tests__/`).
6. **`logTypes.ts` (a non-hook types file) stays in the sub-dir whose hooks consume it** (`terminal/`, since `useTaskLogPolling` and `useAgentTerminalLogs` are the only consumers). It is NOT promoted to `@/types/`. Reason: it's a private contract between two hooks; promoting it would expand the public surface unnecessarily.

## Files to Create

All paths relative to `internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/`.

### Sub-directories with barrel
- `terminal/index.ts` — re-exports for the 10 terminal/session hooks + `logTypes` types
- `workspace/index.ts` — re-exports for the 12 workspace hooks
- `issues/index.ts` — re-exports for the 14 issue hooks
- `agents/index.ts` — re-exports for the 5 agent observability hooks
- `ui/index.ts` — re-exports for the 12 UI substrate hooks
- `common/index.ts` — re-exports for the 12 utility hooks

### `__tests__` directories (one per sub-dir)
- `terminal/__tests__/` (8 test files end up here)
- `workspace/__tests__/` (11 test files)
- `issues/__tests__/` (14 test files)

### Frontend source files (intra-hook updates)

When each hook is moved, its own internal imports must be rewritten to `@/...` alias form. Files affected (from grep of `from "../"` inside `src/hooks/`):

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- `src/components/TerminalView/` (41 files), `src/components/IssueDetailPanel/` (33 files): same Phase 6 dir-size pattern, owned by **task `loomcli-rir82.7`**.
- `src/api/` (34 files): same pattern, originally task `loomcli-rir82.8` — closed because Phase 4 OpenAPI generation (`.15`–`.18`) is replacing the hand-written client. Not in scope here.
- `src/types/` (20 files): owned by **task `loomcli-rir82.26`**.
- `src/components/WorkspaceTree/` (16 files): owned by **task `loomcli-rir82.27`**.
- Repo-wide grep (`find src -type d ... files > 15`) confirmed there are NO other directories above the limit. The neighborhood scan has full coverage; no orphan dirs.
- Promoting `logTypes.ts` to `@/types/`: declined intentionally (see Convention #6). If a future task wants to share log types broadly, it can promote then.
- `eslint-plugin-boundaries` per-domain layer rules: out of scope. Task `.12` keeps `hooks` as a single layer.

## Dependencies

- **External:** none — no new packages.
- **Internal:** 
  - Depends on `loomcli-rir82.20` (Phase 5 frontend decoupling) — already CLOSED, satisfied.
  - Depends on `loomcli-rir82` epic — open umbrella, no blocking.
- **Blocks:** `loomcli-rir82.11` (`check-dir-size.mjs`) and `loomcli-rir82.12` (`eslint-plugin-boundaries`). Neither runs until this lands.
- **No task ordering constraints** with sibling Phase 6 tasks `.7`, `.26`, `.27` — they touch disjoint directories and can land in any order. They MUST follow the conventions established here (sub-barrel pattern, `__tests__/` co-location, `@/`-alias internal imports).

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **A hook is imported only via a re-export from the root barrel and the implementer forgets to re-export it from the sub-barrel.** Result: typecheck fails at every caller. Behavior: implementer must run `npm run build` (or `tsc --noEmit`) after the barrel rewrite and fix any missing exports before proceeding. Acceptance: `npm run build` passes.
- **A direct file import like `@/hooks/useFoo` is missed by the rewrite step.** Result: TS module-not-found error. Behavior: rely on `tsc --noEmit` to surface — do NOT add a fallback re-export shim at the old path. The error is the desired feedback. Acceptance: `grep -rE 'from .[\"\x27]@/hooks/use' src/` returns ZERO matches after the task (only `@/hooks` and `@/hooks/<domain>` forms permitted).
- **A test file's relative import (`../useFoo` or `../../api/foo`) becomes wrong after the move.** Behavior: rewrite ALL test imports to either `../useFoo` (intra-sub-dir, after the test moves into `<domain>/__tests__/`) or `@/...` alias form (any cross-dir reference). Acceptance: `npm run test:unit` passes with no module-resolution errors.
- **A hook in one sub-dir needs to call a hook in a different sub-dir** (e.g., `useEventProvider` in `common/` is consumed by hooks in `agents/`). Behavior: import via the sub-barrel — `import { useEventContext } from "@/hooks/common"`. Do NOT use a relative path like `../common/useEventProvider`. Reason: keeps the import graph readable and decouples sub-dirs from each other's file layout.
- **Cyclic sub-barrel risk.** If two sub-dirs `A` and `B` import each other's sub-barrels, TS may resolve fine but hot-reload and tree-shaking degrade. Behavior: the implementer must verify acyclic-ness with `madge --circular src/hooks/` (or equivalent). Expected outcome: `common/` is depended on by everything; nothing depends on `common/`. No cycles. If a cycle is detected, abort and add a comment to the task — do NOT silently break the layering. The current categorization was designed to avoid cycles (only `common/` is a sink; the four entity sub-dirs do not import each other) but the implementer must verify.
- **`useGraphData` placement debate.** It's named "graph" but consumed by `IssueDetailPanel`/`MonitorDashboard` for blocked-issue visualization. Categorized under `ui/` (alongside `useAutoLayout`) because its responsibility is React Flow node/edge construction, not issue data fetching. If the implementer disagrees, a single move to `issues/` is acceptable AS LONG AS `issues/` does not exceed 14 file slots — meaning one of the recent-* hooks must move out to `common/` to make room. Default: keep in `ui/`.
- **`logTypes.ts` is not a hook but lives in `hooks/`.** Stays in `terminal/` because that's where its only consumers live. Re-exported via `terminal/index.ts` so callers like `LogViewer.tsx` can import via `@/hooks/terminal`. Do NOT promote to `src/types/`.
- **`hooks/__tests__/__tests__/` accidentally created.** Trivial double-nesting if the implementer drags the wrong directory. Behavior: verify after each batch with `find src/hooks -name __tests__ -type d` — should yield exactly 6 paths (one per sub-dir).
- **`vitest` discovery:** vitest's default glob `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` finds tests in any depth — no config change needed. Acceptance: test count before and after the move must match.
- **Run after every batch, not at the end.** The implementer should split the migration into 6 batches (one per sub-dir) and run `npm run build && npm run test:unit` after each batch. Reason: a 65-file move done in one shot will produce hundreds of typecheck errors that are hard to attribute. After each domain, verify green, commit, then move on. (Commits are local — do not push.)
- **Hook grep in caller files must be `from "@/hooks/[a-zA-Z]"`** not just `@/hooks` — the latter matches both the root-barrel form (which we keep) and the direct-file form (which we replace). Use the character-class anchored regex.

## Acceptance Criteria

Verifiable from outside the implementation, ordered by test method:

**Filesystem shape:**
1. `src/hooks/` contains exactly 1 file (`index.ts`) and 6 sub-directories (`agents/`, `common/`, `issues/`, `terminal/`, `ui/`, `workspace/`).
2. Each sub-directory contains an `index.ts` barrel and a `__tests__/` folder.
3. Each sub-directory's non-`__tests__` file count (counted by the criteria of Phase 7's `check-dir-size.mjs`: `.ts`/`.tsx` files at depth 1, excluding `__tests__`) is ≤ 15.
4. `src/hooks/__tests__/` (the old shared tests directory) is deleted — every test file has been moved into its domain `__tests__/`.
5. There are no inline `.test.ts` files at any sub-dir's root — all tests live under `__tests__/` for that sub-dir.
6. `src/hooks/logTypes.ts` no longer exists at the root; it lives at `src/hooks/terminal/logTypes.ts`.

**Build & test:**
7. `npm run build` (TypeScript compile) passes with zero errors.
8. `npm run test:unit` (vitest) passes. Test count is identical to before the move (no tests dropped).
9. `npm run lint` passes (no new warnings about unused exports from sub-barrels — the eslint config update covers them).
10. `npm run check:arch` passes — no LOC-allowlist failures (the allowlist update covers the moved entries).

**Import surface:**
11. `grep -rE 'from .[\"\x27]@/hooks/use' internal/webui/frontend/src/` returns 0 hits. (No direct file imports remain — must go through sub-barrel.)
12. `grep -rE 'from .[\"\x27]@/hooks/logTypes' internal/webui/frontend/src/` returns 0 hits.
13. `import { ... } from "@/hooks"` (root barrel form) still works for every existing call site — verified by criterion #7.
14. `grep -rE 'from .[\"\x27]\.\./' internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/[a-z]*/` (relative-up imports inside any sub-dir, excluding `__tests__/`) returns 0 hits — sub-dir hook files use only `@/...` alias imports or same-dir relative imports.

**Negative cases:**
15. NO new file may be added to `src/hooks/<domain>/` outside the destination map. (i.e., the implementer must not invent helper files during the move.)
16. NO sub-dir other than `terminal/` may contain `logTypes.ts`.
17. The root `src/hooks/index.ts` MUST NOT contain any `from "./useFoo"` references (no leftover direct file references). It should be 6 `export * from "./<sub-dir>"` lines plus an optional header comment.
18. The root `src/hooks/index.ts` MUST exist and MUST re-export every symbol the old root barrel exported (verified transitively by criterion #7).
19. NO file may be deleted from any caller in `src/components/`, `src/views/`, `src/contexts/`, `src/router.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/TestFixtures.tsx` — only their import statements change.

## Testing Strategy

**Automated:**
- `npm run build` after each per-sub-dir batch and at the end. This is the primary correctness verifier.
- `npm run test:unit` after each batch. Test count must stay the same; no skipped tests; no new failures. Run in CI form (`vitest run`, not watch).
- `npm run lint` once at the end.
- `npm run check:arch` once at the end (verifies LOC allowlist update is correct).
- Manual `find src/hooks -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' \) ! -path '*/__tests__/*' | awk -F/ '{print $4}' | sort | uniq -c` — verify the per-sub-dir file count matches the destination map (12, 13, 15, 6, 13, 13).
- Manual `madge --circular internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/` (if `madge` available, otherwise skip) — verify acyclic.

**Manual UI verification:**
- Boot the dev server (`npm run dev` in `internal/webui/frontend/`) and load the workspace view. Confirm: workspace tree renders, an issue can be selected and the IssueDetailPanel opens, the agent panel renders (the most hook-heavy component), the terminal view connects, the toast/keyboard cheatsheet (`?`) overlays work. These are the highest-fan-in hook consumers; if they all render correctly, the barrel re-aggregation is sound.
- Toggle theme (`useTheme`), change a backend (`useBackendConfig`), open the terminal font picker (`useTerminalFont`) — these touch hooks from 3 different sub-dirs through the SettingsView call site, exercising the cross-sub-dir re-export path.

**Suggested batch order** (lowest blast radius first, smallest sub-dir first):
1. `agents/` (5 hooks, 3 tests) — fewest callers
2. `terminal/` (10 hooks + `logTypes.ts`, 8 tests)
3. `ui/` (12 hooks, 11 tests)
4. `common/` (12 hooks, 13 tests)
5. `workspace/` (12 hooks, 11 tests)
6. `issues/` (14 hooks, 14 tests) — largest, last

After each batch: rewrite the relevant section of `src/hooks/index.ts` (replace direct re-exports for that domain with `export * from "./<sub-dir>"`), update direct-file callers for hooks in that batch, run build + tests, commit. The root barrel evolves incrementally so no batch leaves the build broken.
