description: After the default groupBy flip to "epic", selecting "none" in FilterBar/MoreFiltersMenu is a no-op: setGroupBy("none") writes undefined to URL, parseFromSearchParams returns undefined, App.tsx fallback filters.groupBy ?? DEFAULT_GROUP_BY coerces back to "epic". The SwimLaneBoard flat-view branch (groupBy === "none") becomes unreachable through the UI. Fix: either persist "none" to URL explicitly (drop the !== "none" clause in toQueryString/setGroupBy), or remove "none" from the groupBy option set.
design:
## Summary

The groupBy \"none\" option (flat view / no swim lanes) is unreachable through the UI. When a user selects \"All\" (value=\"none\") in the MoreFiltersMenu dropdown, \`setGroupBy(\"none\")\` converts the value to \`undefined\`, which deletes the \`groupBy\` URL param. On the next parse cycle, \`parseFromSearchParams\` returns \`undefined\`, and \`App.tsx\`'s fallback \`filters.groupBy ?? DEFAULT_GROUP_BY\` coerces it back to \"epic\". The dropdown snaps back to \"Epic\" and the flat view never renders.

The fix is to stop treating \"none\" as equivalent to \"clear\". \"none\" is a valid, explicit groupBy selection that must be persisted in the URL as \`?groupBy=none\`. Only the actual default (\"epic\") should be omitted from the URL since it's applied by the \`??\` fallback.

## Technical Approach

Remove the \`!== \"none\"\` guard from three locations in \`useFilterState.ts\`:
1. \`setGroupBy\` — so selecting \"none\" writes \`groupBy=none\` to the URL instead of deleting the param
2. \`toQueryString\` — so serializing \`{groupBy: \"none\"}\` produces \`groupBy=none\` in the query string
3. \`isEmptyFilter\` — so \"none\" is recognized as an active filter state (not empty), which enables the \"clear all\" button to reset back to the default \"epic\" grouping

No changes to \`parseGroupBy\` — it already correctly parses \"none\" from the URL. No changes to \`App.tsx\` or \`MoreFiltersMenu.tsx\` — the \`??\` fallback and the dropdown both work correctly once the URL contains the right value.

**Trade-off considered:** The alternative approach (removing \"none\" from the option set entirely) was rejected because the flat view is a useful feature — the SwimLaneBoard has a \`groupBy === \"none\"\` branch that delegates to KanbanBoard for a flat column view.

## Conventions Established

- Only \`DEFAULT_GROUP_BY\` (\"epic\") is treated as the \"no-op\" value that gets omitted from the URL. All other valid GroupByOption values, including \"none\", are explicitly persisted.
- The \`isEmptyFilter\` function only considers groupBy empty when it matches \`undefined\` or \`DEFAULT_GROUP_BY\`.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### 1. \`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/issues/useFilterState.ts\`

Three changes:

**a. \`setGroupBy\` (lines 291-302):** Remove the \`groupBy !== \"none\"\` condition. Change from:
\`\`\`ts
const value =
  groupBy !== undefined &&
  groupBy !== \"none\" &&
  groupBy !== DEFAULT_GROUP_BY
    ? groupBy
    : undefined;
\`\`\`
To:
\`\`\`ts
const value =
  groupBy !== undefined && groupBy !== DEFAULT_GROUP_BY
    ? groupBy
    : undefined;
\`\`\`

**b. \`toQueryString\` (lines 170-175):** Remove the \`state.groupBy !== \"none\"\` condition. Change from:
\`\`\`ts
if (
  state.groupBy !== undefined &&
  state.groupBy !== \"none\" &&
  state.groupBy !== DEFAULT_GROUP_BY
)
  params.set(\"groupBy\", state.groupBy);
\`\`\`
To:
\`\`\`ts
if (state.groupBy !== undefined && state.groupBy !== DEFAULT_GROUP_BY)
  params.set(\"groupBy\", state.groupBy);
\`\`\`

**c. \`isEmptyFilter\` (lines 196-206):** Remove \`state.groupBy === \"none\"\` from the empty check. Change from:
\`\`\`ts
(state.groupBy === undefined ||
  state.groupBy === \"none\" ||
  state.groupBy === DEFAULT_GROUP_BY)
\`\`\`
To:
\`\`\`ts
(state.groupBy === undefined || state.groupBy === DEFAULT_GROUP_BY)
\`\`\`

### 2. \`internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/issues/__tests__/useFilterState.test.ts\`

Update tests that assert the old (broken) behavior:

**a. \"handles all known groupBy options\" test (lines 507-515):** The \"none\" case currently asserts \`groupBy\` becomes \`undefined\`. Change to assert \`groupBy\` is \`\"none\"\`:
\`\`\`ts
// Seed a non-default first, then \"none\" persists in URL
act(() => {
  result.current[1].setGroupBy(\"assignee\");
});
expect(result.current[0].groupBy).toBe(\"assignee\");
act(() => {
  result.current[1].setGroupBy(\"none\");
});
expect(result.current[0].groupBy).toBe(\"none\");
\`\`\`

**b. \"omits groupBy when value is none\" test (lines 717-719):** Change to assert \"none\" IS serialized:
\`\`\`ts
it(\"serializes groupBy when value is none\", () => {
  const result = toQueryString({ groupBy: \"none\" });
  expect(result).toBe(\"groupBy=none\");
});
\`\`\`

**c. \"serializes all groupBy options except none and epic\" test (lines 727-733):** Add \"none\" to the list of serialized options and update the test description:
\`\`\`ts
it(\"serializes all groupBy options except epic (the default)\", () => {
  const options: GroupByOption[] = [\"none\", \"assignee\", \"priority\", \"type\", \"label\"];
  for (const option of options) {
    const result = toQueryString({ groupBy: option });
    expect(result).toBe(\`groupBy=\${option}\`);
  }
});
\`\`\`

**d. \"returns true when groupBy is none\" test (lines 942-943):** Change to assert false:
\`\`\`ts
it(\"returns false when groupBy is none (it is an active filter)\", () => {
  expect(isEmptyFilter({ groupBy: \"none\" })).toBe(false);
});
\`\`\`

### 3. \`internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/groupby-url-sync.spec.ts\`

**a. \"selecting 'none' removes groupBy from URL\" test (lines 82-95):** Change to assert URL now contains \`groupBy=none\`:
\`\`\`ts
test(\"selecting 'none' sets groupBy=none in URL\", async ({ page }) => {
  await navigateAndWait(page, \"/?groupBy=priority\")
  expect(page.url()).toContain(\"groupBy=priority\")

  const groupByFilter = page.getByTestId(\"groupby-filter\")
  await groupByFilter.selectOption(\"none\")

  await expect(async () => {
    expect(page.url()).toContain(\"groupBy=none\")
  }).toPass({ timeout: 2000 })
})
\`\`\`

**Note:** This E2E test uses \`data-testid=\"groupby-filter\"\` (FilterBar dropdown). A separate task (loomcli-jv259) addresses the mismatch where FilterBar's groupBy is hidden (\`showGroupBy={false}\`) and the MoreFiltersMenu is used instead. This task does NOT change the E2E test selectors — only the URL assertion.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **E2E test selector migration** (\`data-testid=\"groupby-filter\"\` → \`data-testid=\"more-filters-groupby\"\`): Tracked by loomcli-jv259. The groupby-url-sync.spec.ts and groupby-none.spec.ts E2E tests still reference the FilterBar dropdown which is hidden in the live UI. This task only fixes the URL serialization logic; the E2E selector migration is a separate concern.
- **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/SwimLaneBoard/swimLaneStorage.ts\`**: Uses \`groupBy === \"none\"\` at lines 32, 58, 90 to skip persistence for flat view. This is correct behavior — no change needed.
- **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/SwimLaneBoard/SwimLaneBoard.tsx\`**: Uses \`groupBy === \"none\"\` at line 111 to delegate to KanbanBoard. Correct behavior — no change needed.
- **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/SwimLaneBoard/groupingUtils.ts\`**: Uses \`groupBy === \"none\"\` at line 62. Correct behavior — no change needed.
- **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/MoreFiltersMenu/MoreFiltersMenu.tsx\`**: Uses \`groupBy !== \"none\"\` at line 36 for the indicator dot. Correct behavior — the dot should only show when active grouping is enabled (not flat view).
- **\`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/FilterBar/FilterBar.tsx\`**: Has \`groupBy ?? \"none\"\` at line 371 and \`showGroupBy\` prop. Not affected by this fix since the FilterBar dropdown is hidden via \`showGroupBy={false}\`.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- No internal module dependencies beyond what already exists
- No blocking tasks — this fix is self-contained in the filter state hook

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **User navigates to \`?groupBy=none\`**: Already works — \`parseGroupBy(\"none\")\` returns \`\"none\"\`, \`filters.groupBy ?? DEFAULT_GROUP_BY\` returns \`\"none\"\`, flat view renders. No change needed.

2. **User selects \"All\" (none) from dropdown**: After fix, \`setGroupBy(\"none\")\` writes \`groupBy=none\` to URL. On parse, \`filters.groupBy\` is \`\"none\"\`. \`??\` fallback not triggered. Flat view renders correctly.

3. **User clicks \"Clear all\" while groupBy=none**: \`clearAll\` deletes all filter params including \`groupBy\`. URL becomes paramless → \`parseFromSearchParams\` returns \`undefined\` → \`??\` fallback applies \"epic\". Correct: clear resets to default.

4. **User selects \"Epic\" from dropdown**: \`setGroupBy(\"epic\")\` matches \`DEFAULT_GROUP_BY\` → value becomes \`undefined\` → \`groupBy\` param deleted from URL → fallback to \"epic\". No visible change, URL stays clean. Correct.

5. **User selects \"none\" then refreshes the page**: URL contains \`?groupBy=none\`. On reload, \`parseGroupBy(\"none\")\` returns \`\"none\"\`. Flat view restores correctly.

6. **isEmptyFilter with groupBy=none**: Returns \`false\` (\"none\" is no longer considered empty). The FilterBar \"clear\" button appears, allowing the user to reset to the \"epic\" default. This is correct — \"none\" is an explicit deviation from the default state.

7. **\`clearFilter(\"groupBy\")\` called explicitly**: Deletes \`groupBy\` param → fallback to \"epic\". Correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Selecting \"All\" (value=\"none\") in the MoreFiltersMenu dropdown must switch the kanban view from swim lanes to flat columns (KanbanBoard renders instead of swim lanes)
2. After selecting \"All\" (none), the URL must contain \`?groupBy=none\`
3. Refreshing the page with \`?groupBy=none\` in the URL must restore the flat view and show \"All\" selected in the dropdown
4. The \"Clear all\" button must be visible when groupBy is \"none\" (since it's not the default state)
5. Clicking \"Clear all\" when groupBy=none must reset the view back to \"epic\" swim lanes
6. Selecting \"Epic\" from the dropdown must NOT add \`groupBy=epic\` to the URL (it's the default, kept clean)
7. The MoreFiltersMenu indicator dot must NOT show when groupBy is \"none\" (flat view = no active grouping)
8. The MoreFiltersMenu indicator dot MUST show when groupBy is any non-none value (\"epic\", \"assignee\", etc.)
9. All unit tests in \`useFilterState.test.ts\` must pass after updating the affected assertions
10. The groupby-url-sync E2E test must assert \`groupBy=none\` appears in the URL when \"none\" is selected (not that it disappears)

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests** (useFilterState.test.ts):
- Update 4 existing test cases as detailed in Files to Modify section
- Run: \`cd internal/webui/frontend && npx vitest run src/hooks/issues/__tests__/useFilterState.test.ts\`

**E2E tests** (groupby-url-sync.spec.ts):
- Update the \"selecting 'none' removes groupBy from URL\" test to assert the opposite
- Run: \`cd internal/webui/frontend && npx playwright test groupby-url-sync\`

**E2E tests** (groupby-none.spec.ts):
- These tests navigate with \`?groupBy=none\` explicitly and should continue to pass (the parse path was never broken, only the set path). Verify no regressions.
- Run: \`cd internal/webui/frontend && npx playwright test groupby-none\`

**Manual verification**:
1. Open the app at \`/ws/:workspaceId/kanban\` (default: swim lane view)
2. Click the \"...\" button to open MoreFiltersMenu
3. Change \"Group by\" to \"All\" (none)
4. Verify: swim lanes disappear, flat column view appears
5. Verify: URL shows \`?groupBy=none\`
6. Refresh the page — flat view persists
7. Click the \"...\" again — dropdown shows \"All\" selected
8. Change to \"Epic\" — swim lanes return, \`groupBy\` disappears from URL
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Removed !== 'none' guards from setGroupBy, toQueryString, isEmptyFilter so that selecting 'none' persists as ?groupBy=none in the URL instead of collapsing to DEFAULT_GROUP_BY (epic).

title: Bug: IssueDetailData.Design shadows IssueData.Design — JSON encoding loses embedded value
description: types.go:48 embeds IssueData (Design at :35), and IssueDetailData declares its own Design at :52. Go JSON: outer field wins, inner hidden. If details.Design is empty but details.Issue.Design is non-empty, value is lost.
design:
## Summary

`IssueDetailData` (types.go:47) embeds `IssueData` (which has `Design string` at types.go:35) and also declares its own `Design string` at types.go:52. In Go JSON encoding, the outer (directly declared) field always wins over a promoted field with the same JSON tag name. This means if `IssueDetailData.Design` is empty but `IssueDetailData.IssueData.Design` is non-empty, the JSON output will contain an empty `"design":""` (or omit it entirely with `omitempty`), silently losing the value. This also affects the `IssueFromDetailData` mapping path: it reads `d.Design` (outer), not `d.IssueData.Design` (inner), so a populated inner value is overwritten by the empty outer field.

## Technical Approach

**Remove the `Design string` field from `IssueDetailData`** and rely on the promoted field from embedded `IssueData`. After removal:

- `detail.Design` resolves to `detail.IssueData.Design` via Go field promotion
- No more shadowing conflict in JSON encoding — single `"design"` key maps unambiguously
- All existing code that reads/writes `detail.Design` via dot-access continues to work (promoted field access is transparent)
- The only code that breaks is struct literal initialization — you cannot set a promoted field directly in a struct literal (`IssueDetailData{Design: "x"}` is invalid); it must be set in the embedded struct or via post-construction assignment

**Why not the other approach (remove from IssueData)?** `IssueData.Design` was intentionally added for list-view queries where backends include design (see comment at types.go:34). Removing it from `IssueData` would break list-level Design availability. The fix direction is clear: remove the duplicate from the outer struct.

## Conventions Established

None — this is a bugfix removing a duplicate field.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/backend/types.go`
- **Remove line 52**: `Design string \x60json:"design,omitempty"\x60` from `IssueDetailData`
- This is the core fix. After removal, `IssueDetailData.Design` resolves to `IssueData.Design` via promotion.

### 2. `internal/cli/cli_beads_adapter.go`
- **Remove line 302**: `Design: c.Design,` from the `toDetailData()` struct literal
- Reason: `c.toIssueData()` (called at line 300) already sets `IssueData.Design = c.Design` (see line 294). The removed line was redundant — it set the now-removed outer field. Without removing it, the code will not compile (cannot set promoted field in struct literal).

### 3. `internal/backend/mapping/issue_test.go`
- **Move `Design: "Design doc"` (line 188)** from the `IssueDetailData` struct literal into the nested `IssueData` struct literal (around line 175-186)
- Reason: same struct literal restriction — promoted fields cannot be set directly. The test assertion at line 220 (`require.Equal(t, "Design doc", e.Design)`) remains unchanged since `IssueFromDetailData` reads `d.Design` which now resolves to the promoted `IssueData.Design`.

### 4. `internal/backend/types_test.go`
- **Add a regression test** `TestIssueDetailData_DesignNotShadowed` that:
  1. Constructs `IssueDetailData` with `IssueData.Design = "my design"` (no outer Design field anymore)
  2. Marshals to JSON
  3. Verifies JSON contains `"design":"my design"`
  4. Unmarshals back and verifies `decoded.Design == "my design"`
- This test catches any future re-introduction of the shadowing pattern.
- **Update `TestIssueDetailData_JSONRoundTrip`**: add `Design: "Round trip design"` to the `IssueData` sub-literal and verify it survives the round-trip. Currently Design is not tested in this test at all.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- `IssueFromData` (mapping/issue.go:28-50) does not copy `IssueData.Design` to `entity.Issue.Design`. This means the list-view mapping path drops Design even though `IssueData` carries it. This is documented as intentionally lossy ("Fields not present in IssueData...will be zero-valued") but is inconsistent with `IssueData` now having a `Design` field. This is a pre-existing issue unrelated to the shadowing bug. If desired, it can be tracked separately.
- `IssueToData` (mapping/issue.go:112-134) similarly drops Design when converting entity→IssueData. Same pre-existing design choice.

## Dependencies

None. This is a leaf-level change touching only `internal/backend/` types and the CLI adapter.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **IssueData.Design populated, outer removed**: After fix, `detail.Design` correctly resolves to the promoted field. JSON marshal includes `"design":"value"`. No data loss. This is the primary bug scenario.

2. **Neither IssueData.Design nor old outer Design populated**: `detail.Design` is `""`. With `omitempty`, `"design"` key is omitted from JSON. No change in behavior.

3. **Struct literal initialization**: Code that previously wrote `backend.IssueDetailData{Design: "x"}` will fail to compile. The compiler enforces the fix — there are exactly 2 such sites (listed in Files to Modify). Both must be updated.

4. **`convert.go:124` (`d.Design = details.Design`)**: This assignment still compiles and works correctly — Go allows assignment to promoted fields via dot syntax. `d.Design` now resolves to `d.IssueData.Design`. No change needed.

5. **`mapping/issue.go:62` (`e.Design = d.Design`)**: Same as above — reads promoted field. No change needed.

6. **`issue_text.go:37` (`detail.Design`)**: Reads promoted field. No change needed.

7. **`convert_test.go:297` (`got.Design`)**: Reads promoted field. No change needed.

8. **`convert_test.go:812` (`var _ backend.IssueDetailData = ...`)**: Compile-time type check. Still works since `IssueDetailData` still has a `Design` field (promoted). No change needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `IssueDetailData` has no direct `Design` field — only the promoted one from `IssueData`
2. `json.Marshal` of an `IssueDetailData` where `IssueData.Design` is non-empty produces JSON containing the design value (not empty/missing)
3. `json.Unmarshal` of `{"design":"x", ...}` into `IssueDetailData` correctly populates `IssueData.Design`
4. `IssueFromDetailData` correctly reads Design from a struct where only `IssueData.Design` is set
5. `go build ./...` succeeds (no compile errors from promoted field in struct literals)
6. `go test ./internal/backend/... ./internal/backend/mapping/... ./internal/backend/beads/... ./internal/cli/...` all pass
7. The new regression test explicitly verifies the shadowing bug is fixed
8. `detailsToDetailData` correctly populates Design (via promoted field assignment)
9. `cliBeadsAdapter.toDetailData()` correctly populates Design (via the embedded IssueData, not a removed outer field)

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
1. **New test `TestIssueDetailData_DesignNotShadowed`** (types_test.go): construct with IssueData.Design set, JSON marshal/unmarshal round-trip, verify value survives
2. **Updated `TestIssueDetailData_JSONRoundTrip`**: add Design to IssueData in the test fixture, verify it round-trips
3. **Existing `TestDetailsToDetailData`** (convert_test.go): already checks `got.Design == "Design doc"` — should still pass since `got.Design` is now the promoted field
4. **Existing `TestIssueFromDetailData`** (mapping/issue_test.go): already checks `e.Design == "Design doc"` — will pass after moving Design into IssueData sub-literal

### Manual Verification
- Run `go vet ./internal/backend/...` — confirms no struct tag conflicts
- Run full test suite: `go test ./...`
close_reason: Removed shadowing Design field from IssueDetailData, moved test fixtures to use promoted field, added regression test

title: Bug: FleetBackend.Update silently drops UpdateParams.Claim field
description: fleet/params.go updateParamsToPatchRequest maps 15 fields but not Claim. Fleet has dedicated ClaimIssue endpoint, so this is by design — but should document or return error when Claim=true in Update.
design:
## Summary

FleetBackend.Update silently drops the UpdateParams.Claim field because updateParamsToPatchRequest (internal/backend/fleet/params.go) does not map it to the PATCH request body. Unlike BeadsBackend (which passes Claim through to the RPC server's atomic claim handler), FleetBackend uses a separate ClaimIssue endpoint (POST /fleet/claim). The fix is to make FleetBackend.Update return an explicit error when Claim=true, directing callers to use ClaimIssue instead of silently ignoring the claim intent.

## Technical Approach

**Return an error, don't route silently.** When FleetBackend.Update receives UpdateParams with Claim=true, it should return a backend.ErrValidation error explaining that claims must go through ClaimIssue. This is the safest approach because:

1. The fleet server's PATCH /issues/:id endpoint does not support atomic claims — that's what POST /fleet/claim is for.
2. Silently routing to ClaimIssue would change the semantics (ClaimIssue uses fleet server-managed TTL, ignores other UpdateParams fields).
3. Other callers who might accidentally set Claim=true in an Update call will get an immediate, clear error instead of silent data loss.

**Comparison with other backends:**
- BeadsBackend.Update (beads.go:275): Maps Claim to rpc.UpdateArgs.Claim — works because beads RPC server handles claim atomically within the update path.
- agentipc.Backend.Update (agentipc/backend.go:101): JSON-marshals the full UpdateParams — Claim is included since it serializes as json:"claim,omitempty".
- cliBeadsAdapter.Update (cli_beads_adapter.go:142): Maps Claim to --claim flag — works correctly.
- FleetBackend is the only backend that silently drops Claim.

**Why not add Claim to updateParamsToPatchRequest?** The fleet server's PATCH endpoint doesn't handle atomic claims. Sending claim:true in the PATCH body would either be ignored by the server or cause an unknown-field error — neither is correct. The claim operation requires the dedicated /fleet/claim endpoint.

## Conventions Established

Follows the existing validation pattern: backend methods return backend.ErrValidation for unsupported parameter combinations (see FleetBackend.ClaimIssue empty-id check, FleetBackend.Reopen empty-id check, FleetBackend.Delete empty-IDs check).

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

1. **internal/backend/fleet/fleet.go** (FleetBackend.Update method, ~line 267)
   - Add a guard at the top of Update: if params.Claim is true, return backend.ErrValidation("Update", "Claim field is not supported in FleetBackend.Update; use ClaimIssue instead")
   - This check goes BEFORE the updateParamsToPatchRequest call so no HTTP request is made

2. **internal/backend/fleet/fleet_test.go** (after TestUpdate_HappyPath)
   - Add TestUpdate_ClaimRejected: call Update with Claim=true, assert it returns a *backend.BackendError with Kind=KindValidation and message containing "ClaimIssue"
   - Add TestUpdate_ClaimFalseAllowed: call Update with Claim=false (default) and other fields set, assert it succeeds (no false positive)

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **AgentState missing from updateParamsToPatchRequest**: Already tracked as loomcli-589zd (Bug: FleetBackend.Update silently drops UpdateParams.AgentState), currently in review status.
- **third_party/beads/examples/beads-web-ui/handlers.go PatchIssueRequest**: Example app in third_party, not the fleet backend path. Not affected by this change.
- **WebUI pipeline (handlers_issues_write.go, service/issue.go, issue_helpers.go)**: The WebUI PATCH handler goes through patchParamsToUpdateArgs → rpc.UpdateArgs, not through FleetBackend. The WebUI pipeline doesn't expose Claim in PatchIssueRequest/PatchIssueParams (by design — web UI claims go through handleFleetClaim). No change needed.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed.
- No blocking dependencies on other tasks.
- The backend error types (backend.ErrValidation) already exist in internal/backend/errors.go.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Claim=true with no other fields**: Return ErrValidation immediately. No HTTP request is made. The caller should use ClaimIssue instead.
2. **Claim=true with other fields set (e.g., Status, Assignee)**: Return ErrValidation immediately. The caller should split this into two calls: ClaimIssue for the claim, then Update for the other fields. This is a deliberate trade-off — we prefer failing loudly over partial application.
3. **Claim=false (default zero value)**: No change in behavior. The guard checks `params.Claim` which is false by default. Update proceeds normally.
4. **Concurrent Update and ClaimIssue calls**: Not affected by this change. ClaimIssue's atomicity is handled by the fleet server, not by this guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- FleetBackend.Update with Claim=true returns a *backend.BackendError with Kind=KindValidation
- The error message mentions ClaimIssue to guide the caller
- FleetBackend.Update with Claim=false (and valid fields) succeeds as before
- No HTTP request is made when Claim=true (the guard is before the HTTP call)
- All existing fleet backend tests continue to pass

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests

1. **TestUpdate_ClaimRejected**: Create FleetBackend with test server, call Update with Claim=true, assert:
   - Error is non-nil
   - Error is *backend.BackendError with Kind=KindValidation
   - Error message contains "ClaimIssue"
   - The test server was NOT hit (no HTTP request made) — verify by checking request count or using a handler that calls t.Fatal if invoked

2. **TestUpdate_ClaimFalseAllowed**: Call Update with Claim=false and a valid Title field, assert no error (regression guard against false positives on the Claim check)

### Manual Verification

1. Build loom, start in fleet mode
2. Attempt an update with claim via the programmatic API — verify error is returned
3. Use ClaimIssue endpoint — verify claim still works correctly
close_reason: Completed: FleetBackend.Update now returns ErrValidation when Claim=true, with tests

design:
## Summary

This task creates the capstone integration test file `internal/cli/session_echo_test.go` that validates all session audit trail layers work together end-to-end. Using the EchoBackend (controlled, deterministic fake) and real file-based session store, these tests exercise the full lifecycle: session creation → EchoBackend invocation with UsageHandler → hook dispatch (transcript append) → session finalization → index/metadata persistence → API handler query. No real AI calls, git operations, or bd subprocesses are needed.

This is the final validation that the session audit trail feature (epic loomcli-rztzs) works as designed, tying together internal/sessions/, internal/cli/backend_echo.go, internal/cli/hooks_dispatch.go, and internal/webui/handlers_sessions.go.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: One test file with the build tag \`//go:build testbackend\` (same as backend_echo.go and existing echo tests), in the \`cli\` package. Tests use EchoTestEnv for backend setup and \`sessions.NewStore(t.TempDir())\` for isolated session storage. API handler tests use \`httptest.NewRequest\` + \`httptest.NewRecorder\` to call handlers directly without starting a server.

**Key design patterns**:
- Follow existing patterns from \`automode_echo_test.go\` (EchoTestEnv usage), \`finalize_test.go\` (session store helpers), and \`backend_echo_test.go\` (handler variants)
- Each test is self-contained with its own temp dir and session store — no shared state
- Use \`UsageHandler(inputTokens, outputTokens)\` to inject known token counts
- Use \`ErrorHandler(err)\` to simulate failures
- Use \`dispatchHookEvent()\` directly to test transcript appending (it's in the same \`cli\` package)
- Use \`handleListTaskSessions(sessStore)\` directly via httptest to test API response shape

**Trade-offs**:
- Tests are in \`internal/cli/\` (not \`internal/sessions/\`) because they need access to both the EchoBackend (cli package) and the session store — the \`cli\` package already imports \`sessions\`
- Build tag \`testbackend\` keeps these tests out of normal CI unless explicitly requested (matching existing convention)
- Tests create real files on disk (prompt.txt, metadata.json, transcript.jsonl, index.jsonl) rather than mocking the store, because the goal is integration validation

## Files to Create

### internal/cli/session_echo_test.go
Build tag: \`//go:build testbackend\`
Package: \`cli\`

Contains 5 test functions:

**1. TestSessionCapture_FullLifecycle**
- Creates a \`sessions.Store\` with \`sessions.NewStore(t.TempDir())\`
- Creates a session via \`store.CreateSession(CreateOptions{AgentName: "test-agent", Backend: "echo", Prompt: "implement feature X", AttemptNum: 1})\`
- Sets up EchoTestEnv, configures \`UsageHandler(5000, 2000)\` on the backend
- Sets LOOM_SESSION_ID env var to the session ID (for hook dispatch context)
- Runs \`env.RunNonInteractive("implement feature X")\`
- Finalizes the collector to get token counts, then calls \`sess.Finalize(FinalizeOptions{TaskID: "task-lifecycle", ExitCode: 0, InputTokens: su.InputTokens, OutputTokens: su.OutputTokens, ...})\`
- Verifies:
  - \`index.jsonl\`: Query by task_id returns 1 record with correct session_id, task_id, exit_code=0, status=completed, input_tokens=5000, output_tokens=2000
  - \`metadata.json\`: LoadMetadata returns matching data, EndedAt is non-nil, DurationS > 0
  - \`prompt.txt\`: ReadPrompt returns "implement feature X"
  - Backend invocations: \`env.AssertInvoked(1)\`

**2. TestSessionCapture_HookAppendTranscript**
- Creates a session store and session
- Calls \`dispatchHookEvent()\` directly with several HookEvent values:
  - \`{Type: HookSessionStart, Model: "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250514"}\`
  - \`{Type: HookTurnStart, Prompt: "user question"}\`
  - \`{Type: HookTurnEnd}\`
  - \`{Type: HookSessionEnd}\`
- Passes the store's beadsDir and session ID to dispatchHookEvent
- Calls \`store.LoadTranscript(sessionID)\` and verifies:
  - Returns 4 entries
  - Entry roles: "system", "user", "assistant", "system"
  - Entry types: "session_start", "text", "turn_end", "session_end"
  - Content of session_start entry contains "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250514"
  - Content of text entry is "user question"

Note: dispatchHookEvent takes beadsDir (the parent of sessions/) and sessionID. Since Store is created with NewStore(beadsDir) which creates beadsDir/sessions/, we need to pass the correct beadsDir. The test will create the store, then use the beadsDir path (the temp dir itself) when calling dispatchHookEvent.

**3. TestSessionCapture_MultipleSessionsPerTask**
- Creates a session store
- Creates 3 sessions with the same agent name but different attempt numbers (1, 2, 3) — simulating retries
- Finalizes each with the same TaskID "task-retry" and ExitCode 0
- Calls \`store.SessionsByTask("task-retry")\`
- Verifies:
  - Returns exactly 3 records
  - All have TaskID "task-retry"
  - All have status completed
  - Records are sorted by StartedAt (ascending — each session created sequentially)
  - AttemptNum values are 1, 2, 3 respectively

**4. TestSessionCapture_FailedSession**
- Creates an EchoTestEnv with \`ErrorHandler(errors.New("lint failure"))\`
- Creates a session store and session
- Runs \`env.RunNonInteractive(...)\` — expects error return
- Finalizes with \`ExitCode: 1, ErrorClass: "lint_failure"\`
- Verifies:
  - \`metadata.json\`: status=failed, exit_code=1, error_class="lint_failure"
  - \`index.jsonl\`: Query returns record with status=failed, exit_code=1
  - Backend was still invoked (\`env.AssertInvoked(1)\`)

**5. TestSessionCapture_ApiQuery**
- Creates a session store, creates 2 sessions for "task-api", finalizes both
- Constructs \`handleListTaskSessions(sessStore)\` handler
- Creates \`httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/api/tasks/task-api/sessions", nil)\` with path value set
- Note: Since Go 1.22 \`http.ServeMux\` sets path values but httptest doesn't, we need to use \`r.SetPathValue("taskId", "task-api")\` on the request
- Calls handler with \`httptest.NewRecorder\`
- Verifies:
  - Status code 200
  - Response body unmarshals to \`SessionListResponse\`
  - \`response.Success == true\`
  - \`response.Data.TaskID == "task-api"\`
  - \`len(response.Data.Sessions) == 2\`
  - Each session record has the expected fields (session_id non-empty, task_id matches, status is completed)

## Files to Modify

None — this is a new test file. All dependencies already exist on the \`session-audit-trail\` branch.

## Dependencies

**Internal modules (all exist on session-audit-trail branch)**:
- \`internal/sessions\` — Store, CreateSession, Session.Finalize, SessionsByTask, LoadMetadata, LoadTranscript, ReadPrompt, Query
- \`internal/cli/backend_echo.go\` — EchoBackend, EchoTestEnv, UsageHandler, ErrorHandler, DefaultEchoHandler
- \`internal/cli/testenv_echo_test.go\` — NewEchoTestEnv, RunNonInteractive, AssertInvoked
- \`internal/cli/hooks_dispatch.go\` — dispatchHookEvent, HookEvent types
- \`internal/webui/handlers_sessions.go\` — handleListTaskSessions, SessionListResponse
- \`internal/usage\` — Collector, NewCollector

**External packages**: None beyond stdlib (\`net/http/httptest\`, \`encoding/json\`, \`testing\`, \`errors\`)

**Task dependencies**: All completed (loomcli-rztzs.1, loomcli-rztzs.2, loomcli-m03mm.3, loomcli-ag9nf.3, loomcli-b4ija.1)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **dispatchHookEvent with empty beadsDir/sessionID**: The function already handles this (returns nil). Test 2 should verify this precondition by passing valid values.

2. **Session ID uniqueness**: Each \`CreateSession\` call generates a unique ID via crypto/rand. Tests should not assume ID format but verify non-empty and unique across sessions.

3. **Timing sensitivity**: Tests should not depend on sub-millisecond timing. Use \`before := time.Now().UTC().Add(-1 * time.Second)\` pattern (from finalize_test.go) for time window assertions.

4. **Empty results**: API handler test should verify that querying a non-existent task returns empty array (not null) — matching the handler's nil-to-empty-slice normalization.

5. **EchoTestEnv is global state**: EchoTestEnv calls \`SetBackend("echo")\` which mutates global backend state. Tests should not run in parallel (\`t.Parallel()\` should NOT be used) — matching the pattern in \`automode_echo_test.go\`.

6. **httptest path values**: Go 1.22's \`http.ServeMux\` pattern matching sets \`r.PathValue()\`, but \`httptest.NewRequest\` does not. Must use \`r.SetPathValue("taskId", value)\` explicitly.

7. **Store beadsDir vs sessions dir**: \`NewStore(beadsDir)\` creates \`beadsDir/sessions/\`, but \`dispatchHookEvent\` takes beadsDir (not the sessions/ subdir). The test must pass the right directory.

## Testing Strategy

**How to run**:
\`\`\`bash
cd /home/admin/codebase/2/loomcli/worktrees/drift
go test -tags testbackend -run TestSessionCapture ./internal/cli/ -v
\`\`\`

**Key scenarios covered**:
1. Full lifecycle: create → invoke → finalize → verify all artifacts (index, metadata, prompt)
2. Hook dispatch: transcript entries are correctly appended and retrievable
3. Multiple sessions per task: retry scenario with correct sorting and filtering
4. Failure path: error propagation, failed status in both metadata and index
5. API layer: handler returns correct JSON shape matching design doc

**Manual verification**: After implementation, run with \`-v\` flag and inspect t.Log output. Verify no leaked temp directories. Run with \`-race\` to check for race conditions. Run with \`-count=10\` to check for flaky timing issues.

**What is NOT tested here** (covered by other tasks):
- Session purge (covered by finalize_test.go TestPurgeOlderThan)
- Concurrent transcript appends (covered by store_test.go TestAppendTranscript_Concurrent)
- EchoBackend unit behavior (covered by backend_echo_test.go)
- Individual handler error paths (can be added later as unit tests)

title: E2E: Sessions tab in issue detail panel
description: labels: e2e,browser,sessions,P1
design:
## Summary

This task creates a Playwright browser E2E test spec for the Sessions tab in the IssueDetailPanel. The Sessions tab displays a cost summary bar and a two-column layout with a SessionTimeline (list of session rows) and a SessionDetailView (transcript/diff viewer). Tests verify the full user flow: opening an issue panel, switching to the Sessions tab, seeing the cost summary, selecting sessions in the timeline, viewing transcript/diff content, and handling loading/error/empty states. All API endpoints are mocked at the Playwright route level.

## Technical Approach

Follow the established inline-mock pattern from \`comments-section.spec.ts\`: inline mock data, \`page.route()\` interception, helper functions for navigation and panel interaction, assertions using \`data-testid\` and \`toBeVisible()\`/\`toContainText()\`.

**Key decisions (all verified against source code):**

- **Tab selection:** Use \`page.locator('#issue-panel-tab-sessions')\` — the component renders \`id="issue-panel-tab-\${tab.id}"\` where tab.id is "sessions" (IssueDetailPanel.tsx:281-293, rendered at line ~1064). Do NOT use \`getByRole('tab', { name: 'Sessions' })\` — these are \`<div role="tab">\` elements where accessible name matching is unreliable due to nested spans.

- **SSE handling:** Mock \`/api/events\` with \`route.abort()\`. The \`useTaskSessions\` hook (useTaskSessions.ts) subscribes to SSE via \`useSSE\` for \`session_change\` events. Without this mock, EventSource reconnection loops cause hangs. Using \`route.abort()\` (not \`createSSEMock\`) because this spec never needs to send SSE events — it only needs to prevent the hang. Sibling spec a0n5u uses \`createSSEMock\` because it tests SSE-triggered refetches.

- **API response envelopes (verified against TypeScript types in types/session.ts):**
  - Sessions list: \`{ success: true, data: { task_id: string, sessions: SessionRecord[] } }\` — matches \`SessionListResponse\` (types/session.ts:50-56). Client does \`resp.data?.sessions ?? []\` (api/sessions.ts:29).
  - Transcript: \`{ success: true, data: { session_id: string, entries: TranscriptEntry[] } }\` — matches \`TranscriptResponse\` (types/session.ts:65-71). Client does \`resp.data?.entries ?? []\` (api/sessions.ts:75).
  - Diff: Raw text body with \`contentType: 'text/plain'\` — client uses \`getText()\` (api/client.ts:209-216, api/sessions.ts:96-98).
  - Issue details: Direct JSON object (not wrapped in \`{ success: true, data }\`) — follows \`comments-section.spec.ts\` pattern (line 137).
  - Ready list: \`{ success: true, data: [issues] }\` — follows \`comments-section.spec.ts\` pattern (line 114).

- **Scope boundaries:** This spec covers the *SessionsTab container* concerns. Deep timeline row interactions (sorting, formatting, keyboard nav) belong to loomcli-hmq8g. Deep transcript/diff content testing (CodeMirror rendering, entry role formatting, error per inner tab) belongs to loomcli-a0n5u. This spec verifies the container orchestration: tab switching, cost summary, empty/error/loading states, timeline rendering, session selection showing detail view, and basic inner tab visibility.

- **No shared helper file:** All three session specs (this, hmq8g, a0n5u) use self-contained inline mocks per the \`comments-section.spec.ts\` pattern. This avoids merge conflicts in parallel agent workflows. The duplication is intentional and minimal (~20 lines per factory function).

## Conventions Established

- **Session mock factory pattern:** \`createMockSession(overrides?: Partial<SessionRecord>): SessionRecord\` with sensible defaults (id auto-generated, agent_name "agent-1", status "completed", etc.). Sibling specs hmq8g and a0n5u should follow this same factory shape.
- **Navigation pattern for sessions:** \`navigateToApp\` → \`openIssuePanel\` → \`switchToSessionsTab\` — three discrete helper functions. The \`switchToSessionsTab\` helper clicks \`#issue-panel-tab-sessions\` then waits for \`data-testid="sessions-tab"\` OR \`data-testid="sessions-empty"\` to be visible.
- **SSE abort pattern:** For specs that don't need SSE events, mock with \`page.route('**/api/events', route => route.abort())\` — must be set up before \`page.goto('/')\`.
- **Error text assertion:** Use \`toContainText('Failed to load sessions')\` (not exact match) because error div renders \`Failed to load sessions: {error.message}\` (SessionsTab.tsx:48).

## Files to Create

### \`internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/sessions-tab.spec.ts\`

The main E2E spec file. Structure:

**Imports:**
\`\`\`typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from "@playwright/test";
\`\`\`

**Mock data (top of file):**

- \`createMockSession(overrides?)\` factory returning a valid \`SessionRecord\` shape:
  \`\`\`typescript
  function createMockSession(overrides?: Record<string, unknown>): SessionRecord {
    return {
      id: overrides?.id ?? "sess-001",
      agent_name: "agent-alpha",
      backend: "claude",
      model: "opus-4",
      phase: "implementation",
      status: "completed",
      started_at: "2026-03-20T10:00:00Z",

- 3 pre-built mock sessions:
  - \`completedSession\`: Default from factory (completed, has_transcript: true, has_diff: true, input_tokens: 5000, output_tokens: 3000, cost: 0.45)
  - \`activeSession\`: Override id: "sess-002", agent_name: "agent-beta", status: "running", is_active: true, has_diff: false, ended_at: undefined, duration_s: undefined, input_tokens: 1500, output_tokens: 800, cost: 0.12

**Helper functions:**

     - If \`options.transcriptError\`: return 500

  7. \`**/api/tasks/*/sessions/*/diff\` → (also before broader sessions route)

- Neighborhood scan found no unaddressed sibling files in the SessionsTab component directory — all session components (SessionsTab.tsx, SessionTimeline.tsx, SessionTimelineRow.tsx, SessionDetailView.tsx) are tested through the three session E2E specs.

- Playwright infrastructure: playwright.config.ts, chromium project

  - \`sessions-tab\` (SessionsTab.tsx:63)
  - \`sessions-empty\` (SessionsTab.tsx:56)
  - \`session-timeline\` (SessionTimeline.tsx:42)
  - \`session-detail-view\` (SessionDetailView.tsx:54)
  - \`session-inner-tab-transcript\` (SessionDetailView.tsx:106)

- Tab panel: \`#issue-panel-tabpanel-sessions\` (IssueDetailPanel.tsx)
- No external packages needed. No blocking task dependencies.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **Sessions API 500:** Renders error state (no testid) with text "Failed to load sessions: {error.message}" (SessionsTab.tsx:47-49). Test assertion: use \`toContainText('Failed to load sessions')\` on the tab panel locator. The error renders in a \`<div className={styles.emptyState}>\` — abort and show error, do not retry.
- **Sessions API 404:** Client catches 404 and returns \`[]\` (api/sessions.ts:31-33) → shows empty state with \`data-testid="sessions-empty"\` and text "No sessions recorded yet".
- **Empty sessions list (200 with empty array):** Same as 404 — shows empty state.
- **Active sessions badge visibility:** Only rendered when \`summary.activeSessions > 0\` (SessionsTab.tsx:81). When no sessions have \`is_active: true\`, the badge element does not exist in the DOM. Test both presence (with active session) and absence (with all inactive).
- **Token formatting edge cases:** \`formatTokensShort\` (SessionsTab.tsx:127-130): ≥1M → "X.XM", ≥1K → "X.XK", <1K → raw number. Mock data total is 11000 → "11.0K".
- **Cost formatting edge cases:** \`formatCostUSD\` (SessionsTab.tsx:133-136): 0 → "$0.00", <$0.01 → "<$0.01", else → "$X.XX". Mock data total is $0.60 → "$0.60".
- **Session with has_diff=false:** Diff inner tab button has \`disabled={!session.has_diff}\` (SessionDetailView.tsx:114) and title="No diff available" (line 115). Test asserts \`toBeDisabled()\`.
- **Session with has_transcript=false:** When transcript API returns empty entries and loading is done, shows "No transcript entries" (SessionDetailView.tsx:137). This is tested indirectly via the failedSession (has_transcript: false), but deep testing is in a0n5u scope.
- **Detail view metadata conditional rendering:** "Model:" only shown when \`session.model\` is truthy (line 57). "Files:" only shown when \`session.files_changed > 0\` (line 69). "+X -Y" only shown when either is > 0 (line 75). Tests use completedSession (all present) and verify activeSession selection changes content.
- **Polling interference:** Hooks poll at 10s/3s intervals. Tests must NOT rely on polling timing. Mock initial responses and assert on first render. The \`route.abort()\` on SSE prevents SSE-triggered refetches from interfering.
- **Loading state (race condition):** The loading state (SessionsTab.tsx:36-42) shows a spinner with no testid. This spec does NOT test the loading spinner — it would require a deferred response mock which adds complexity for minimal value. The unit test (SessionsTab.test.tsx) already covers loading state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Test file \`tests/e2e/sessions-tab.spec.ts\` exists and passes: \`npx playwright test tests/e2e/sessions-tab.spec.ts\`
- Sessions tab is reachable by clicking \`#issue-panel-tab-sessions\` after opening an issue panel
- Cost summary displays correct session count, formatted token total, and formatted cost total
- Active sessions badge appears when at least one session has \`is_active: true\` and does NOT appear when none are active
- Empty state shows \`data-testid="sessions-empty"\` with "No sessions recorded yet" when sessions API returns empty array
- Error state shows "Failed to load sessions" text when sessions API returns 500
- Timeline renders one row per session with correct \`data-testid="session-row-{id}"\` pattern
- Clicking a session row shows \`data-testid="session-detail-view"\` and hides the placeholder text
- Detail view displays model, exit code, files changed, and lines added/removed for the selected session
- Transcript tab (\`session-transcript\`) is visible by default when a session is selected
- Diff tab (\`session-diff\`) is visible after clicking the diff inner tab button
- Diff inner tab button is disabled when the selected session has \`has_diff: false\`
- Sessions API endpoint is called when the Sessions tab is activated (not before)
- Transcript API endpoint is called when a session is selected
- Diff API endpoint is called only when the diff inner tab is clicked (not on session selection)
- All tests must NOT depend on SSE events or polling timing

## Testing Strategy

**Automated (Playwright browser E2E):**
- Run with: \`npx playwright test tests/e2e/sessions-tab.spec.ts\`
- All tests use mocked API routes (no real backend needed)
- Assertion patterns:
  - \`expect(locator).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 })\` for element presence
  - \`expect(locator).toContainText('...')\` for text content (not exact match)
  - \`expect(locator).toBeDisabled()\` for disabled buttons
  - \`expect.poll(() => counter, { timeout: 5000 })\` for API call count tracking
- Each test calls \`setupMocks()\` fresh — no shared state between tests
- Tests run in isolation (no \`test.describe.serial\`)

**Manual verification:**
- Open the app with a task that has session data
- Click the task card to open detail panel
- Switch to Sessions tab and verify cost summary bar
- Click session rows and verify detail view updates
- Switch between Transcript and Diff inner tabs
- Test with a task that has no sessions (empty state)

description: Add unit tests for init.go setup flow (13 untested functions). Key functions to test: runInit, createWorktree, setupHooks, validateGitRepo, ensureBeadsInit. design:
## Summary

Add comprehensive unit tests for init.go setup flow to increase coverage from ~35% to 70%+. The init.go file contains 17 functions, with 10 already tested. This plan focuses on testing the remaining untested functions and improving coverage for partially-tested functions through stdin mocking for interactive functions and command mocking for orchestration functions.

## Technical Approach

### Testing Strategy
1. **Stdin Mocking** - Add a test helper to mock os.Stdin using pipes for interactive functions (promptYesNo, promptString, promptInt)
2. **Command Mocking** - Use existing CommandMock infrastructure for orchestration functions (createWorktrees)
3. **Output Capture** - Optionally capture stdout for output-only functions (showSummary)
4. **Table-driven tests** - Follow existing patterns with test cases covering happy paths and edge cases

### Key Design Decision
The interactive prompt functions read from os.Stdin via bufio.NewReader. We'll create a test helper that:
- Creates a pipe (read/write ends)
- Writes test input to write end
- Replaces os.Stdin with read end for duration of test
- Uses t.Cleanup() for restoration

## Files to Create

None - all tests go in existing init_test.go

## Files to Modify

### internal/cli/testutil_test.go
Add stdin mocking helper function:
- `MockStdin(t *testing.T, input string)` - creates pipe, writes input, replaces os.Stdin, auto-restores via t.Cleanup()

### internal/cli/init_test.go
Add the following new tests:

**1. Tests for createWorktrees (0% → 70%+)**
- `TestCreateWorktrees_NonInteractive_NoExisting` - creates worktrees with --yes flag
- `TestCreateWorktrees_NonInteractive_WithExisting` - skips existing worktrees
- `TestCreateWorktrees_NonInteractive_CustomNames` - uses --names flag
- `TestCreateWorktrees_NonInteractive_NoneToCreate` - all names already exist

**2. Tests for promptYesNo (0% → 100%)**
- `TestPromptYesNo_DefaultYes` - tests default yes with empty input
- `TestPromptYesNo_DefaultNo` - tests default no with empty input  
- `TestPromptYesNo_ExplicitYes` - tests 'y' and 'yes' inputs
- `TestPromptYesNo_ExplicitNo` - tests 'n' and 'no' inputs

**3. Tests for promptString (0% → 100%)**
- `TestPromptString_Default` - empty input returns default
- `TestPromptString_Custom` - custom input returned
- `TestPromptString_Whitespace` - whitespace trimmed

**4. Tests for promptInt (0% → 100%)**
- `TestPromptInt_Default` - empty input returns default
- `TestPromptInt_ValidInt` - valid integer parsed
- `TestPromptInt_InvalidInt` - invalid input returns default

**5. Tests for showSummary (0% → 100%)**
- `TestShowSummary_MultipleNames` - verifies output with multiple names
- `TestShowSummary_EmptyNames` - verifies fallback to 'falcon'

**6. Tests to improve partial coverage**
- `TestInitBeads_Failure` - bd init returns error (64.3% → 85%+)
- `TestCreateSingleWorktree_RetryFails` - second attempt also fails (75% → 90%+)
- `TestCheckPrerequisites_InsideWorktree` - warns when in worktree (92.3% → 100%)

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- Uses existing CommandMock infrastructure from testutil_test.go
- Standard library os, bytes, io packages for stdin mocking

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

### Interactive Function Edge Cases
- EOF/read error on stdin → returns default value
- Mixed case input (Y/YES/Yes) → normalized to lowercase
- Whitespace around input → trimmed before processing
- Invalid integer input → returns default value

### createWorktrees Edge Cases
- All requested names already exist → returns existing names only
- Some names exist, some don't → creates only new ones
- Empty worktrees directory → creates all requested
- initNames flag with custom comma-separated names

### Error Scenarios
- bd init fails with error message
- git worktree add fails on retry attempt
- Directory creation fails (permissions)

## Testing Strategy

### How to Verify Tests Work
1. Run `go test ./internal/cli/... -run TestInit -v` to see all init tests pass
2. Run `go test ./internal/cli/... -coverprofile=cover.out` for coverage
3. Run `go tool cover -func=cover.out | grep init.go` to verify per-function coverage

### Key Scenarios to Cover
- Non-interactive mode (--yes flag) for all functions
- Interactive mode with stdin mocking
- Error paths (command failures, invalid input)
- Edge cases (empty input, existing resources, retries)

### Coverage Target
Current: ~35% of init.go
Target: 70%+ of init.go

Functions by priority:
1. createWorktrees - high value, testable (large function)
2. promptYesNo/promptString/promptInt - medium value, need stdin mock
3. showSummary - low value but easy to test
4. initBeads/createSingleWorktree/checkPrerequisites - improve existing coverage

Coverage improved significantly across all targeted functions.

title: webui: Escape during EditableTitle/EditableDescription edit closes the whole issue panel
description: LIVE-CONFIRMED via agent-browser: clicking a kanban card to open the panel, clicking the title to enter edit mode, then pressing Escape closes the entire panel instead of just cancelling the edit. Root cause: handleEscapeKeyDown in internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/ui/useKeyboardShortcuts.tsx around line 123 is attached to document via addEventListener. React's e.stopPropagation() in EditableTitle.tsx:108-112 only stops the synthetic React bubble — it does not stop native events from reaching document-level listeners. Fix: add an isInputFocused(event) guard to handleEscapeKeyDown (helper already exists at line ~75 of the same file). Same fix covers EditableDescription's textarea.
design:
# Fix: Escape during inline edit closes the whole issue panel

## Summary
The global Escape layer registry in `useKeyboardShortcuts.tsx` attaches a single document-level keydown listener that fires whichever layer is on top (e.g., `LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL` → `onClose`). Inline-edit components (EditableTitle, EditableDescription) cancel their edit from the input's React `onKeyDown` and call `e.stopPropagation()` — but React synthetic propagation-stopping does **not** stop the native event from reaching the document listener. Result: a single Escape press both cancels the edit *and* closes the entire panel.

The fix is NOT a blanket "skip when input is focused" guard on `handleEscapeKeyDown`, because several modals (`SessionNamePrompt`, `BackendPickerPrompt`, `CreateIssueModal`, `CreateWorkspaceModal`, `AssigneePrompt`) auto-focus an input and legitimately rely on the registry listener to close them when Escape is pressed from that input — a blanket guard would regress those modals.

Instead, extend the layer API with a per-layer opt-in flag. Layers that host inline editing (panels) opt in; modals that want Escape-from-input to close them leave the flag off (default).

## Technical Approach
1. Extend the `Layer` record and `registerLayer`/`useRegisterEscapeLayer` signatures with an optional `suppressWhenInputFocused: boolean` (default `false`).
2. In the registry's `handleEscapeKeyDown`, after locating the top layer, if `top.suppressWhenInputFocused && isInputFocused(event)`, return early (do NOT fire the handler, do NOT fall through to the next layer, do NOT call `preventDefault`). This lets the component's own React `onKeyDown` run its local cancel logic.
3. Set the flag to `true` on the three panel-level layer registrations that host inline editing:
   - `IssueDetailPanel.tsx` (LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL)
   - `IssueDetailView.tsx` (LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL)
   - `AgentDetailPanel.tsx` (LAYER_AGENT_PANEL)
4. Leave every other registration unchanged (modals, dropdowns-as-layers, cheatsheet, workspace switcher, task drawer, toast, confirm dialog). They default to `false` and continue to close on Escape from an input — which is what they want.

### Why not just guard globally?
- SessionNamePrompt, BackendPickerPrompt, CreateIssueModal, CreateWorkspaceModal, AssigneePrompt all auto-focus an input/select and rely on the registry listener to close the modal on Escape — they have no local onKeyDown cancel. A global guard would silently break "Escape closes the modal" for these.

### Why not fall through to the next layer?
- If IssueDetailPanel is the top layer and we skip it when input is focused, falling through to (e.g.) a KeyboardCheatsheet or WorkspaceSwitcher layer lower in the stack would surprise the user. The inline-edit component's own handler is what should run; registry should simply step aside.

### Why not also preventDefault?
- When we skip, we want the browser's default Escape behavior to remain (e.g., IME cancel) AND we want the React synthetic onKeyDown to receive the event. Calling `preventDefault` after returning is moot; the current code only calls it when it fires a handler, and we preserve that.

## Conventions Established
- **Per-layer input-suppression flag**: `useRegisterEscapeLayer(priority, handler, active, { suppressWhenInputFocused: true })`. The fourth argument is an options object so we can extend without more positional params later. Default behavior (no options object) is unchanged.
- **When to set the flag**: if the registered target is a *panel/container* that hosts inline-edit inputs whose local `onKeyDown` already calls a cancel action on Escape. Do NOT set it for modals that auto-focus a field and expect registry-driven close.

## Files to Modify

### `internal/webui/frontend/src/hooks/ui/useKeyboardShortcuts.tsx`
1. Add an optional field to `Layer`:
   ```ts
   interface Layer {
     id: string;
     priority: number;
     handler: () => void;
     suppressWhenInputFocused: boolean; // default false; stored canonicalised
   }
   ```
2. Extend `EscapeRegistryAPI.registerLayer` signature:
   ```ts
   registerLayer: (
     priority: number,
     handler: () => void,
     suppressWhenInputFocused?: boolean,
   ) => string;
   ```
3. Update `handleEscapeKeyDown` (lines 123-129):
   ```ts
   function handleEscapeKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
     if (event.key !== "Escape") return;
     if (state.layers.length === 0) return;
     const top = state.layers[0];
     if (!top) return;
     if (top.suppressWhenInputFocused && isInputFocused(event)) return;
     event.preventDefault();
     top.handler();
   }
   ```
   Note: `preventDefault` is now only called after the suppress check (moved below the early-return), so a suppressed Escape reaches the component's React onKeyDown with `defaultPrevented` still false.
4. Update `registerLayer` implementation to store the flag with a default:
   ```ts
   registerLayer(priority, handler, suppressWhenInputFocused = false): string {
     const id = `layer-${++state.idCounter}`;
     state.layers.push({ id, priority, handler, suppressWhenInputFocused });
     ...
   }
   ```
5. Extend `useRegisterEscapeLayer` hook signature:
   ```ts
   export function useRegisterEscapeLayer(
     priority: number,
     handler: () => void,
     active: boolean,
     options?: { suppressWhenInputFocused?: boolean },
   ): void
   ```
   Pass `options?.suppressWhenInputFocused ?? false` through to `registry.registerLayer`. Re-register when this flag changes (add to effect deps).

### `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx` (line 1379)
Change:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL, onClose, isOpen);
```
to:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL, onClose, isOpen, {
  suppressWhenInputFocused: true,
});
```

### `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailView/IssueDetailView.tsx` (line 201)
Change:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL, handleEscapeBack, true);
```
to:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL, handleEscapeBack, true, {
  suppressWhenInputFocused: true,
});
```

### `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/AgentDetailPanel/AgentDetailPanel.tsx` (line 90)
Change:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_AGENT_PANEL, onClose, isOpen);
```
to:
```ts
useRegisterEscapeLayer(LAYER_AGENT_PANEL, onClose, isOpen, {
  suppressWhenInputFocused: true,
});
```
(This panel has inline inputs in `TargetBranchSelector`, `GitActionBar` PR form, `DiffFileRow` — all have local `if (e.key === 'Escape')` cancel handlers that suffer the same bubble bug today.)

## Files to Create
None.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)
Neighborhood scan results that exhibit the same pattern but are excluded from this fix:

- **`DesignPanel.tsx:98-110`** — attaches its own capture-phase `document.addEventListener("keydown")` to exit fullscreen and only calls `e.stopPropagation()` (not `stopImmediatePropagation`). Because both its capture listener and the registry's bubble listener are attached to `document`, stopPropagation does **not** prevent the bubble listener on the same element from firing. So pressing Escape in fullscreen design panel will still close the outer IssueDetailPanel. Not caused by our bug and not fixed by this task's approach (DesignPanel has no input, so `isInputFocused` returns false). Track separately.
- **`search/SearchInput.tsx:103`** — has its own Escape handler to clear the search box. Not inside any registered layer context that would be affected. No change needed.
- **Dropdown components** (RepoDropdown/OwnerDropdown/AssigneeDropdown/PriorityDropdown/TypeDropdown/LabelEditor inside IssueDetailPanel) — after this fix, their local Escape handlers close the dropdown as expected, and the panel stays open because LAYER_ISSUE_PANEL now suppresses when input is focused. Works correctly without per-component changes.
- **`TaskDrawer.tsx`** (LAYER_TERMINAL_PANEL) — no inline editing, no inputs inside the drawer. Leaving the flag off is correct: Escape closes the drawer regardless of focus.
- **Modals** (SessionNamePrompt/BackendPickerPrompt/CreateIssueModal/CreateWorkspaceModal/AssigneePrompt/MoveIssueDialog/ConfirmDialog) — intentionally leave flag off; these auto-focus a control and rely on the registry to close them.

## Dependencies
None. Pure frontend TS refactor inside `hooks/ui/useKeyboardShortcuts.tsx` plus three panel call-sites.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling
- **Focus on a non-input element inside a panel** (e.g., a focused button, the panel body itself): `isInputFocused` returns false → registry fires `onClose` → panel closes. Expected.
- **Focus on a <select>** inside an AgentDetailPanel: `isInputFocused` returns true (helper explicitly covers SELECT). Registry skips → select's native Escape behavior applies (typically does nothing). No regression because today's behavior for a focused select is to close the panel, which is also wrong-ish; the chosen behavior is "Escape does nothing when select is focused inside the panel," which matches the inline-edit UX goal.
- **Focus inside a CodeMirror or xterm instance** inside a panel: `isInputFocused` returns true (helper covers `.cm-editor` and `.xterm`). Registry skips. The terminal/editor handles Escape locally (xterm forwards it to PTY). This is desired — Escape in a terminal must NOT close the surrounding agent panel.
- **Focus completely outside the app** (e.g., browser chrome): event never reaches our listener. Not our concern.
- **Rapid re-focus** between an input and a button: each Escape keydown is a discrete event; focus at event-dispatch time determines behavior. No race.
- **A suppressed Escape must NOT fall through to the next-highest layer.** Explicit behavior: if top layer suppresses and input is focused, the registry returns; no lower layer is invoked. Rationale: the component's local onKeyDown is expected to handle it.
- **A suppressed Escape must NOT call `preventDefault`.** Rationale: we want the React synthetic event to be dispatched normally so the input's local onKeyDown runs. Move `event.preventDefault()` below the suppress check.
- **Flag change while layer is mounted**: treat `suppressWhenInputFocused` as a re-registration trigger — add it to the `useEffect` deps in `useRegisterEscapeLayer`. This matches how the hook already handles `priority` changes. Callers almost never change the flag dynamically, but the hook should be correct under that case.

## Acceptance Criteria
Behavioral assertions verifiable from the outside:

1. **Inline title edit cancel**: Open an issue panel → click the title to enter edit mode → press Escape. The title reverts to its pre-edit value and the input disappears (back to display mode). The panel remains open. URL/route unchanged.
2. **Inline description edit cancel**: Open an issue panel → click "Edit" on the description → type text → press Escape. The textarea disappears, the rendered markdown returns to the pre-edit content. The panel remains open.
3. **Panel close via Escape still works when no input is focused**: Open an issue panel → click somewhere on the panel background (not on any input/button) → press Escape. The panel closes.
4. **Modal close via Escape still works when input is focused**: Open the Create Issue modal (auto-focuses the title input) → without clicking elsewhere → press Escape. The modal closes.
5. **Session name prompt still closes on Escape from its input**: Open New Terminal Session modal → input auto-focuses → press Escape. The modal closes.
6. **Backend picker still closes on Escape from its focused select**: Open Backend Picker → select auto-focuses → press Escape. The modal closes.
7. **Agent panel inline PR form cancel**: Open an agent panel → click Create PR → type in target branch input → press Escape. The form closes; the agent panel remains open.
8. **Agent panel target branch selector cancel**: Open an agent panel → click to edit target branch → input focuses → press Escape. Input cancels; agent panel remains open.
9. **Dropdown close inside panel**: Open issue panel → open the Assignee dropdown (focuses its search input) → press Escape. Dropdown closes; panel remains open.
10. **Negative**: Pressing Escape from a focused input inside IssueDetailPanel does NOT call `onClose`.
11. **Negative**: Pressing Escape from a focused input inside CreateIssueModal does NOT fail to close the modal (unchanged existing behavior).
12. **No fall-through**: When IssueDetailPanel is the top layer with `suppressWhenInputFocused: true` and an input is focused, no lower-priority layer handler is invoked (e.g., keyboard cheatsheet does NOT open).

## Testing Strategy

### Unit tests (add to `hooks/ui/__tests__/useKeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx`)
New `describe("Escape layer registry — suppressWhenInputFocused")`:
- Top layer with `suppressWhenInputFocused: true` — Escape dispatched while focus is on an `<input type="text">` inside the provider → handler does NOT fire.
- Same setup, focus on a `<textarea>` → handler does NOT fire.
- Same setup, focus on a `<select>` → handler does NOT fire.
- Same setup, focus on a `<div role="button">` or body → handler DOES fire.
- Top layer with `suppressWhenInputFocused: false` (default) — Escape while input focused → handler fires (proves backward compatibility for modal behavior).
- Suppress top layer does NOT fall through: register two layers — top with suppress=true, lower with suppress=false. Focus an input, press Escape. Neither handler fires.
- Toggling the flag via re-render updates behavior (covers deps-array correctness).

### Component tests to update
- `IssueDetailPanel/__tests__/IssueDetailPanel.test.tsx` — the hoisted mock of `useRegisterEscapeLayer` currently asserts on `(priority, handler, active)`. Update the assertion to tolerate the new 4th `options` arg.
- `IssueDetailView/__tests__/IssueDetailView.test.tsx` — same update.
- `AgentDetailPanel/AgentDetailPanel.test.tsx` — same update.
- `EditableTitle/__tests__/EditableTitle.test.tsx` — add a test: render inside a `KeyboardShortcutProvider` with a mock panel layer (suppress=true, handler=spy), enter edit mode, dispatch a native keydown(Escape) on the input via userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}'), assert:
  (a) the component returns to display mode,
  (b) the mock panel handler was NOT called.
- `IssueDetailPanel/sections/__tests__/EditableDescription.test.tsx` — analogous test for the textarea.

### Manual verification
Start the dev UI; with the seeded session, walk through acceptance criteria 1–9 in a browser. Use the loom dev container (podman) if the local stack is already wired up — this is the validation-infra pattern documented in auto-memory.

- Open any issue with a title and description.
- Click title, type a change, press Escape → title reverts, panel stays open.
- Click Edit on description, type, press Escape → textarea disappears, panel stays open.
- Click outside inputs on panel body, press Escape → panel closes.
- Open Create Issue modal, press Escape from the title input → modal closes.
- Open an agent's detail panel, click the PR target branch input, press Escape → input cancels, panel stays open.

### Non-goals for testing
- DesignPanel fullscreen Escape behavior (out of scope; separate bug).
- xterm/CodeMirror Escape forwarding (unchanged; already handled locally).
close_reason: Fixed: Escape layer registry extended with per-layer suppressWhenInputFocused opt-in; inline-edit components now cancel locally without closing the panel. Live-verified in browser (loom dev container): title edit→Escape returns to display mode with panel open; Escape with non-input focus still closes panel. Unit test suite +12 tests including deps-array correctness and regression fix for IssueDetailView reject textarea local Escape.
