title: Fix double time.Sleep in monitor watch loop causing 2x refresh interval
description: monitor.go has two time.Sleep calls in the watch loop (lines 207 and 220), causing the actual refresh interval to be double the configured value (10s default instead of 5s). Remove the second time.Sleep on line 220.
design:
## Summary

The monitor watch loop in monitor.go has two time.Sleep calls (lines 207 and 220), causing the actual refresh interval to be double the configured value. With the default 5-second interval, the dashboard only refreshes every 10 seconds. The second time.Sleep on line 220 is redundant and should be removed.

## Technical Approach

Remove the second time.Sleep on line 220. The first time.Sleep at line 207 (at the top of the for loop) is sufficient — it pauses before each data collection cycle, which is the standard pattern for a polling loop. The second sleep at line 220 (at the bottom of the loop, after rendering) creates a double-wait.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

1. **internal/cli/monitor.go** (line 220):
   - Remove: \`time.Sleep(time.Duration(monitorInterval) * time.Second)\`
   - This is the second sleep at the bottom of the watch loop (line 220). The first sleep at line 207 remains.

## Dependencies

None.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- No edge cases — this simply removes a redundant sleep call
- The loop structure remains sound: sleep → collect → render → (loop back to sleep)
- The initial data collection before the loop (line 196) is unaffected, so the first render still happens immediately on startup

## Testing Strategy

- Run existing tests: \`go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestMonitor -v\`
- Manual verification: run \`loom watch\` with default settings and confirm refreshes happen every ~5 seconds instead of ~10 seconds
- The watch loop isn't directly unit tested (it's an infinite loop with terminal I/O), so this is primarily a manual verification
close_reason: Removed redundant time.Sleep at bottom of watch loop. Tests pass, code review clean.

title: [e2e-audit] table.md — verify passing assertions have Playwright coverage
description: For each passing assertion from the table.md validation report: search existing Playwright specs (table-sort.spec.ts, journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts) and Go tests for coverage. Record covered/uncovered per VAL-ID. Create sub-tickets for uncovered. Deliverable: reports/e2e-audit-table.json
design:
## Summary

Audit the 59 passing assertions from `reports/validation-table.json` (in the nova worktree) against all existing Playwright E2E specs and Go tests to determine which behavioral assertions already have automated test coverage. Produce `reports/e2e-audit-table.json` recording covered/uncovered per VAL-ID, and create sub-tickets (beads issues) for each uncovered group of passing assertions that need new Playwright tests.

This task follows the conventions established by loomcli-ot68r (kanban e2e-audit).

## Technical Approach

The agent will:
1. Read the validation report from `reports/validation-table.json` located in the nova worktree at `/Users/tyson/codebase/code-agents/loomcli/worktrees/nova/reports/validation-table.json`. Filter to only `status: "pass"` assertions (59 total).
2. For each passing assertion, search the Playwright spec files and Go test files listed below for test(s) that exercise the same behavior.
3. Classify each assertion as `covered`, `partial`, or `uncovered` per the conventions from loomcli-ot68r.
4. Write the audit report to `reports/e2e-audit-table.json`.
5. Create beads sub-tickets for uncovered/partial assertions grouped by behavioral category.

**Matching methodology**: Same as loomcli-ot68r. A test "covers" an assertion if it exercises the same user-visible behavior and checks the same output. Partial means related behavior is tested but not all evidence criteria. Do NOT count view-switcher or nav-rail tests as coverage for table-specific behavioral assertions (they only confirm the table view renders, not its behavior).

## Conventions Established

None new — follows all conventions from loomcli-ot68r (report schema, classification rules, sub-ticket naming).

## Files to Create

1. **`reports/e2e-audit-table.json`** — The audit report following the schema from loomcli-ot68r. Contains one entry per passing assertion with coverage classification.

## Files to Modify

None — this is a pure analysis/reporting task. No source code changes.

## Out of Scope

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. This task only reads spec files and validation reports; it does not modify them.

## Dependencies

- **Validation report**: `reports/validation-table.json` in the nova worktree (`/Users/tyson/codebase/code-agents/loomcli/worktrees/nova/reports/validation-table.json`). Copy it to the local worktree's `reports/` dir before processing, or read from nova directly.

- **Primary spec files** (all under `internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/`):
  - `table-sort.spec.ts` (460 lines) — sort cycling, indicators, keyboard header sort, accessibility, empty table
  - `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` (373 lines) — priority/status sort, row selection, bulk toolbar, deselect all

- **Secondary spec files** (may cover ancillary table assertions):
  - `issue-detail-panel.spec.ts` — "Table View" section: clicking table row opens panel, close methods
  - `view-switcher.spec.ts` — table tab renders IssueTable (not behavioral coverage)
  - `filter.spec.ts` — combined search+priority across kanban/table (limited)
  - `search-filter-journey.spec.ts` — navigates to table, verifies table renders
  - `assembled-views.spec.ts` — kanban↔table filter persistence, table row click to detail panel
  - `server-push.spec.ts` — SSE lifecycle (not table-specific)
  - `skeleton.spec.ts` — kanban skeleton loading (not table loading)

- **Go test files**:
  - `internal/webui/handlers/issues/issues_test.go` — handleListIssues handler tests (backend, not E2E)

## Pre-computed Coverage Map

Based on thorough analysis of all spec files, here is the expected mapping. The implementation agent MUST verify each by reading the actual spec files.

### Covered (15 assertions)

| VAL-ID | Spec File | Test Name | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| VAL-FE-TABLE-002 | table-sort.spec.ts, journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | getRowIds helper used in sort tests | Both specs verify ID cells contain exact issue IDs in sort-order checks |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-014 | table-sort.spec.ts | "third click clears sort" | Explicitly tests asc→desc→none cycle with aria-sort and indicator text |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-015 | table-sort.spec.ts | "only one column shows sorted at a time" | Verifies sorted class on active column, not on previous |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-019 | table-sort.spec.ts, journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Sort by Priority" tests | Both verify numeric sort P0→P4 ascending, P4→P0 descending |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-022 | table-sort.spec.ts, journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "only one column shows sorted" / "resets priority header" | Clicking new column removes sort from previous |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-024 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Select issues via row checkboxes" | Uses `getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Select issue sort-001" })` confirming checkbox column exists |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-025 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Select issues via row checkboxes" | Clicks checkbox, verifies `toBeChecked()` state toggles |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-029 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Select issues via row checkboxes" | Checks "1 selected" and "2 selected" text on bulk toolbar |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-031 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Clear selection via toolbar button" | Clicks deselect-all, verifies checkboxes unchecked and toolbar hidden |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-033 | issue-detail-panel.spec.ts | "clicking table row opens panel" (Table View section) | Clicks table row, verifies panel opens with data-state="open" and correct issue ID |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-034 | issue-detail-panel.spec.ts | "clicking table row opens panel" | Verifies panel displays correct issue ID (panel-test-1) from the clicked row |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-053 | table-sort.spec.ts | "sorting with empty table displays empty message" | Mocks empty response, verifies `issue-table-empty` testID is visible |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-064 | table-sort.spec.ts | "aria-label describes sort state" | Verifies aria-label includes "currently sorted ascending/descending" |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-066 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | "Select issues via row checkboxes" | `getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Select issue sort-001" })` confirms labels identify the row |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-067 | table-sort.spec.ts | Keyboard Navigation + Accessibility sections | Enter/Space trigger sort, Tab navigates headers, headers have role=button |

### Partial (6 assertions)

| VAL-ID | Spec File | What's Covered | What's Missing |
|--------|-----------|----------------|----------------|
| VAL-FE-TABLE-001 | table-sort.spec.ts | Verifies 5 sortable columns (id, priority, title, status, issue_type) have aria-sort | Does NOT verify all default columns exist (SELECT, BLOCKED, ASSIGNEE, REPO, UPDATED columns not checked) |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-003 | table-sort.spec.ts | getRowTitles verifies title text renders correctly in sort tests | Search box filtering and highlight behavior not tested |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-004 | table-sort.spec.ts | Status column sorts correctly (sorted by string: closed < in_progress < open) | Badge styling, colored chips, status-specific CSS classes not verified |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-005 | journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts | Priority column sorts numerically P0-P4 | P0-P4 badge rendering and color-coding not explicitly checked |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-006 | table-sort.spec.ts | Type column sorts alphabetically (bug, chore, task) | Rendered type names (capitalized Task, Bug, Feature, Epic) not verified |
| VAL-FE-TABLE-035 | table-sort.spec.ts | Enter/Space tested on column HEADERS | Enter/Space not tested on table ROWS to trigger row click/detail panel |

### Uncovered (38 assertions)

**Column rendering & display (4):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-007: Assignee column shows assignee name or dash for unassigned
- VAL-FE-TABLE-008: Updated column shows relative date
- VAL-FE-TABLE-011: Null/empty field renders placeholder (dash or empty)
- VAL-FE-TABLE-012: Extremely long title truncates gracefully with ellipsis

**Sort edge cases (4):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-017: Sorting null/empty values: sort to end (asc) or beginning (desc)
- VAL-FE-TABLE-018: String sort is case-insensitive
- VAL-FE-TABLE-021: Sort state persists after filter/search change
- VAL-FE-TABLE-023: Sorting is stable — rows with equal values maintain original order

**Selection (3):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-028: Clicking row (non-checkbox) does not toggle selection
- VAL-FE-TABLE-030: Selection survives sort/filter changes
- VAL-FE-TABLE-036: Row highlight shows visual feedback when selected

**Virtual scrolling (7):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-038: Small list (< 100 rows) renders all rows statically
- VAL-FE-TABLE-039: Large list (> 100 rows) uses virtual scrolling
- VAL-FE-TABLE-040: Virtual scroll with 1000 issues maintains 60 fps
- VAL-FE-TABLE-041: Virtualized row rendering uses spacer rows for scroll height
- VAL-FE-TABLE-042: Row height is consistent and estimated correctly
- VAL-FE-TABLE-043: Scrolling to bottom loads/shows all remaining rows
- VAL-FE-TABLE-044: Overscan buffer ensures smooth scroll without visible gaps

**SSE real-time updates in table context (8):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-045: New issue added via SSE appears as new row
- VAL-FE-TABLE-046: Existing issue updated via SSE updates row in place
- VAL-FE-TABLE-047: Issue deleted via SSE removes row
- VAL-FE-TABLE-048: Live updates respect current sort order
- VAL-FE-TABLE-049: Live updates don't clear user selection
- VAL-FE-TABLE-050: SSE connection state displayed
- VAL-FE-TABLE-051: SSE reconnect with exponential backoff
- VAL-FE-TABLE-052: SSE catch-up: events since last ID are replayed on reconnect

**Loading states (2):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-054: Loading skeleton during initial data fetch
- VAL-FE-TABLE-055: Loading state persists until first data arrives

**Edge cases & robustness (6):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-071: Long assignee names truncate or wrap without breaking layout
- VAL-FE-TABLE-072: Issue with all fields null/empty renders without errors
- VAL-FE-TABLE-073: Sorting with mixed data types (null and string)
- VAL-FE-TABLE-074: Search term with regex special characters
- VAL-FE-TABLE-076: Rapidly toggling sort clicks does not cause race conditions
- VAL-FE-TABLE-078: High-frequency SSE updates don't cause flickering
- VAL-FE-TABLE-079: Issue created and immediately deleted via SSE

**Performance (3):**
- VAL-FE-TABLE-207: Sort of 1000 rows completes in <200ms
- VAL-FE-TABLE-208: Sort is stable for equal keys
- VAL-FE-TABLE-209: Large dataset sort does not block user input

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **Validation report not found**: If the report doesn't exist at the expected nova worktree path, abort with error message identifying the missing file path. Do NOT fabricate data.
- **Ambiguous coverage**: When a test covers part of an assertion but not all criteria, classify as `partial` and document what's missing in the `notes` field. Never round up to `covered`.
- **Duplicate coverage**: If multiple spec files cover the same assertion, list all matching spec files and test names. Pick the strongest match for the primary classification.
- **SSE assertions (050-052)**: server-push.spec.ts tests SSE lifecycle generically (not table-specific). Do NOT count these as coverage for TABLE-specific SSE assertions. The contract asks about SSE behavior *within the table view* — general SSE tests exercise a different code path (typically kanban view).
- **Performance assertions (207-209)**: These need specialized performance testing approaches. Classify as `uncovered` and note that standard Playwright assertions cannot meaningfully verify fps or sub-200ms timing.
- **View-switcher/assembled-views tests**: These verify the table *renders* when switching views but do not exercise table-specific behavior (sorting, selection, virtual scroll). Do NOT count as coverage for functional assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `reports/e2e-audit-table.json` exists and is valid JSON conforming to the schema from loomcli-ot68r
2. The report contains exactly 59 entries (one per passing assertion from the validation report)
3. Every entry has `id`, `title`, `coverage` (one of: covered, partial, uncovered), `spec_files` (array, may be empty), `test_names` (array, may be empty), and `notes` (string explaining the classification)
4. The `summary` object has correct counts: `total_passing` = 59, `covered + partial + uncovered` = 59, `coverage_pct` = `covered / total_passing * 100` rounded to 1 decimal
5. No assertion is classified as `covered` unless the agent verified by reading the spec file that a test explicitly exercises the behavior
6. Sub-tickets are created for all `uncovered` and `partial` assertion groups, with title format `[e2e-gap] table: <description>`, type=task, priority=3, parent=loomcli-umzyd
7. Sub-tickets are grouped by category (aim for 8-12 sub-tickets, not 44+): column rendering, sort edge cases, selection gaps, virtual scrolling, SSE in table, loading states, edge cases, performance
8. The report file is committed to the local worktree (not pushed)

## Testing Strategy

- **Self-check**: After generating the report, verify `assertions` array length equals 59 and that summary counts sum correctly (`covered + partial + uncovered == 59`)
- **Spot-check**: For 3-5 `covered` assertions, manually verify the referenced spec file and test name actually test the claimed behavior (e.g., read table-sort.spec.ts line for VAL-FE-TABLE-014)
- **Completeness check**: Cross-reference all 59 passing VAL-IDs from the validation report against the report's assertion IDs — ensure zero omissions
- **Sub-ticket check**: Verify each sub-ticket references specific VAL-IDs and has actionable descriptions

title: T10: Update reset and recover for workspace mode
description: reset.go: loom reset falcon resets all repos in workspace to their integration branches. recover.go: check git logs across ALL repos in workspace when analyzing orphaned tasks, clear lock at workspace level. Legacy unchanged. Files: modify reset.go, recover.go. Depends on T2, T5.
design:
## Summary

This task updates reset.go and recover.go to work correctly in workspace mode, where a single workspace contains multiple repos sharing one lock. In legacy mode (no config), behavior is unchanged. In workspace mode: `loom reset <workspace>` resets ALL repos in the workspace to their integration branches; `loom recover <workspace>` checks git logs across ALL repos when analyzing orphaned tasks, and clears the lock at the workspace level (using ResolveLockDir).

## Technical Approach

Both files already use the free function wrappers (DiscoverWorktrees, ResolveWorktreePath, CheckLock) which, in the falcon worktree, delegate to the Resolver and ResolveLockDir abstractions. The key changes are:

**reset.go**: In workspace mode, `loom reset <name>` should resolve via the Resolver (which already handles workspace repos). The `resetAllWorktrees` function already calls `DiscoverWorktrees()` which in workspace mode returns all repos in the workspace. The main change is:
1. Each repo in a workspace may have its own default/integration branch (from RepoConfig.DefaultBranch), so when resetting all, each repo should reset to its own integration branch rather than a single global target branch.
2. Update command help text to mention workspace mode.

**recover.go**: The main changes are:
1. `forceReleaseLock` must use `ResolveLockDir` to find the correct lock location (workspace root vs worktree path). Currently it hardcodes `filepath.Join(worktreePath, LockFileName)`.
2. `analyzeTaskCompletion` currently runs `git log` in a single worktreePath. In workspace mode, it should search git logs across ALL repos in the workspace to find commits mentioning the task ID, giving Claude a complete picture.
3. `cleanUntrackedFiles` should clean across all repos in the workspace, not just one path.
4. Update command help text to mention workspace mode.

**Design decisions:**
- Use the existing Resolver (via `getDefaultResolver()`) for discovery — no new abstractions needed.
- For `analyzeTaskCompletion`, aggregate git log output from all workspace repos into a single prompt. This gives Claude the best chance of finding relevant commits.
- For `forceReleaseLock`, simply use `ResolveLockDir(worktreePath)` — one-line fix.
- For `cleanUntrackedFiles` in workspace mode, iterate over all discovered repos and clean each one.
- Legacy mode (no config) is unchanged in all cases.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/cli/reset.go` (and `worktrees/falcon/internal/cli/reset.go`)

**a) `resetAllWorktrees(targetBranch string)`**:
- In workspace mode, when resetting "all", use each repo's configured `DefaultBranch` (from `WorktreeInfo.Repo.DefaultBranch`) if available, falling back to the provided `targetBranch` argument.
- Update the summary output to show per-repo target branches when they differ.

**b) `runReset` function**:
- When in workspace mode and a workspace name is given (not a single repo), detect this and handle accordingly. Since `ResolveWorktreePath` already handles workspace repo names, and `DiscoverWorktrees` returns workspace repos, the existing `--all` flow mostly works. The key change is per-repo branch handling.

**c) Command help text**:
- Add workspace examples: `loom reset --all  # In workspace mode, resets all repos to their integration branches`

### 2. `internal/cli/recover.go` (and `worktrees/falcon/internal/cli/recover.go`)

**a) `forceReleaseLock(worktreePath string) error`**:
- Change from `filepath.Join(worktreePath, LockFileName)` to `filepath.Join(ResolveLockDir(worktreePath), LockFileName)`.
- This ensures the workspace-level lock is cleared, not a nonexistent per-repo lock.

**b) `analyzeTaskCompletion(worktreePath, taskID string)`**:
- Add workspace-aware git log search:
  - Call `DiscoverWorktrees()` (or `getDefaultResolver().DiscoverWorktrees()`)
  - If in workspace mode (resolver.Mode() == ModeWorkspace), run `git log --oneline -20 --all --grep <taskID>` in EACH repo path
  - Aggregate all git log output with repo name labels into the Claude prompt
  - If in legacy mode, keep current behavior (single repo git log)

**c) `cleanUntrackedFiles(worktreePath string, force bool)`**:
- In workspace mode, iterate over all repos from `DiscoverWorktrees()` and run `GitCleanDryRun` / `GitClean` on each.
- Show untracked files grouped by repo name.
- In legacy mode, keep current behavior.

**d) `runRecover` function**:
- When in workspace mode, the argument is a workspace name (or repo name). The Resolver handles this.
- After clearing the lock, clean untracked files across all repos in the workspace.
- The orphaned task analysis already uses the worktreePath parameter, which is fine for the `bd` commands. The git log aggregation in `analyzeTaskCompletion` handles the multi-repo search.

**e) Command help text**:
- Update Long description and examples to mention workspace mode.
- Add example: `loom recover myworkspace  # Recover workspace-level agent`

## Files to Create

No new files needed. All changes are modifications to existing files.

## Dependencies

- T2 (WorkspaceResolver) — DONE in falcon worktree. Provides Resolver, DiscoverWorktrees (workspace-aware), ModeWorkspace/ModeLegacy.
- T5 (Workspace-level lock) — DONE in falcon worktree. Provides ResolveLockDir, resolveWorkspaceName, workspace-aware lock functions.
- T1 (Config) — DONE. Provides LoomConfig, RepoConfig, LoadConfig.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Mixed workspace/legacy**: If no config exists, all behavior is identical to current code. The Resolver falls back to legacy mode.
2. **Partial repo failures in reset**: If one repo in a workspace fails to reset, continue with the others (current behavior for --all already does this).
3. **Partial repo failures in recover**: If git log fails in one repo, skip it and continue. Don't let one bad repo prevent recovery.
4. **Empty workspace (no repos)**: Handle gracefully — "No repos found in workspace" message.
5. **Lock at workspace level**: forceReleaseLock using ResolveLockDir ensures the shared lock is found even when called with a specific repo path.
6. **analyzeTaskCompletion with no commits**: If no commits found in any repo, report as incomplete (same as current behavior).

## Testing Strategy

### Unit tests
- Test `forceReleaseLock` with workspace paths (verifies ResolveLockDir usage).
- Test that `analyzeTaskCompletion` aggregates logs from multiple repos (mock execCommand).
- Test `cleanUntrackedFiles` iterates over workspace repos.

### Manual verification
1. **Legacy mode**: Run `loom reset --all` and `loom recover falcon` — verify identical behavior to current.
2. **Workspace mode**: 
   - Create config.yaml with workspace containing 2 repos
   - Run `loom reset --all` — verify both repos reset to their respective integration branches
   - Simulate crash (kill agent, leave stale lock at workspace root)
   - Run `loom recover <workspace>` — verify lock cleared at workspace root, git logs checked across both repos
3. **Mixed**: Verify that a repo-level argument in workspace mode still works (resolves through Resolver).

title: CLI E2E: loom daemon lifecycle
description: labels: e2e,cli,P3
design:
## Summary

This task creates a Go-based CLI E2E test file for the \`loom daemon\` lifecycle commands. The test validates that the daemon binary can start, report status, prevent concurrent instances, stop gracefully, and handle SIGTERM — all as subprocess invocations of the real \`loom\` binary with stub backends. This complements existing unit tests (which test internal functions like \`isLoomDaemonRunning\`, \`computeBackoff\`, \`shouldRestart\`) and the shell-based scripts in \`docs/testing/daemon-e2e/\` by providing a structured, repeatable Go test that runs inside the container E2E pipeline.

## Technical Approach

**Pattern**: Follow the existing \`automode_e2e_test.go\` pattern. Use a \`//go:build e2e\` build tag. Each test spawns \`loom daemon\` as a real subprocess in an isolated temp directory with a minimal \`loom.yaml\` config using the stub backend. Tests validate process lifecycle via PID files, exit codes, stdout/stderr output, and signal handling.

**Command structure** (verified from daemon_cmd.go):
- \`loom daemon\` — starts the supervisor in the foreground (there is NO \`start\` subcommand)
- \`loom daemon status\` — shows daemon and agent status
- \`loom daemon stop\` — stops the running daemon
- \`loom daemon --dry-run\` — validates config and prints what would be started

**Key design decisions**:
- Use \`os/exec\` to spawn \`loom daemon\` as a background process
- Create a minimal git repo + worktree setup in \`t.TempDir()\` per test so tests are fully isolated
- Use the stub backends (\`claude\` stub from \`e2e/stubs/claude\`) via PATH manipulation so daemon can spawn agents
- Set \`STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT_CODE=0\` and \`STUB_CLAUDE_DELAY=30\` so agents stay alive long enough for lifecycle assertions
- Use short timeouts (backoff_initial=1, backoff_max=1, max_retries=0) so tests complete quickly
- Parallel-safe: each test uses its own temp directory and unique PID file paths

**Trade-offs**:
- Go subprocess tests vs shell scripts: Go tests integrate with \`go test\`, provide better assertions, run in CI. Shell scripts remain for manual testing.
- Real binary vs in-process: Using the real compiled binary ensures CLI arg parsing, signal handling, and process isolation are tested end-to-end.

## Conventions Established

This is the first CLI E2E test for daemon commands. Establishes:
- Helper function \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\` that creates a temp dir with git repo, worktree, and minimal loom.yaml
- All output assertions use exact substrings from the actual code (verified against daemon_cmd.go and daemon_run_helpers.go)
- Daemon processes are always cleaned up via \`t.Cleanup\` with process-group kill

### Exact Output Strings (verified from source code)

These are the authoritative output patterns tests must match:

| Context | Exact output string | Source |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Already running | \`Error: daemon already running (lock held on <lockFilePath>)\` (stderr, exit 1) | daemon_cmd.go:169 |
| Status: running | \`Daemon: running (PID <pid>)\` (capital D) | daemon_cmd.go:314 |
| Status: not running | \`Daemon: not running\` | daemon_cmd.go:310 |
| Stop: success | \`Daemon stopped.\` (with period) | daemon_cmd.go:396 |
| Stop: not running | \`Daemon is not running.\` (with period) | daemon_cmd.go:380 |
| Stop: starting | \`Stopping daemon (PID <pid>)...\` | daemon_cmd.go:384 |
| Shutdown signal | \`Shutting down...\` | daemon_cmd.go:281 |
| Shutdown complete | \`Daemon stopped.\` | daemon_cmd.go:284 |
| Dry-run banner | \`DRY RUN - No daemon will be started\` | daemon_run_helpers.go:78 |
| Dry-run agent | \`- <worktree> (role: <role>, auto: <bool>)\` | daemon_run_helpers.go:107 |
| Startup banner | \`Loom Agent Supervisor\` | daemon_cmd.go:240 |

## Files to Create

### \`internal/cli/daemon_e2e_test.go\`
Main E2E test file (~350 lines).

**Build tag**: \`//go:build e2e\`
**Package**: \`cli\`

**Helper functions**:

- \`setupDaemonTestDir(t *testing.T) string\` — Creates a fully isolated test environment:
  1. Creates \`t.TempDir()\` as the project root
  2. Runs \`git init\` and \`git commit --allow-empty -m "init"\` in it
  3. Creates a worktree: \`git worktree add ./worktrees/stub -b stub\`
  4. Creates \`loom.yaml\` with one agent: worktree=stub, role=task, auto=true, plus daemon settings: max_retries=0, backoff_initial=1, backoff_max=1
  5. Creates \`.loom/logs\` directory
  6. Returns the temp dir path

- \`startDaemon(t *testing.T, dir string, extraArgs ...string) (*exec.Cmd, *bytes.Buffer, *bytes.Buffer)\` — Starts \`loom daemon\` as a subprocess:
  1. Builds \`exec.Command("loom", "daemon", extraArgs...)\` with \`Dir\` set to the test dir
  2. Sets PATH to include \`e2e/stubs/\` directory (for claude stub) plus original PATH
  3. Sets \`STUB_CLAUDE_DELAY=30\` so agents stay alive for lifecycle testing
  4. Sets \`STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT_CODE=0\`
  5. Captures stdout and stderr into \`bytes.Buffer\`
  6. Starts the process
  7. Registers \`t.Cleanup\` that kills the process group (negative PID via \`syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)\`) if still running
  8. Returns the Cmd, stdout buffer, stderr buffer

- \`waitForPIDFile(t *testing.T, pidFilePath string, timeout time.Duration) int\` — Polls for PID file creation:
  1. Polls every 200ms until file exists and contains a valid PID > 0
  2. Returns the PID
  3. Calls \`t.Fatalf\` on timeout

- \`runLoomDaemon(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) (stdout, stderr string, exitCode int)\` — Runs \`loom daemon <args>\` synchronously:
  1. Builds \`exec.Command("loom", append([]string{"daemon"}, args...)...)\` with \`Dir=dir\`
  2. Captures stdout/stderr
  3. Runs and returns output + exit code (0 on success, nonzero on error)

- \`requireLoomBinary(t *testing.T)\` — Skips test if \`loom\` binary not on PATH

**Test functions (7 tests)**:

1. **\`TestE2E_DaemonDryRun\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\` to get test dir
   - Run \`runLoomDaemon(t, dir, "--dry-run")\`
   - Assert exit code == 0
   - Assert stdout contains \`"DRY RUN - No daemon will be started"\`
   - Assert stdout contains \`"stub (role: task, auto: true)"\` (the configured agent)
   - Assert stdout contains \`"PID file:"\` and \`"State file:"\`
   - Assert \`.loom/daemon.pid\` does NOT exist in test dir

2. **\`TestE2E_DaemonStartCreatesPIDFile\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\` to get test dir
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\` to launch daemon in background
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, ".loom/daemon.pid"), 15*time.Second)\`
   - Read PID from file, verify PID > 0
   - Verify process is running via \`syscall.Kill(pid, 0)\` — expect nil error
   - (Cleanup: automatic via t.Cleanup registered in startDaemon)

3. **\`TestE2E_DaemonStatusShowsRunning\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\`
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\` to launch daemon
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, ..., 15*time.Second)\` to get PID
   - Run \`runLoomDaemon(t, dir, "status")\`
   - Assert exit code == 0
   - Assert stdout contains \`"Daemon: running (PID"\` (capital D, exact format from daemon_cmd.go:314)
   - Assert stdout contains the PID number as a substring

4. **\`TestE2E_DaemonConcurrentStartBlocked\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\`
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\` to launch first daemon
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, ..., 15*time.Second)\`
   - Run \`runLoomDaemon(t, dir)\` (no extra args — this IS the start command) — this attempts a second daemon
   - Assert exit code != 0 (should be 1)
   - Assert stderr contains \`"daemon already running (lock held on"\` (exact string from daemon_cmd.go:169)
   - (Cleanup: automatic via t.Cleanup)

5. **\`TestE2E_DaemonStop\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\`
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\` to launch daemon
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, ..., 15*time.Second)\`
   - Run \`runLoomDaemon(t, dir, "stop")\`
   - Assert exit code == 0
   - Assert stdout contains \`"Stopping daemon (PID"\` (from daemon_cmd.go:384)
   - Assert stdout contains \`"Daemon stopped."\` (with period, from daemon_cmd.go:396)
   - Wait up to 5s for PID file to be removed (the daemon's defer removes it)
   - Run \`runLoomDaemon(t, dir, "status")\`
   - Assert stdout contains \`"Daemon: not running"\`

6. **\`TestE2E_DaemonSIGTERMCleanShutdown\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\`
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\` to get cmd and stdout buffer
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, ..., 15*time.Second)\` to get PID
   - Send \`syscall.SIGTERM\` to the daemon PID (\`syscall.Kill(pid, syscall.SIGTERM)\`)
   - Wait up to 15s for process to exit (poll with \`cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.Signal(0))\` or check ProcessState)
   - Assert process exited (if not within 15s, \`t.Fatalf\`)
   - Wait up to 2s for PID file to be removed
   - Assert PID file does not exist
   - Assert stdout buffer contains \`"Daemon stopped."\` (with period, from daemon_cmd.go:284)

7. **\`TestE2E_DaemonStateFileUpdated\`**:
   - Call \`requireLoomBinary(t)\`
   - Call \`setupDaemonTestDir(t)\`
   - Call \`startDaemon(t, dir)\`
   - Call \`waitForPIDFile(t, ..., 15*time.Second)\` to get PID
   - Wait for \`.loom/daemon-agents.json\` to appear (poll up to 20s — state updates every 5s, so first write may take up to ~10s after startup)
   - Read and parse JSON into a struct with fields: \`PID int\`, \`StartedAt time.Time\`, \`Agents []struct{Worktree, Role, Status string}\`
   - Assert \`state.PID\` equals the PID from the PID file
   - Assert \`len(state.Agents) == 1\`
   - Assert \`state.Agents[0].Worktree == "stub"\`
   - Assert \`state.Agents[0].Role == "task"\`
   - Assert \`state.StartedAt\` is not zero
   - (Cleanup: automatic via t.Cleanup)

## Files to Modify

None. This is a new test file with the \`e2e\` build tag, so it won't affect regular \`go test ./...\` runs.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. The only existing E2E test file is \`automode_e2e_test.go\` which tests tmux session lifecycle, not daemon commands.

## Dependencies

- **External**: None new. Uses existing \`loom\` binary (must be built before running E2E tests), stub backends from \`e2e/stubs/\`.
- **Internal**: \`os/exec\`, \`encoding/json\`, \`syscall\`, \`path/filepath\`, \`testing\`, \`time\`, \`os\`, \`strings\`, \`strconv\`, \`bytes\`
- **Prerequisites**: The \`loom\` binary must be compiled and on PATH. The stub backends must be in PATH. This is handled by the E2E test infrastructure.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Race condition on PID file**: Use polling with 200ms interval and generous timeout (15s) rather than fixed sleep. The \`waitForPIDFile\` helper handles this.
2. **Zombie processes**: Each test defers a cleanup function that sends SIGKILL to the daemon's process group (negative PID), ensuring child agents are also terminated. The cleanup runs even if the test panics.
3. **Lock/PID file conflicts**: Each test uses its own \`t.TempDir()\`, so lock files don't conflict between parallel tests.
4. **Slow CI**: All wait timeouts are generous (15-20s) but tests should complete in <5s normally.
5. **Binary not found**: Skip tests with \`t.Skip("loom binary not found")\` if \`exec.LookPath("loom")\` fails.
6. **Stale processes from failed tests**: The \`t.Cleanup\` function kills the daemon process group (negative PID) to ensure child agents are also terminated. Use \`syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL)\` which kills the entire process group.
7. **Git worktree setup**: \`setupDaemonTestDir\` must create a valid git repo with at least one commit and a worktree for the stub agent. Without the commit, \`git worktree add\` fails. The worktree directory must exist at \`worktrees/stub\` relative to the project root.
8. **State file timing**: The daemon writes the initial state file synchronously during startup (daemon_cmd.go:258), then a goroutine updates it every 5s. But the initial write happens BEFORE \`daemon.Start()\` at line 258, so the state file should appear shortly after the PID file. Poll up to 20s to be safe.
9. **Process group isolation**: The daemon calls \`syscall.Setpgid(0, 0)\` at startup, creating its own process group. Our cleanup must target this PID (not our own PGID) with \`syscall.Kill(pid, SIGKILL)\`.
10. **Stop command when not running**: \`loom daemon stop\` prints \`"Daemon is not running."\` to stdout (NOT stderr) and exits with code 0 (no error). This is intentional — stopping an already-stopped daemon is not an error.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. \`go test -tags=e2e -run TestE2E_Daemon ./internal/cli/\` passes with all 7 tests green
2. \`loom daemon --dry-run\` produces output containing "DRY RUN" and does NOT create a PID file
3. \`loom daemon\` creates a PID file at \`.loom/daemon.pid\` containing the daemon's actual PID
4. \`loom daemon status\` outputs \`"Daemon: running (PID <N>)"\` when daemon is running
5. \`loom daemon status\` outputs \`"Daemon: not running"\` when daemon is stopped
6. A second \`loom daemon\` invocation while one is already running prints \`"daemon already running (lock held on ..."\` to stderr and exits with code 1
7. \`loom daemon stop\` outputs \`"Daemon stopped."\` (with period) and the PID file is removed
8. Sending SIGTERM to the daemon PID causes clean shutdown, PID file removal, and \`"Daemon stopped."\` in output
9. The state file \`.loom/daemon-agents.json\` is created and contains valid JSON with the daemon PID and agent entries
10. Tests MUST NOT leave zombie daemon processes — verify \`t.Cleanup\` kills process groups
11. Regular \`go test ./internal/cli/\` (without -tags=e2e) MUST NOT run these tests

## Testing Strategy

**How to run**:
\`\`\`bash
# Build binary first
make build

# Run just daemon lifecycle E2E tests
go test -tags=e2e -timeout=2m -run TestE2E_Daemon ./internal/cli/

# Run all E2E tests
go test -tags=e2e -timeout=5m ./internal/cli/

# Run in Docker container (full pipeline)
e2e/run_local.sh -- --phase e2e
\`\`\`

**Key scenarios covered**:
1. Dry-run mode validates config without starting daemon (flag validation)
2. Daemon starts and creates PID file (process management)
3. Daemon reports accurate status with correct format (status command)
4. Only one daemon instance allowed via lock file (concurrency prevention)
5. Daemon stops cleanly via \`loom daemon stop\` (stop command)
6. Daemon handles SIGTERM gracefully (signal handling)
7. State file is written with correct structure (state persistence)

**Manual verification**:
- Run the tests locally with \`-v\` flag to see detailed output
- Compare results with the shell-based tests in \`docs/testing/daemon-e2e/test-daemon-lifecycle.sh\`
- Verify no zombie processes remain after test suite completes: \`ps aux | grep loom\`

**What is NOT covered (by design — these belong to other tasks)**:
- Agent execution and task completion (test-agent-execution.sh scope)
- Epic assignment and exhaustion (separate task)
- Backend failover (separate task)
- Config hot-reload (separate task)
- Health check watchdog (tested at unit level in daemon_lifecycle_test.go)

title: Agent Logs tab and Issue Planning tab show garbled ANSI escape sequences
description:
Both the Agent detail panel Logs tab AND the Issue detail panel Planning tab show garbled raw terminal output:

1. **Agent Logs tab**: Shows raw tmux scrollback with sequential line numbers (140555, 140556...), unprocessed ANSI escape sequences ('[?2026l [?2026h [6A•'), and mostly blank lines. The actual agent activity is buried in noise.

2. **Issue Planning tab** (Needs Review cards): Same problem — shows raw terminal session output with line numbers (9009, 9010...) and garbled escape codes ('[2C▸▸ [1Cbypass [1Cpermissions...') instead of the structured design/plan content. This tab should show the design field content (the plan written by the planning agent), not the raw terminal session.

Both cases appear to use the same terminal relay/WebSocket viewer. The fix should either:
- Use a proper terminal emulator (xterm.js) to interpret the escape sequences correctly
- Or for the Planning tab specifically, show the structured design markdown instead of raw terminal output
- Strip ANSI codes and filter empty lines as a minimum fallback
design:
## Summary The Agent Logs tab and Issue Planning tab both display raw tmux terminal output through the LogViewer component, which renders text literally without processing ANSI escape sequences. The logs captured from Claude Code sessions contain full VT100/VT102 terminal control codes (cursor movement like \x1b[1C for spaces, mode-setting like \x1b[?2004h, screen redraws like \x1b[6A), not just simple color codes. This causes garbled output with sequences like '[1CCode[1Cv2.1.37' instead of 'Code v2.1.37'. The fix has two parts: (1) strip ANSI escape sequences in the LogViewer, converting cursor-forward movements to spaces so words remain properly separated, and (2) change the Issue Planning tab to show the structured design field as rendered markdown instead of raw terminal logs. ## Technical Approach **Frontend ANSI stripping over backend stripping.** Stripping on the frontend in a utility function keeps the backend simple and preserves raw data in the SSE stream. The performance impact is negligible since the stripping regex runs on individual lines as they arrive. **Cursor-forward-to-spaces conversion.** The key insight is that \x1b[C sequences represent visible whitespace in the terminal output. Naive ANSI stripping would join words together (e.g., 'Claude[1CCode' becomes 'ClaudeCode'). The strip function must first replace cursor-forward sequences with the appropriate number of spaces before stripping remaining escape codes. **Empty line filtering.** After stripping, many log lines consist entirely of whitespace (terminal mode-setting lines, blank redraws). Filtering these out in the LogViewer produces dramatically cleaner output - the bug report specifically mentions 'mostly blank lines' as part of the problem. **Design field for Planning tab.** The issue.design field already contains the structured plan/design content written by planning agents as markdown. The IssueDetailPanel already imports and uses MarkdownRenderer for the Details tab's design section. The Planning tab should display this same content instead of streaming raw terminal logs. When no design field exists, fall back to the cleaned-up LogViewer. ## Files to Create ### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/utils/ansiStrip.ts` ANSI escape sequence stripping utility with two exported functions: - `stripAnsi(text: string): string` — Processes a single line of terminal output: 1. Replace CSI cursor-forward sequences `\x1b[C` (and `\x1b[C` for n=1) with n space characters 2. Replace CSI cursor-back/up/down/position sequences with empty string 3. Strip all remaining CSI sequences: `\x1b\[[\x30-\x3f]*[\x20-\x2f]*[\x40-\x7e]` 4. Strip OSC sequences: `\x1b\].*?(\x07|\x1b\\)` 5. Strip remaining single-character escape sequences: `\x1b[\x20-\x7e]` 6. Strip bare ESC characters The regex should be applied in order: cursor-forward replacement first (to preserve spacing), then strip everything else. - `isEmptyAfterStrip(text: string): boolean` — Returns true if the stripped text is empty or whitespace-only. Used for filtering. ### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/utils/__tests__/ansiStrip.test.ts` Unit tests for the ANSI stripping utility covering: - Basic color code stripping (e.g., `\x1b[31mError\x1b[0m` → `Error`) - Cursor-forward to spaces (e.g., `\x1b[3Cfoo` → ` foo`, `Claude\x1b[1CCode` → `Claude Code`) - OSC title-setting sequences stripped (e.g., `\x1b]0;Title\x07` → ``) - Terminal mode sequences stripped (e.g., `\x1b[?2004h` → ``) - Empty line detection for mode-only lines - Mixed content: real text + escape sequences - No-op on plain text (no escape sequences) - Edge cases: empty string, string with only ESC characters ## Files to Modify ### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/LogViewer/LogViewer.tsx` Import `stripAnsi` and `isEmptyAfterStrip` from `@/utils/ansiStrip`. Add a `useMemo` that processes the incoming `lines` prop: ```tsx const processedLines = useMemo(() => { return lines .map((logLine) => ({ ...logLine, line: stripAnsi(logLine.line), })) .filter((logLine) => !isEmptyAfterStrip(logLine.line)); }, [lines]); ``` Replace `lines` with `processedLines` in the render section (the `.map()` that renders `
`). This is a two-line change in the render method — swap `lines.length` and `lines.map` to use `processedLines`. Also update the empty state check to use `processedLines.length === 0` instead of `lines.length === 0`. Add `useMemo` to the React imports. ### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueDetailPanel/IssueDetailPanel.tsx` Modify the Planning tab rendering (around lines 642-651). Currently when `shouldConnectToLogs` is true, it renders LogViewer. Change this to: When `activeLogTab === 'planning'` AND `issue.design` exists: - Render the design content using MarkdownRenderer in a scrollable container - Do NOT connect to the log stream (skip the SSE connection entirely) When `activeLogTab === 'planning'` AND `issue.design` is empty/null: - Fall back to LogViewer with the log stream (which now strips ANSI) When `activeLogTab === 'implementation'`: - Continue using LogViewer with log stream (unchanged behavior, now with ANSI stripping) Specific changes: 1. Update `shouldConnectToLogs` logic (around line 288): ```tsx const shouldConnectToLogs = isTaskType && ( (activeLogTab === 'planning' && !issue?.design) || activeLogTab === 'implementation' ); ``` 2. Update the conditional rendering (around lines 642-651) to add a third branch: ```tsx {activeLogTab === 'planning' && issue?.design ? (
) : shouldConnectToLogs ? (
) : ( /* Details tab content (existing code) */ ... )} ``` ## Dependencies - No new npm packages needed - `useMemo` from React (already available) - `stripAnsi` utility is pure TypeScript with no dependencies - `MarkdownRenderer` component already exists and is imported in IssueDetailPanel ## Edge Cases & Error Handling 1. **Lines with only escape sequences**: After stripping, these become empty/whitespace and are filtered out. The log viewer won't show blank lines where terminal mode-setting happened. 2. **Lines where all 'spaces' are cursor-forward sequences**: The cursor-forward-to-spaces conversion handles this correctly. A line like `\x1b[4Cfoo\x1b[2Cbar` becomes ` foo bar`. 3. **Mixed content with partial ANSI**: The regex handles incomplete sequences gracefully — bare \x1b characters are stripped, partial sequences that don't match the full CSI pattern remain as text (defensive behavior). 4. **Performance with 5000-line buffer**: `useMemo` ensures stripping only recomputes when the lines array reference changes. Since `useLogStream` creates a new array on each update, the memo will recompute, but stripping 5000 strings with regex is well under 1ms on modern hardware. 5. **Issue with no design field**: The Planning tab falls back to LogViewer (with ANSI stripping), so there's always something to show. 6. **Design field with malformed markdown**: MarkdownRenderer already handles this — react-markdown renders best-effort. 7. **Unicode content in logs**: The ANSI regex targets escape sequences specifically (starting with \x1b). Unicode characters like box-drawing and emoji pass through unmodified. 8. **Cursor-forward with no number**: `\x1b[C` (no number parameter) means cursor forward 1 position, same as `\x1b[1C`. The regex should handle both forms. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit tests for ansiStrip utility: - Test `stripAnsi()` with various ANSI code types (SGR color, CSI cursor movement, OSC, terminal modes) - Test cursor-forward-to-spaces conversion with different counts - Test `isEmptyAfterStrip()` for lines that are purely escape sequences - Test with real log snippets from the codebase (e.g., `[?2004h[?1004h[?25l`) - Test no-op behavior on plain text ### Existing LogViewer tests pass unchanged: All existing `LogViewer.test.tsx` tests should pass because: - Tests use plain text lines (no ANSI codes), so `stripAnsi` is a no-op - The `processedLines` memo preserves non-empty lines - `isEmptyAfterStrip` returns false for non-empty plain text - Line numbers, status indicators, scroll behavior are unchanged ### Manual verification: ```bash cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run test:unit -- --run src/utils/__tests__/ansiStrip.test.ts cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run test:unit -- --run src/components/LogViewer/__tests__/LogViewer.test.tsx cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run typecheck ``` Then visually verify: 1. Open an agent detail panel → Logs tab → Should show clean text without escape codes 2. Open an issue detail panel (task with design) → Planning tab → Should show rendered markdown 3. Open an issue detail panel (task without design) → Planning tab → Should show cleaned log output 4. Open an issue detail panel → Implementation tab → Should show cleaned log output

title: [e2e-audit] filters-bulk.md — verify passing assertions have Playwright coverage
description: For each passing assertion from the filters-bulk.md validation report: search existing Playwright specs (filter.spec.ts, filter-bar.spec.ts, filter-url-sync.spec.ts, search.spec.ts, search-filter-journey.spec.ts) and Go tests. Record covered/uncovered. Create sub-tickets for uncovered. Deliverable: reports/e2e-audit-filters-bulk.json
design:
## Summary

Audit the 61 passing assertions from `reports/validation-filters-bulk.json` (in the nova worktree) against all existing Playwright E2E specs and Go tests to determine which behavioral assertions already have automated test coverage. Produce `reports/e2e-audit-filters-bulk.json` recording covered/uncovered/partial per VAL-ID, and create sub-tickets (beads issues) for each group of uncovered or partially-covered assertions that needs new Playwright tests.

## Technical Approach

The agent will:
1. Read the validation report from `reports/validation-filters-bulk.json` (located in the nova worktree at `/Users/tyson/codebase/code-agents/loomcli/worktrees/nova/reports/validation-filters-bulk.json`) and filter to only `status: "pass"` assertions (61 total).
2. For each passing assertion, search the Playwright spec files and Go test files for test(s) that exercise the same behavior.
3. Classify each assertion as `covered` (test exists), `partial` (test exists but doesn't fully verify the assertion's evidence criteria), or `uncovered` (no test found).
4. Write the audit report to `reports/e2e-audit-filters-bulk.json`.
5. Create beads sub-tickets for uncovered/partial assertions that need new Playwright tests, grouped by category (aim for 7-10 sub-tickets).

**Matching methodology**: For each VAL-ID, the agent must search the spec files listed below for test cases whose assertions verify the *same behavioral claim*. A test "covers" an assertion if it exercises the same user-visible behavior and checks the same output. Partial coverage means a test exercises related behavior but doesn't verify all evidence criteria. Do NOT count tests that use `filter()` as a Playwright locator helper (e.g., `locator("article").filter({ hasText: "..." })`) as filter-feature coverage — only tests that exercise the FilterBar/SearchInput UI components count.

## Conventions Established

Following the conventions established by sibling task `loomcli-ot68r` (kanban e2e-audit):

### Report Schema
```json
{
  "contract_file": "frontend/filters-bulk.md",
  "validation_report": "reports/validation-filters-bulk.json",
  "audit_date": "2026-04-17T..Z",
  "spec_files_searched": ["internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/filter.spec.ts", ...],
  "go_test_files_searched": ["internal/webui/handlers/issues/issues_test.go", ...],
  "summary": {
    "total_passing": 61,
    "covered": N,
    "partial": N,
    "uncovered": N,
    "coverage_pct": N.N
  },
  "assertions": [
    {
      "id": "VAL-FE-FILTER-001",
      "title": "Filter state initialized from URL query parameters",
      "coverage": "covered|partial|uncovered",
      "spec_files": ["filter-url-sync.spec.ts"],
      "test_names": ["navigating to URL with priority param applies filter"],
      "notes": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

### Coverage classification rules (from loomcli-ot68r)
- `covered`: A Playwright test explicitly exercises the behavior and asserts the expected outcome described in the VAL assertion
- `partial`: A Playwright test exercises related behavior but is missing key assertion criteria
- `uncovered`: No existing test exercises this behavior

### Sub-ticket naming convention (from loomcli-ot68r)
- Title format: `[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: <short behavior description>`
- Type: `task`
- Priority: 3 (P3)
- Parent: `loomcli-umzyd` (the validation suite epic)
- Description should reference the VAL-ID(s) and the behavioral assertion from the contract

## Files to Create

1. **`reports/e2e-audit-filters-bulk.json`** — The audit report following the schema above. Contains one entry per passing assertion (61 total) with coverage classification.

## Files to Modify

None — this is a pure analysis/reporting task. No source code changes.

## Out of Scope

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. This task only reads spec files and validation reports; it does not modify them.

## Dependencies

- **Validation report**: `reports/validation-filters-bulk.json` must exist in the nova worktree. It contains 61 passing, 5 failing, 29 blocked, 2 deferred assertions.

- **Spec files to search** (all under `internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/`):
  - `filter.spec.ts` — 22 tests: priority filtering, search filtering, URL sync, clear button, view switch persistence
  - `filter-bar.spec.ts` — 1 comprehensive test: clear filters button resets all filters and shows all issues
  - `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` — 14 tests: URL param sync for priority/type/search, edge cases (invalid/empty/non-numeric params), page refresh persistence
  - `search.spec.ts` — 7 tests: title/description match, case-insensitive, partial match, no matches, clear button, escape key
  - `search-filter-journey.spec.ts` — 1 journey test: search+filter persist through kanban→table→graph→kanban round-trip
  - `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` — 5 tests: table sorting, row selection, bulk toolbar appear/hide/clear

- **Go test files**:
  - `internal/webui/handlers/issues/issues_test.go` — `TestHandleListIssues_ParseListParams_Filters` (priority filter parsing)
  - `internal/webui/handlers/issues/coverage_test.go` — `TestHandleListIssues_MultipleFilters` (combined status+type+assignee+priority+labels query)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **Validation report not found**: If the report doesn't exist at the expected location, abort with error message identifying the missing file path. Do NOT generate a report with fabricated data.
- **Ambiguous coverage**: When a test covers part of an assertion but not all criteria, classify as `partial` and document what's missing in the `notes` field. Never round up to `covered`.
- **Duplicate coverage**: If multiple spec files cover the same assertion, list all matching spec files and test names. Pick the strongest match for the primary classification.
- **Go tests vs Playwright tests**: Go handler tests that verify server-side filter parsing count as backend coverage but NOT as E2E coverage for frontend assertions. Mention them in notes but classify based on Playwright coverage only.
- **Playwright `filter()` locator**: The Playwright `locator("article").filter({ hasText: ... })` is a test helper, NOT a filter-feature test. Do not confuse these with FilterBar tests.
- **Performance assertions**: Classify as `uncovered` if no test exists, noting in `notes` that specialized performance tests may be needed rather than standard Playwright assertions.

## Pre-computed Coverage Map

Based on codebase analysis, here is the expected mapping for each of the 61 passing assertions. The implementation agent MUST verify each mapping by reading the actual spec files, but this serves as the authoritative starting guide.

### Covered (28 assertions)

- **VAL-FE-FILTER-001**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "navigating to URL with priority param applies filter", "navigating to URL with type param applies filter", "navigating to URL with multiple filter params applies all filters"; `filter.spec.ts` → "navigating to URL with filter params applies filters" — verifies filter dropdowns reflect URL query params on load
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-002**: `filter.spec.ts` → "selecting priority filter updates URL with ?priority=N"; `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "priority filter updates URL params", "type filter updates URL params" — verifies URL updates when filter changes
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-003**: `filter.spec.ts` → "combined filters in URL work correctly (?priority=1&type=bug)"; `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "navigating to URL with multiple filter params applies all filters" — verifies multiple params coexist in URL
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-005**: `filter.spec.ts` → "clearing all filters removes query params from URL", "clear filters button clears all active filters at once"; `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "clear filters button removes URL params"; `filter-bar.spec.ts` → comprehensive clear test — verifies Clear All removes all params
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-006**: `filter.spec.ts` → "filter state survives page refresh via URL"; `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "filter state preserved through page refresh" — verifies URL round-trip restores filters
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-007**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "invalid URL params are ignored gracefully", "empty priority param is ignored", "non-numeric priority param is ignored" — verifies malformed params don't break the app
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-008**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "search input updates URL params with debounce"; `filter.spec.ts` → "combined priority + type + search filters work together" — verifies search param coexists with filter params in URL
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-011**: `filter.spec.ts` → "selecting priority filters issues to only matching priority"; `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "priority filter updates URL params" — verifies single priority selection filters cards
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-012**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "type filter updates URL params" — verifies single type selection filters cards
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-016**: `filter.spec.ts` → "clear filters button clears all active filters at once", "clear filters button clears combined priority+type+search filters"; `filter-bar.spec.ts` → comprehensive clear test — verifies Clear All clears all dimensions
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-001**: `search.spec.ts` → "filters issues by title match"; `filter.spec.ts` → "typing in search filters issues by text" — verifies search input accepts and filters on free-text
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-002**: `search.spec.ts` → "filters issues by title match", "partial match filters correctly"; `filter.spec.ts` → "typing in search filters issues by text" — verifies substring, case-insensitive title matching
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-003**: `search.spec.ts` → "filters issues by description match"; `filter.spec.ts` → "search matches title, description, and notes" — verifies search matches descriptions
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-004**: `search.spec.ts` → "search is case-insensitive"; `filter.spec.ts` → "search is case-insensitive" — verifies case-insensitive search
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-006**: `search.spec.ts` → "clearing search shows all issues"; `filter.spec.ts` → "clearing search input shows all issues" — verifies clear button removes search text
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-007**: `search.spec.ts` → "Escape key clears search"; `filter.spec.ts` → "escape key clears search" — verifies Escape key clears search
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-008**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "search input updates URL params with debounce" — verifies search param appears in URL
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-009**: `filter.spec.ts` → "combined priority + type + search filters work together"; `search-filter-journey.spec.ts` → journey test — verifies combined search + filter
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-010**: `search.spec.ts` → "clearing search shows all issues" — verifies empty search returns all non-filtered issues
- **VAL-FE-BULK-001**: `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` → "Select issues via row checkboxes and verify bulk toolbar" — verifies toolbar appears on first selection
- **VAL-FE-BULK-002**: `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` → "Clear selection via toolbar button" — verifies toolbar hides when selections cleared
- **VAL-FE-BULK-003**: `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` → "Select issues via row checkboxes and verify bulk toolbar" — checks "1 selected" then "2 selected" count
- **VAL-FE-BULK-020**: `journey-table-sort-select.spec.ts` → "Clear selection via toolbar button" — clicks the deselect/clear button
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-KANBAN-001**: `filter.spec.ts` → "selecting priority filters issues to only matching priority" — verifies non-matching issues are hidden from kanban columns
- **VAL-FE-ADV-009**: `filter.spec.ts` → "clearing filter shows all issues again", "clear filters button clears all active filters at once" — verifies empty filter state shows all issues
- **VAL-FE-ADV-010**: `filter.spec.ts` → "clear filters button clears combined priority+type+search filters" — verifies search clears when filters clear
- **VAL-FE-STATE-001**: `filter.spec.ts` (multiple URL sync tests); `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` (comprehensive URL sync tests) — verifies FilterState and URL remain synchronized
- **VAL-FE-STATE-003**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` → "search input updates URL params with debounce", "navigating to URL with search param applies filter" — verifies search input and URL param stay in sync
- **VAL-FE-REGRESSION-002**: `filter.spec.ts` → "filtering persists across view switches"; `search-filter-journey.spec.ts` → kanban→table→graph→kanban journey — verifies filters persist across view changes

### Partial (9 assertions)

- **VAL-FE-FILTER-004**: Tests exist for clearing ALL filters and checking URL, but no test specifically clears ONE filter dimension (e.g., priority) while leaving another (e.g., type) and verifies only the cleared param is removed from URL while the other is preserved. `filter.spec.ts` "clearing filter shows all issues again" clears priority but starts with only priority set, so there's no second dimension to verify preservation.
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-009**: Tests select specific priority values (P0, P1, P2, P4) but no test enumerates all dropdown options. Coverage verifies individual options work but not that all options are present.
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-010**: Tests select specific type values (bug, task, feature) but no test enumerates all dropdown options to verify completeness.
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-017**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` navigates to URLs with params which applies filters, but "externally" implies programmatic pushState/replaceState or browser back/forward updates, which isn't explicitly tested.
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-005**: `filter.spec.ts` and `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` wait for debounce (350ms) before asserting results, but no test verifies that requests are NOT fired before the 300ms threshold. Tests assume debounce works but don't prove it.
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-001**: `search-filter-journey.spec.ts` switches to table view with filters and verifies filter params persist, but doesn't explicitly verify that filtered-out issues are absent from the table rows.
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-KANBAN-004**: `swimlane-wiring.spec.ts` → "groupBy works with type/priority filter" tests filter+groupBy interaction from the groupBy perspective, but not from the FilterBar perspective with kanban groupBy.
- **VAL-FE-ADV-002**: `filter-url-sync.spec.ts` tests invalid priority values (99, empty, "abc") which are related edge cases, but doesn't test malformed JSON or URL-encoded invalid structures specifically.
- **VAL-FE-PERF-001**: Tests wait for debounce delays but don't measure re-render counts or verify that excessive API calls are prevented. Debounce is assumed to work based on timing, not measured.

### Uncovered (24 assertions)

**Search highlighting (8 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-001**: No Playwright test checks for `<mark>` tags or highlight styling on matched search text in titles
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-002**: No test for multiple highlight marks in the same field
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-003**: No test for case-insensitive highlighting
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-004**: No test for highlighting with regex special characters
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-005**: No test verifying no `<mark>` tags when search is empty
- **VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-006**: No test verifying `<mark>` tags are removed when search clears
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-004**: No test for search highlighting in table rows
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-KANBAN-005**: No test for search highlighting in kanban cards

**Table-view filtering (3 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-002**: No test combining table sorting with active filters
- **VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-005**: No test for clearing filters in table view and verifying full table restoration
- **VAL-FE-REGRESSION-001**: No test verifying that filter changes don't break existing sort order

**Selection persistence (2 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-BULK-005**: No test for selection persisting across filter state changes
- **VAL-FE-STATE-002**: No test for selection state persisting when filters change

**Search/filter edge cases (4 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-ADV-001**: No test for filtering with a non-existent label value
- **VAL-FE-ADV-003**: No test for conflicting filter values (e.g., status=open AND status=closed)
- **VAL-FE-ADV-004**: No test for very long search strings (100+ characters)
- **VAL-FE-ADV-005**: No test for regex metacharacters in search input (e.g., `.*`, `[`, `(`)

**Accessibility (3 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-A11Y-001**: No keyboard navigation tests for the filter bar (Tab between dropdowns, Enter to select)
- **VAL-FE-A11Y-002**: No screen reader/aria-live announcement tests for the bulk action toolbar
- **VAL-FE-A11Y-004**: No test verifying search input has an accessible label (aria-label or associated label element)

**Performance (3 assertions)**:
- **VAL-FE-PERF-002**: No performance test for filtering 1000+ issues
- **VAL-FE-PERF-004**: No test for URL with many filter params
- **VAL-FE-PERF-005**: No test for table scrolling with 1000+ filtered results

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `reports/e2e-audit-filters-bulk.json` exists and is valid JSON conforming to the schema in Conventions above
2. The report contains exactly 61 entries (one per passing assertion from the validation report)
3. Every entry has `id`, `title`, `coverage` (one of: covered, partial, uncovered), `spec_files` (array, may be empty), `test_names` (array, may be empty), and `notes` (string explaining the classification)
4. The `summary` object has correct counts: `total_passing` = 61, `covered + partial + uncovered` = 61, `coverage_pct` = `covered / total_passing * 100` rounded to 1 decimal
5. Expected approximate coverage split: ~28 covered, ~9 partial, ~24 uncovered (~45.9% coverage)
6. No assertion is classified as `covered` unless the agent verified by reading the spec file that a test explicitly exercises the behavior
7. Sub-tickets are created for all `uncovered` and `partial` assertions, grouped logically (7 sub-tickets, see below)
8. Each sub-ticket references specific VAL-IDs and has actionable descriptions
9. The report file is written to the nova worktree's `reports/` directory

## Sub-tickets to Create

The implementation agent must create these 7 grouped sub-tickets:

1. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Search text highlighting`** — VAL-FE-SEARCH-HIGHLIGHT-001 through 006, VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-004, VAL-FE-FILTER-KANBAN-005 (8 assertions). Tests needed: verify `<mark>` tags appear on matched text in kanban cards and table rows, case-insensitive matching, regex escaping, and cleanup on clear.

2. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Table-view filter integration`** — VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-002, VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-005, VAL-FE-REGRESSION-001, plus strengthen VAL-FE-FILTER-TABLE-001 (partial) (4 assertions). Tests needed: apply filter in table view and verify filtered-out rows are absent, sort while filtered, clear filters and verify full table restores.

3. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Selection persistence across filter changes`** — VAL-FE-BULK-005, VAL-FE-STATE-002 (2 assertions). Tests needed: select issues, change filter, verify selection persists for still-visible issues.

4. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Search and filter edge cases`** — VAL-FE-ADV-001, VAL-FE-ADV-003, VAL-FE-ADV-004, VAL-FE-ADV-005, plus strengthen VAL-FE-ADV-002 (partial) (5 assertions). Tests needed: non-existent label filter, conflicting filter values, 100+ char search, regex metacharacters in search, malformed JSON in URL.

5. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Accessibility`** — VAL-FE-A11Y-001, VAL-FE-A11Y-002, VAL-FE-A11Y-004 (3 assertions). Tests needed: keyboard Tab navigation through filter bar, aria-live region for bulk toolbar, accessible label on search input.

6. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Performance with large datasets`** — VAL-FE-PERF-002, VAL-FE-PERF-004, VAL-FE-PERF-005 (3 assertions). Tests needed: filter 1000+ issues responsively, URL with many params doesn't cause slowdown, table with 1000+ filtered results scrolls. Note: may require specialized performance test infrastructure.

7. **`[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: Partial coverage hardening`** — VAL-FE-FILTER-004, VAL-FE-FILTER-009, VAL-FE-FILTER-010, VAL-FE-FILTER-017, VAL-FE-SEARCH-005, VAL-FE-PERF-001, VAL-FE-FILTER-KANBAN-004 (7 partial assertions). Tests needed: clear one filter dimension while preserving others in URL, enumerate all dropdown options, test external URL changes via pushState, verify debounce prevents early requests, test filter+groupBy from FilterBar perspective.

## Testing Strategy

- **Self-check**: After generating the report, verify `assertions` array length equals 61 and that summary counts sum correctly
- **Spot-check**: For 3-5 `covered` assertions, manually verify the referenced spec file and test name actually test the claimed behavior
- **Completeness check**: Cross-reference all 61 passing VAL-IDs from the validation report against the report's assertion IDs — ensure zero omissions
- **Sub-ticket check**: Verify each sub-ticket references specific VAL-IDs, has the correct title format `[e2e-gap] filters-bulk: ...`, type=task, priority=3, and parent=loomcli-umzyd
