title: Kanban cards show owner badge but no assignee avatar
description: Cards display owner initial badge (e.g. 'V' for val@test) but no separate assignee avatar. Issue with assignee='alice' shows no indication of the assignee on the card. Ref: VAL-FE-KANBAN-021
design:
## Summary Kanban cards currently show an owner initial badge (gray circle with 1-2 letter initials) but have zero visual representation of the assignee outside of the in_progress and review columns — where the AgentRow component provides rich assignee info (avatar, name, status dot, activity text). In all other columns (open, blocked, done, backlog, ready), a card with assignee='alice' shows no indication whatsoever of who is assigned. The fix adds a colored assignee initial badge — visually distinct from the gray owner badge — that appears on all cards where the AgentRow is NOT already shown, giving every column assignee visibility. ## Technical Approach **Approach**: Add a colored circular badge (same dimensions as the owner badge) that displays the assignee's initial(s). The badge renders conditionally: only when issue.assignee is truthy AND the AgentRow is not shown (i.e., the card is NOT in in_progress or review columns). This avoids redundancy — AgentRow already provides assignee info in active columns. **Visual distinction from owner badge**: The owner badge uses a static gray background (var(--color-bg-secondary)). The assignee badge uses a deterministic pastel color from getAvatarColor() — the same color utility already used by AgentRow for its mini avatar. This gives each assignee a consistent, recognizable color across the board. **Layout change**: The current owner badge is a standalone flex child of the card. Both badges will be wrapped in a
flex container so they sit side-by-side. The wrapper only renders when at least one badge would be visible. **Key design decisions:** - Assignee badge shows ONLY when AgentRow is NOT shown (no redundancy) - Uses getAvatarColor() for colored background (already imported in IssueCard.tsx) - Uses dark text color (var(--color-text-primary)) since all AVATAR_COLORS are pastel/light (brightness > 160 for all 8 colors) - Strips [H] prefix for human assignees (same logic as AgentRow) - Initial extraction follows the same pattern as the owner badge: split by whitespace, take first char of each word, uppercase, slice to 2 chars **Trade-offs considered:** - "Show assignee badge on ALL columns including in_progress/review" was rejected: creates visual redundancy with AgentRow, which already shows the assignee's avatar, name, and live status. - "Reuse AuthorAvatar component" was rejected: AuthorAvatar has agent-detection logic (square shape for agents) and is designed for the detail panel context, not the compact card. A simple inline badge is more appropriate and consistent with the existing owner badge pattern. ## Conventions Established - data-testid="issue-card-assignee" is the canonical selector for the assignee badge in tests - Badge row wrapper pattern: when multiple small badges need side-by-side layout on a card, wrap them in a div.badgeRow - Assignee badge follows the same initial-extraction logic as the owner badge (split by whitespace, first chars, uppercase, max 2 chars) - The [H] prefix stripping pattern (already in AgentRow) is applied here too ## Files to Create None. ## Files to Modify ### 1. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx **What changes:** a) Add a computed boolean at line ~141 (after showAgentRow): ```tsx const showAssigneeBadge = !!issue.assignee && !showAgentRow; ``` b) Replace the standalone owner badge block (lines 274-287) with a wrapper that contains both badges. The wrapper renders only when at least one badge would be visible: ```tsx {(!!issue.owner || showAssigneeBadge) && (
{issue.owner && ( {issue.owner .split(/\s+/) .map((w) => w[0]) .join("") .toUpperCase() .slice(0, 2)} )} {showAssigneeBadge && ( {issue.assignee! .replace(/^\[H\]\s*/, "") .split(/\s+/) .map((w) => w[0]) .join("") .toUpperCase() .slice(0, 2)} )}
)} ``` **Why:** This is the core fix. The badge wrapper keeps both badges side-by-side. The assignee badge provides visual indication of assignment on cards where AgentRow does not appear. ### 2. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.module.css **What changes:** Add these styles after the existing .ownerBadge block (after line 367): ```css .badgeRow { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .assigneeBadge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 22px; height: 22px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-text-primary); border-radius: 50%; flex-shrink: 0; } ``` **Why:** The assigneeBadge matches the ownerBadge dimensions (22x22, 10px font, 600 weight, circle) for visual consistency. The key difference is: no static background-color — it's set via inline style from getAvatarColor(), and the text color is --color-text-primary (dark) since all AVATAR_COLORS are pastel/light. The badgeRow keeps both badges horizontally aligned with a 6px gap. ### 3. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/__tests__/IssueCard.test.tsx **What changes:** Add a new describe("assignee badge") block with these test cases: 1. "renders assignee badge when issue has assignee and columnId is open" - Create issue with assignee: "alice", render with columnId="open" - Expect data-testid="issue-card-assignee" to be in the document - Expect the badge to contain "A" (first initial of "alice") 2. "renders assignee badge with tooltip showing assignee name" - Create issue with assignee: "alice", render with columnId="open" - Expect title attribute to be "Assignee: alice" 3. "does not render assignee badge in in_progress column (AgentRow handles it)" - Create issue with assignee: "nova", render with columnId="in_progress" - Expect data-testid="issue-card-assignee" NOT to be in the document 4. "does not render assignee badge in review column (AgentRow handles it)" - Create issue with assignee: "nova", render with columnId="review" - Expect data-testid="issue-card-assignee" NOT to be in the document 5. "renders assignee badge in done column" - Create issue with assignee: "bob", render with columnId="done" - Expect data-testid="issue-card-assignee" to be in the document 6. "renders assignee badge in blocked column" - Create issue with assignee: "charlie", render with columnId="blocked" - Expect data-testid="issue-card-assignee" to be in the document 7. Assignee badge does NOT render (showAgentRow is true). **Expected**: AgentRow handles it. 6. **Card dragged (no columnId)**: showAgentRow is false (columnId is undefined). If assignee exists, showAssigneeBadge is true. **Expected**: assignee badge visible during drag. 7. **Assignee name with multiple words**: e.g., "Alice Smith" → initials "AS". The badge shows 2 characters max. **Expected**: "AS" in the badge. 8. **Very long assignee name**: Initial extraction always produces at most 2 characters. Tooltip shows full name. **Expected**: no layout issues. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A kanban card with assignee="alice" in the "done" column MUST show the assignee badge 3. A kanban card with assignee="alice" in the "blocked" column MUST show the assignee badge 4. A kanban card with NO assignee MUST NOT show the assignee badge, regardless of column 8. The assignee badge MUST be visually distinct from the owner badge (colored vs gray background) 9. The assignee badge MUST strip the [H] prefix for display: "[H] Alice" shows "A" and tooltip "Assignee: Alice" 10. When both owner and assignee exist, both badges MUST appear side-by-side 11. The assignee badge MUST have data-testid="issue-card-assignee" 12. All existing IssueCard tests (IssueCard.test.tsx, IssueCard.agentRow.test.tsx, IssueCard.repoBadge.test.tsx, AgentRow.test.tsx) MUST continue to pass ## Testing Strategy **Unit tests (vitest):** - Add ~12 new tests in IssueCard.test.tsx covering: rendering in various columns, not rendering in in_progress/review, no assignee, empty assignee, [H] prefix stripping, both badges together, and standalone scenarios - Run: cd internal/webui/frontend && npx vitest run src/components/IssueCard/__tests__/IssueCard.test.tsx - Verify existing tests still pass: npx vitest run src/components/IssueCard/__tests__/ **Manual verification:** 1. Start dev server 2. Create issues with assignees in various columns 3. Verify colored assignee badge appears on open/blocked/done/backlog cards 4. Verify assignee badge does NOT appear on in_progress/review cards (AgentRow is there instead) 5. Verify badge color matches the agent's color in AgentRow (same getAvatarColor function) 6. title: [e2e-audit] multi-agent-parallel.md — verify passing assertions have E2E test coverage
description: For each passing assertion from the multi-agent-parallel.md validation report: search existing tests (concurrent-ops.integration.spec.ts, daemon_concurrency_test.go, claim_test.go, recover_test.go). Record covered/uncovered. Create sub-tickets for uncovered. Deliverable: reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json
design:
## Summary

Audit each of the 43 passing assertions from the multi-agent-parallel.md validation report (reports/validation-multi-agent-parallel.json) to determine whether existing E2E tests (Go unit/integration tests + Playwright specs) cover the validated behavior. Produce a machine-readable report at reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json recording covered/uncovered for each passing assertion. Create bd sub-tickets for uncovered assertions.

This task follows the conventions established by loomcli-717r5 ([e2e-audit] e2e-agent-lifecycle.md), using the same report schema, coverage type classification, and assertion-to-test mapping rules.

## Technical Approach

This is a **research-and-report task**, not a code-change task. The implementation agent will:
1. Parse the 43 passing assertions from reports/validation-multi-agent-parallel.json
2. For each, search Go test files and Playwright specs for matching coverage
3. Record findings in a structured JSON report following the schema from loomcli-717r5
4. Create bd issues for uncovered assertions

The multi-agent-parallel contract covers four behavioral domains:
- **Lock lifecycle** (VAL-001–013): Lock acquisition, release, stale detection, concurrent prevention, lock field contents, workspace-scoped locks
- **Daemon management** (VAL-023–030, 049, 053–055): Daemon startup, restart policy, SIGTERM shutdown, concurrent instance prevention, per-agent logging, control socket IPC, daemon-agent coexistence
- **Push/sync** (VAL-031–033, 052): Push to main, push with uncommitted files, sync, rebase-conflict retry
- **SSE events** (VAL-040–042): SSE event delivery for mutations
- **Miscellaneous** (VAL-005, 036–039, 046–047, 056, 058–061, 064): Claim atomicity, kill-9 behavior, recovery, status transitions, lock permissions, design gating

**Trade-off**: Go unit tests that mock dependencies count as coverage since they test the behavioral logic. Playwright integration specs that exercise real server count as stronger coverage. Both are recorded with a coverage_type qualifier.

## Conventions Established

None — this task follows all conventions from loomcli-717r5 (the first e2e-audit task). See that task's design for the report schema, coverage type classification, and mapping rules.

## Files to Create

1. **reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json** — The audit report following the loomcli-717r5 schema. One entry per passing assertion (43 total).

## Files to Modify

None. This is a report-generation task.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. Each e2e-audit task targets a specific contract, and no other contracts share the VAL-E2E-MULTI-* assertion IDs.

## Dependencies

### Input Data
- **reports/validation-multi-agent-parallel.json** — Source of 43 passing assertions to audit. Already exists (43 pass, 1 fail, 20 blocked, 0 deferred).

### Test Files to Search (Go)

**Lock lifecycle tests:**
- internal/cli/lock_test.go — Lock acquire, release, stale detection, task update, state update, clear task ID, read lock file, concurrent retry (TestAcquireLock, TestAcquireLockFailsWhenLocked, TestCheckLockNoLock, TestCheckLockWithLock, TestUpdateLockTask, TestReleaseLock, TestGetLockStatus, TestUpdateLockState, TestClearLockTaskID, TestReadLockFile, TestAcquireLockStale_ConcurrentRetry, TestAcquireLockStale, TestCheckLockStale, TestSingleTaskModeLockStatePattern)
- internal/cli/lock_workspace_test.go — Workspace-scoped independent locks, lock info workspace field (TestAcquireLock_WorkspaceIndependentLocks, TestCheckLock_Workspace, TestReleaseLock_Workspace, TestLockInfo_WorkspaceField, TestUpdateLockTask_Workspace, TestClearLockTaskID_Workspace, TestUpdateLockState_Workspace)
- internal/lockfile/lock_test.go — Low-level lock read, PID check, daemon lock, flock, concurrent access (TestReadLockInfo, TestCheckPIDFile, TestTryDaemonLock, TestFlockFunctions, TestIsProcessRunning, TestTryLockExclusive_Success, TestTryLockExclusive_AlreadyLocked, TestTryLockExclusive_ReleasedAfterClose, TestConcurrentLockAccess)
- internal/types/lock_test.go — Lock struct marshal/unmarshal, validation, permissions (TestExclusiveLock_MarshalJSON, TestExclusiveLock_Validate, TestNewExclusiveLock)
- internal/types/lock_check_test.go — Lock skip logic (TestShouldSkipDatabase)

**Agent tests:**
- internal/cli/agent/claim_test.go — Claim with lock update (TestRunClaim_Success, TestRunClaim_NoTitle)
- internal/cli/agent/recover_test.go — Force release lock, reset tasks, handle orphaned tasks, kill process, workspace recovery (TestForceReleaseLock_RemovesLockFile, TestResetTask_Success, TestHandleOrphanedTask_NoAnalyze, TestRecoverWorktree_NoLock, TestRecoverWorktree_StaleLock, TestResetOrphanedAgentTasks_FindsAndResetsMultiple, TestKillProcess_Success)

**Push/sync tests:**

- internal/cli/git/sync_test.go — Sync command flags, single workspace sync (TestSyncCmd_NoArgs, TestSyncCmd_Flags, TestSyncSingleWorkspace_EmptyWorktrees)

### Test Files to Search (Playwright)
- internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/server-push.spec.ts — SSE connection, mutation events, reconnection, two-browser SSE (test: "mutation events are processed by the app", "two browser contexts can both attempt SSE connections", "SSE client retries connection on failure")
- internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/server-push-integration.spec.ts — CLI mutation triggers UI update, status change via CLI, multiple rapid mutations, SSE reconnects, two-window sync (test: "CLI mutation triggers UI update", "multiple rapid mutations are processed in order", "update in one window reflects in the other")
- internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/integration/concurrent-ops.integration.spec.ts — Concurrent creates, concurrent PATCH, concurrent status transitions, SSE burst delivery (test: "concurrent creates all succeed and return distinct IDs", "concurrent PATCH of different fields preserves all changes", "concurrent status transitions end in valid state", "burst of rapid creates and status changes reach SSE client")

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Assertion covers multiple behaviors**: Some assertions test compound scenarios (e.g., VAL-E2E-MULTI-007 tests stale lock cleanup + task status reset). Map to ALL covering tests; use coverage_type "both" if tests span Go + Playwright.

2. **Test covers mechanism but not exact scenario**: If a Go test tests lock acquisition and another tests concurrent lock rejection, together they cover VAL-E2E-MULTI-002 ("Lock file prevents concurrent agent in same worktree"). Note the combined coverage in the relevance field.

3. **No test found**: Mark e2e_covered=false, coverage_type="none", add to uncovered_summary with suggested ticket title following pattern "[e2e-gap] {assertion title}".

4. **VAL-E2E-MULTI-064 (meta-assertion)**: This is a "count and coverage verification" meta-assertion. Mark as covered if the validation report itself demonstrates 64 assertions were executed — no test file needed.

5. **Multiple tests partially cover**: List all covering tests in the covering_tests array. The assertion is "covered" if the union of tests exercises the full expected behavior.

6. **Daemon tests use mocks vs E2E**: daemon_cmd_test.go uses mocks; daemon_e2e_test.go uses real processes. Both count, with daemon_e2e_test.go noted as stronger coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json exists and is valid JSON
2. The report contains exactly 43 assertion entries (one per passing assertion from the validation report)
3. Every assertion with e2e_covered=true has at least one entry in covering_tests with a valid file path and test_name
4. Every assertion with e2e_covered=false has an entry in uncovered_summary with a suggested_ticket_title
5. coverage_pct equals (covered_count / passing_assertion_count) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
6. covered_count + uncovered_count equals passing_assertion_count (43)
7. All file paths in covering_tests are relative to the repo root and point to files that actually exist
8. coverage_type is one of: "go_unit", "playwright", "both", "none"
9. No assertions with validation_status other than "pass" appear in the report (skip fail/blocked/deferred)
10. The report does NOT fabricate test names — every test_name listed must exist in the referenced file

## Testing Strategy

### Self-Verification (implementation agent must run these)
1. `python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json')); assert len(r['assertions'])==43"` — Correct count
2. `python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json')); assert r['covered_count']+r['uncovered_count']==43"` — Totals match
3. For each covering_tests entry, verify the file exists: `test -f {file_path}`
4. For each Go test_name, verify it exists: `grep -q 'func {test_name}' {file_path}`
5. For each Playwright test_name, verify it exists: `grep -q '{test_name}' {file_path}` (test descriptions may be partial)
6. `python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('reports/e2e-audit-multi-agent-parallel.json')); assert all(a['validation_status']=='pass' for a in r['assertions'])"` — Only passing assertions

### Sub-ticket Creation
After generating the report, create bd issues for each uncovered assertion:
- Title: "[e2e-gap] {assertion title}"

title: SSE token exchange URL mismatch
description: Frontend fetchSseToken() in src/api/sse.ts calls GET /api/events/token but the backend registers GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/events/token (workspace-scoped). The 404 silently falls back to kind:disabled, meaning SSE token exchange is broken in external auth mode. Fix: make fetchSseToken accept a workspaceId parameter and use wsUrl(workspaceId, '/events/token'). Introduced in commit 973d653d (task loomcli-laf73.23).
design:
## Summary

Fix the SSE token exchange URL mismatch where the frontend calls `GET /api/events/token` (flat path) but the backend only registers `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/events/token` (workspace-scoped). The 404 response is silently caught and treated as "disabled," which means SSE token exchange is broken whenever external auth mode is enabled — opaque tokens are never obtained and SSE connections fail silently. The fix is to make `fetchSseToken()` accept a `workspaceId` parameter and use the existing `wsUrl()` helper to construct the correct workspace-scoped path.

## Technical Approach

**Frontend-only change.** The backend is correct — the route is registered at the workspace-scoped path and the `handleSSEToken` handler correctly extracts `workspaceID` from context. The bug is entirely in the frontend's `fetchSseToken()` function which hardcodes a flat path.

**Fix:**
1. Add a `workspaceId: string` parameter to `fetchSseToken()`
2. Replace the hardcoded `"/api/events/token"` path with `wsUrl(workspaceId, "/events/token")`
3. Update the call site in `BeadsSSEClient.connect()` to pass `this.workspaceId`

**Why this approach (vs alternatives):**
- Could register a flat fallback route on the backend — but that would break the workspace-scoped auth model and contradict the design decision to make all API routes workspace-scoped
- Could add a middleware redirect — unnecessary complexity for a one-line frontend fix
- Changing `fetchSseToken` to accept workspaceId is the minimal, correct fix that aligns with how every other workspace-scoped API call works in the frontend (all use `wsUrl()`)

## Conventions Established

None — this fix follows existing conventions. All workspace-scoped frontend API calls already use `wsUrl()`.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/sse.ts`

**Change `fetchSseToken` signature and URL construction (lines 14-25):**

Change from:
```typescript
async function fetchSseToken(): Promise<SseTokenResult> {
  try {
    const resp = await get<{ token: string }>("/api/events/token");
```

To:
```typescript
async function fetchSseToken(workspaceId: string): Promise<SseTokenResult> {
  try {
    const resp = await get<{ token: string }>(wsUrl(workspaceId, "/events/token"));
```

No other changes to this function. The `wsUrl` import already exists on line 6.

**Update call site in `connect()` (line 129):**

Change from:
```typescript
    const tokenResult = await fetchSseToken();
```

To:
```typescript
    const tokenResult = await fetchSseToken(this.workspaceId);
```

### 2. `internal/webui/frontend/src/api/sse.test.ts`

**Add assertion that `get()` is called with the correct workspace-scoped URL.**

In the "connect() with token success" test (around line 845), add after `mockGet.mockResolvedValue(...)`:
```typescript
expect(mockGet).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/api/workspaces/test-ws-id/events/token");
```

Similarly, add URL assertions to:
- "connect() with token disabled (404)" test (line 856) — verify `mockGet` was called with workspace-scoped URL
- "connect() with token error" test (line 865) — verify `mockGet` was called with workspace-scoped URL

The workspace ID "test-ws-id" is used because `BeadsSSEClient` is instantiated with `"test-ws-id"` throughout the test file (e.g., line 868: `new BeadsSSEClient("test-ws-id", ...)`).

### 3. `internal/webui/frontend/tests/e2e/unblock-stuck-task.spec.ts`

**Update the route mock in `setupInfrastructureMocks` (line 208):**

Change from:
```typescript
await page.route("**/api/events/token", async (route) => {
```

To:
```typescript
await page.route("**/api/workspaces/*/events/token", async (route) => {
```

The glob `**/api/workspaces/*/events/token` matches the workspace-scoped path regardless of which workspace ID is used. The response body (`{ token: "test-sse-token" }`) remains unchanged.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

None — neighborhood scan found no unaddressed siblings. The `wsUrl()` pattern is already used consistently across all other frontend API calls. No other files reference the flat `/api/events/token` path.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- No internal module dependencies beyond what's already imported (`wsUrl` from `./client`)
- No blocking tasks

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Empty workspaceId**: If `workspaceId` is empty string, `wsUrl("", "/events/token")` produces `/api/workspaces//events/token` (double slash). This cannot happen in practice — `BeadsSSEClient` receives `workspaceId` from `useWorkspaceContext()` which always returns a non-empty workspace ID (the hook throws if no workspace context is available). No additional validation needed.

2. **WorkspaceId with special characters**: `wsUrl()` already calls `encodeURIComponent()` on the workspace ID (client.ts:13), so this is handled. No additional handling needed.

3. **404 still means "disabled"**: After the fix, a 404 from the workspace-scoped endpoint correctly means the server has no SSE token exchange configured (non-external-auth mode). The existing 404→`kind:disabled` fallback remains correct — the only change is that the endpoint URL is now correct, so the 404 actually comes from the right place (server intentionally not registering the route when `sseTokens` is nil) rather than from a route mismatch.

4. **Auth failure (401)**: When ExtAuth is enabled but the JWT is expired/invalid, the middleware returns 401 before hitting `handleSSEToken`. The frontend's `get()` helper already handles 401 via the auth token expired interceptor (client.ts:177-179), which clears the token and triggers re-authentication. `fetchSseToken` catches this as a non-404 error and returns `kind: "error"`. The `connect()` method then calls `onError` and sets state to "disconnected" (lines 136-140). This is correct behavior — no change needed.

5. **Race condition on disconnect during token fetch**: Already handled — line 132 checks `this.manualDisconnect` after awaiting `fetchSseToken()`. No change needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fetchSseToken()` accepts a `workspaceId: string` parameter.
2. `fetchSseToken()` calls `get()` with path `wsUrl(workspaceId, "/events/token")`, which resolves to `/api/workspaces/{ws}/events/token`.
3. `BeadsSSEClient.connect()` passes `this.workspaceId` to `fetchSseToken()`.
4. In external auth mode, SSE token exchange succeeds (returns `kind: "token"` with a valid opaque token) instead of silently falling back to `kind: "disabled"`.
5. In non-external-auth mode, the endpoint returns 404 (server doesn't register the route) and `fetchSseToken` correctly returns `kind: "disabled"` — behavior unchanged.
6. Unit tests in `sse.test.ts` pass and assert the correct workspace-scoped URL is passed to `get()`.
7. E2E test `unblock-stuck-task.spec.ts` route mock matches the workspace-scoped URL pattern.
8. `npm run typecheck` passes (no TypeScript errors from the signature change).
9. The flat path `/api/events/token` must NOT appear anywhere in frontend source code (excluding test mocks and comments).

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (sse.test.ts)

**Existing tests** — All existing tests continue to pass. The `mockGet` mock intercepts all `get()` calls regardless of path, so the behavioral tests (token success, token disabled, token error, bail on disconnect) are unaffected.

**New assertions** — Add `expect(mockGet).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` assertions in 3 existing tests to verify the correct workspace-scoped URL:
- Token success test: verify `mockGet` called with `/api/workspaces/test-ws-id/events/token`
- Token disabled (404) test: same URL assertion
- Token error (500) test: same URL assertion

### E2E Test (unblock-stuck-task.spec.ts)

Update the Playwright route mock glob to `**/api/workspaces/*/events/token` so it intercepts the workspace-scoped path.

### Manual Verification

1. Start the WebUI in external auth mode (`ExtAuthURL` configured)
2. Open browser DevTools Network tab
3. Load the app — verify the SSE token exchange request goes to `/api/workspaces/{ws}/events/token` (not the flat path)
4. Verify the response is 200 with `{ token: "..." }` (not 404)
5. Verify the EventSource URL includes `?token=...` parameter
6. Verify SSE events are received (mutations appear in real-time)

### Build Verification

- `cd internal/webui/frontend && npm run typecheck` — TypeScript compilation
- `cd internal/webui/frontend && npm test` — Vitest unit tests
- `cd internal/webui/frontend && npx playwright test tests/e2e/unblock-stuck-task.spec.ts` — E2E test (if CI environment available)

title: Add single-agent restart/stop to daemon CLI
description:
Add per-agent control commands to the daemon CLI:

- \`loom daemon restart <agent-name>\` — stop and restart a single agent (reset its counters)
- \`loom daemon stop <agent-name>\` — stop a single agent without affecting others
- \`loom daemon start <agent-name>\` — restart a previously stopped agent

This is critical for operations — when one agent is misconfigured or stuck, you shouldn't have to disrupt all other agents.

## Implementation Notes (from code architect)

**Requires new IPC infrastructure.** No RPC channel currently exists between CLI and daemon — all communication is via filesystem artifacts (PID file, state JSON).

- Add a **Unix domain socket control server** (~200-250 lines) to the daemon
- \`restartAgent\` = \`drainAgent\` + \`addAgent\` with fresh counters
- The reconciler's \`addAgent\`/\`drainAgent\` pattern can be reused directly
- Socket path: \`<lockDir>/daemon.sock\`
- Known limitation: \`loom daemon stop <agent>\` without the socket means the reconciler re-adds the agent on next config poll. The socket approach avoids this.

**Highest effort ticket** in the daemon CLI batch — save for last. Estimated ~200-250 lines of new code for the socket server + client.
design:
## Summary

Add per-agent control commands (`loom daemon restart <agent>`, `loom daemon stop <agent>`, `loom daemon start <agent>`) that communicate with the running daemon via a new Unix domain socket control server. This enables operators to stop, start, or restart individual agents without disrupting the entire fleet — critical when one agent is stuck or misconfigured. The control socket is a lightweight JSON-over-newline protocol separate from the existing bd RPC socket.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: A dedicated Unix domain socket control server runs inside the daemon process. CLI subcommands connect as clients, send a JSON command, receive a JSON response, and disconnect. This is intentionally simpler than the existing bd RPC protocol — it's a single-purpose control plane with no auth, no health checks, and no connection reuse.

**Why a separate socket (not extend bd RPC)?** The bd RPC socket serves the issue tracker daemon. The loom daemon is a separate process with different lifecycle. Adding control operations to bd RPC would create a coupling between the two systems. A dedicated `daemon.sock` keeps concerns separated and avoids requiring the bd daemon to be running for agent control.

**Why not use signals?** Signals can only target the entire daemon process. There's no way to signal "restart agent falcon" via SIGTERM/SIGUSR1. The socket approach allows structured commands with agent names and typed responses.

**Key design decisions:**
1. **Socket path**: `<lockDir>/daemon.sock` where lockDir is `filepath.Dir(pidFilePath)`, typically `.loom/daemon.sock`. This co-locates with `daemon.pid` and `daemon.lock`.
2. **Protocol**: Single JSON line request → single JSON line response (same framing as bd RPC but different message types). One connection per command — no persistent connections.
3. **Restart = drain + add**: `restartAgent(name)` calls `drainAgent(name)` then looks up the original `AgentEntry` from config and calls `addAgent(entry)`. This resets all counters (restartCount, rateRetryCount, currentBackendIdx).
4. **Stop persistence**: When an agent is stopped via control socket, record its name in a `stoppedAgents` set on the Daemon struct. The config reconciler must check this set and NOT re-add stopped agents on config reload. `start` clears the agent from this set.
5. **Agent identification**: Agents are identified by their `Worktree` name (e.g., "falcon", "nova"), matching the existing convention in `drainAgent`/`addAgent`/`diffAgents`.

## Conventions Established

- **Control socket path**: `<lockDir>/daemon.sock` (adjacent to daemon.pid and daemon.lock)
- **Control protocol message types**: `DaemonControlRequest` / `DaemonControlResponse` (distinct from bd's `rpc.Request`/`rpc.Response`)
- **Control operations**: `"agent_stop"`, `"agent_start"`, `"agent_restart"`, `"agent_list"` (list is for validation/discovery)
- **Stopped agents tracking**: `Daemon.stoppedAgents map[string]struct{}` (protected by `agentsMu`)

## Files to Create

### `internal/cli/daemon_control.go` (~200 lines)
Control socket server and protocol types. Contains:
- `DaemonControlRequest` struct: `Operation string`, `AgentName string`
- `DaemonControlResponse` struct: `Success bool`, `Error string`, `Data json.RawMessage` (optional, for list)
- `(d *Daemon) startControlServer(socketPath string) error` — creates Unix listener, accepts connections in a goroutine, dispatches to handler. Closes listener on `d.shutdown`.
- `(d *Daemon) handleControlConnection(conn net.Conn)` — reads one JSON line, dispatches by Operation, writes one JSON line response, closes conn.
- `(d *Daemon) handleAgentStop(name string) error` — validates agent exists in config, calls `drainAgent(name)`, adds to `stoppedAgents` set.
- `(d *Daemon) handleAgentStart(name string) error` — validates agent is in `stoppedAgents`, removes from set, looks up `AgentEntry` from current config, calls `addAgent(entry)`.
- `(d *Daemon) handleAgentRestart(name string) error` — validates agent exists (either running or stopped). If running: `drainAgent` + `addAgent`. If stopped: remove from `stoppedAgents` + `addAgent`.
- `(d *Daemon) handleAgentList() []AgentListEntry` — returns list of agent names with status (running/stopped).
- `resolveDaemonSocketPath(projectDir string, pidFile string) string` — returns socket path adjacent to PID file.

### `internal/cli/daemon_control_client.go` (~60 lines)
Client-side helper for CLI commands to send control requests:
- `sendDaemonControlRequest(socketPath string, op string, agentName string) (*DaemonControlResponse, error)` — dials Unix socket, sends request JSON, reads response JSON, closes conn. 5-second timeout on dial, 30-second timeout on read (drain+stop can take time).

### `internal/cli/daemon_control_test.go` (~250 lines)
Tests for the control server:
- Test stop/start/restart lifecycle
- Test stopping an already-stopped agent returns error
- Test starting a non-stopped agent returns error
- Test restarting a stopped agent (start + fresh supervisor loop)
- Test that stopped agents survive config reconciliation (not re-added)
- Test agent name validation (non-existent agent)
- Test concurrent control requests
- Test control server shutdown cleanup (socket file removed)

## Files to Modify

### `internal/cli/daemon.go`
- Add `stoppedAgents map[string]struct{}` field to `Daemon` struct. This set is protected by `agentsMu` (reuse existing mutex to avoid lock ordering issues).
- Initialize `stoppedAgents: make(map[string]struct{})` in `NewDaemon()`.
- Add `(d *Daemon) isAgentStopped(name string) bool` helper method (reads under `agentsMu.RLock`).

### `internal/cli/daemon_cmd.go`
- Add three new Cobra subcommands: `daemonAgentStopCmd`, `daemonAgentStartCmd`, `daemonAgentRestartCmd`.
- Register in `init()`: `daemonCmd.AddCommand(daemonAgentStopCmd, daemonAgentStartCmd, daemonAgentRestartCmd)`.
- Each command's Run function: resolve project dir, resolve socket path (using same pidFile resolution as status/stop commands), call `sendDaemonControlRequest`, print result.
- Update `daemonCmd.Long` help text to document the new subcommands.
- In `runDaemon()`: after `daemon.Start()`, call `daemon.startControlServer(socketPath)`. Add defer for socket cleanup (`os.Remove(socketPath)`). Compute socketPath using `resolveDaemonSocketPath(projectDir, config.Daemon.PIDFile)`.

### `internal/cli/daemon_reconciler.go`
- In `reloadAndReconcile()`: after computing `added` list, filter out agents whose Worktree name is in `d.stoppedAgents`. This prevents the reconciler from re-adding manually stopped agents.
- Add comment explaining the filtering: "Agents stopped via control socket are excluded from re-addition until explicitly started."

### `internal/cli/daemon_supervisor.go`
- In `Stop()`: also close the control server listener (if running). The control server goroutine will exit when the listener is closed.

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

- **`loom daemon logs <agent>`** (loomcli-bcaeh) — separate task, no RPC needed
- **`loom daemon config`** (loomcli-kt7ab) — separate task for showing resolved config
- **`loom daemon status` enhancements** (loomcli-fkca7, in progress by comet) — that task extends the status display but does not add control operations
- **Authentication on control socket** — the daemon.lock already prevents unauthorized startup; the control socket is local-only (Unix domain socket with filesystem permissions). Auth can be added later if needed.
- **Persistent stop state across daemon restarts** — if the daemon is restarted, all agents start fresh per config. The stoppedAgents set is in-memory only. This is intentional: a full daemon restart implies the operator wants a clean slate.

## Dependencies

- **Internal modules**: `internal/cli` (Daemon, AgentProcess, drainAgent, addAgent), `internal/lockfile` (for process checking)
- **External packages**: None new — uses only `net`, `encoding/json`, `os`, `path/filepath` from stdlib
- **No task dependencies**: This is independent of other daemon CLI tasks. However, implementations of loomcli-bcaeh and loomcli-kt7ab should be aware that the control socket now exists and could potentially be extended for their use cases in the future.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Agent name not found**: If the requested agent name doesn't match any `AgentEntry.Worktree` in the current config, return error: `"agent %q not found in daemon config"`. Do NOT check only the running agents list — an agent that was stopped is still in the config.

2. **Stop an already-stopped agent**: If the agent is in `stoppedAgents` and not in the running `agents` slice, return error: `"agent %q is already stopped"`. This prevents confusion.

3. **Start a running agent**: If the agent is NOT in `stoppedAgents` (meaning it's currently running or being supervised), return error: `"agent %q is not stopped (use restart to reset a running agent)"`.

4. **Restart a stopped agent**: This is valid — `handleAgentRestart` should handle both running and stopped states. If stopped: remove from `stoppedAgents`, call `addAgent`. If running: `drainAgent` then `addAgent`.

5. **Restart during agent backoff**: If `drainAgent` is called while the agent's superviseAgent goroutine is sleeping in a backoff `time.After`, the `stopCh` close will interrupt the backoff select and the goroutine will exit cleanly. `drainAgent` then waits on `<-target.done`. This already works correctly.

6. **Control socket dial failure (daemon not running)**: The CLI client should check for connection refused or socket-not-found and print: `"daemon is not running (no control socket at %s)"`. Exit code 1.

7. **Control socket timeout**: The CLI client uses a 30-second read timeout. If the operation takes longer (e.g., drainAgent waiting for a long-running subprocess), the client prints a timeout warning but the server-side operation continues to completion. This is acceptable — the state file will eventually reflect the change.

8. **Concurrent control requests**: The control server accepts connections sequentially (one handler goroutine per connection). `drainAgent` and `addAgent` are already thread-safe (use `agentsMu`). Multiple concurrent stop/start requests are safe but will serialize on the mutex. No additional locking needed.

9. **Config reconciler race with stop**: The reconciler runs on a 500ms debounce timer. Between a stop command and the next reconcile, the agent is drained. The reconciler's `diffAgents` will see the agent in the config but not in `d.agents` — it would normally add it as "new". The `stoppedAgents` filter prevents this re-addition. If the user edits loom.yaml to remove the agent AND it was stopped, the filter is a no-op (agent isn't in the added list). If the user edits loom.yaml to modify the agent AND it was stopped, the filter prevents re-addition with the new config — the user must explicitly `start` it.

10. **Socket cleanup on crash**: If the daemon crashes, the socket file is orphaned. On next daemon startup, `startControlServer` should `os.Remove(socketPath)` before `net.Listen` to clean up stale sockets. This is safe because the daemon.lock prevents concurrent startup.

11. **Socket path length**: The daemon socket lives at `.loom/daemon.sock` which is much shorter than bd's `.beads/bd.sock`. No short-path fallback needed since `.loom/` is always within the project dir and well under the 103-char Unix socket limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `loom daemon stop falcon` stops only the "falcon" agent; other agents continue running unaffected.
2. `loom daemon start falcon` restarts a previously stopped agent; it resumes its superviseAgent loop with fresh counters (restartCount=0, rateRetryCount=0).
3. `loom daemon restart falcon` stops and restarts a running agent with fresh counters.
4. `loom daemon restart falcon` also works on a stopped agent (equivalent to start).
5. After `loom daemon stop falcon`, editing loom.yaml does NOT cause the reconciler to re-add falcon.
6. After `loom daemon start falcon`, editing loom.yaml resumes normal reconciliation for falcon.
7. `loom daemon stop nonexistent` prints an error and exits non-zero.
8. `loom daemon stop falcon` when falcon is already stopped prints an error and exits non-zero.
9. `loom daemon start falcon` when falcon is running prints an error and exits non-zero.
10. Running any control command when the daemon is not running prints "daemon is not running" and exits non-zero.
11. The control socket file is cleaned up on graceful daemon shutdown.
12. The control socket file is cleaned up on next daemon startup (stale socket from crash).
13. `loom daemon status` continues to work and shows stopped agents with "stopped" status.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (`daemon_control_test.go`)

1. **TestControlServer_StopAgent**: Start daemon with 2 agents, send stop for one, verify it's removed from agents slice and added to stoppedAgents, verify the other agent is unaffected.
2. **TestControlServer_StartAgent**: Stop an agent, then start it, verify it's back in agents slice with fresh counters and removed from stoppedAgents.
3. **TestControlServer_RestartAgent**: Start daemon with agent, send restart, verify drainAgent+addAgent called with fresh state.
4. **TestControlServer_RestartStoppedAgent**: Stop an agent, then restart it (should succeed, equivalent to start).
5. **TestControlServer_StopAlreadyStopped**: Stop agent, stop again — expect error response.
6. **TestControlServer_StartNotStopped**: Start an agent that's running — expect error response.
7. **TestControlServer_UnknownAgent**: Stop/start/restart with name not in config — expect error response.
8. **TestControlServer_ReconcilerRespectsStoppedAgents**: Stop agent, trigger reloadAndReconcile with same config, verify agent is NOT re-added.
9. **TestControlServer_ReconcilerAfterStart**: Stop agent, start agent, trigger reloadAndReconcile, verify agent IS included in normal reconciliation.
10. **TestControlServer_SocketCleanup**: Start control server, stop daemon, verify socket file is removed.
11. **TestControlServer_StaleSocketCleanup**: Create a stale socket file, start control server, verify it starts successfully (removes stale file first).

### Integration Tests
- Manual verification: run `loom daemon` in one terminal, use `loom daemon stop/start/restart <agent>` in another terminal.
- Verify `loom daemon status` reflects the stopped/started state.

### Key Scenarios to Cover
- Stop agent while it's in backoff sleep (should interrupt cleanly)
- Stop agent while subprocess is running (should SIGTERM → SIGKILL)
- Restart agent while it's spawning (should wait for spawn, then drain)
- Concurrent stop+start of same agent (should serialize safely)
- Config change during stop operation (reconciler waits on reconcileMu)

title: Fix daemon status/stop detection and destructive cleanup
description:
Repro from real daemon e2e on 2026-03-22:
- daemon spawned a real planner and the planner successfully claimed a task, wrote a design, moved it to review, ran bd sync, and signaled loom complete
- while the daemon process was alive, `loom daemon status` reported "Daemon: not running"
- while the same daemon process was alive, `loom daemon stop` reported "Daemon is not running"
- after the agent exited cleanly, daemon cleanup treated untracked runtime state as disposable and removed .beads/, .loom/, and sessions/
- the next restart attempt then failed because no beads database remained

Expected outcome:
- daemon lifecycle commands reflect the real supervisor state
- daemon cleanup preserves required runtime/state directories and repo metadata
- restart or idle transitions after a clean run do not destroy the workspace
- add regression coverage for the observed e2e path
design:
## Summary
Fix the daemon lifecycle regressions surfaced by the real end-to-end run on 2026-03-22. The implementation should make `loom daemon status` and `loom daemon stop` derive liveness from authoritative daemon runtime state instead of a single PID file, and it should harden daemon recovery / branch-reset cleanup so shared runtime paths such as `.beads/`, `.loom/`, `sessions/`, and required Loom control files are never deleted as disposable untracked files.

## Technical Approach
Add a shared daemon-runtime detection helper and use it everywhere daemon liveness is reported or acted on. The helper should resolve daemon state from the same sources the supervisor already maintains: the held Beads daemon lock (`internal/lockfile`), the Loom state file (`.loom/daemon-agents.json`), and the configured PID file as a backward-compatible fallback. The precedence should be: lockfile-first when present and valid, then state/PID fallback for older daemons or partial state. `loom daemon status`, `loom daemon stop`, and any general status summary that surfaces daemon state should all call the same helper so they cannot disagree.

Separately, replace blanket untracked cleanup with an explicit protected-runtime allowlist. The observed deletion happened because recovery and branch-reset flows treat all dirty or untracked state as ephemeral, but in workspace mode the shared repo root can also hold live supervisor state and Beads/session storage. Introduce one shared preservation rule that protects Loom/Beads/session/config paths even when they are untracked or missing ignore coverage. Apply that rule in both `RecoverWorktree(...)/cleanUntrackedFiles(...)` and the `discardDirtyState` path used by `EnsureWorktreeBranch`, so the fix closes both cleanup avenues instead of patching only one code path.

Keep the allowlist narrow and explicit. The goal is not to disable cleanup entirely, but to preserve a small set of control/runtime paths while still removing genuine per-agent debris such as stray lockfiles or unrelated temporary files. The design should treat workspace root repos and per-repo worktrees consistently: if cleanup runs against the shared root, it must preserve shared runtime state; if it runs against a normal worktree, it should still preserve Loom/Beads/session/config paths present there.

## Files to Create
- `internal/cli/daemon_runtime.go`: shared helper(s) for resolving daemon liveness and runtime metadata from lockfile/state/PID fallback, plus any path-protection helpers that are clearer outside the existing command files.
- `internal/cli/daemon_runtime_test.go`: focused tests for runtime detection precedence (lock present, PID missing; stale lock; PID fallback; inconsistent state file).

## Files to Modify
- `internal/cli/daemon_cmd.go`: route `runDaemonStatus` and `runDaemonStop` through the shared runtime-detection helper instead of trusting only `.loom/daemon.pid`.
- `internal/cli/status.go`: reuse the same daemon-runtime detection for aggregated status output so `loom status` and `loom daemon status` report the same reality.
- `internal/cli/daemon_state.go`: update or reuse state-file helpers so runtime detection can read useful metadata from `.loom/daemon-agents.json` without duplicating parsing logic.
- `internal/cli/recover_helpers.go`: replace blanket `git clean -fd` behavior with selective cleanup that preserves protected Loom/Beads/session/config paths.
- `internal/cli/daemon_branch.go`: harden `discardDirtyState` / branch-reset cleanup to preserve the same protected runtime paths during branch switching.
- `internal/cli/git.go`: add a selective clean helper (for example dry-run parse + filtered delete, or path-targeted clean) so recovery can remove only non-protected untracked files.
- `internal/cli/daemon_cmd_test.go`: add coverage for `daemon status` / `daemon stop` when PID files are missing but lock/state still indicate a live daemon.
- `internal/cli/status_test.go`: add coverage for the shared daemon detection path in status summaries.
- `internal/cli/recover_test.go`: add regression tests proving cleanup preserves `.beads/`, `.loom/`, `sessions/`, `loom.yaml`, and `AGENTS.md` while still removing unrelated junk.
- `internal/cli/daemon_branch_test.go`: add coverage proving branch-reset cleanup does not discard protected runtime state.
- `internal/cli/git_test.go`: add tests for the new filtered clean helper and its path-matching rules.
- `docs/testing/daemon-e2e/setup.sh` and/or `docs/testing/daemon-e2e/test-daemon-lifecycle.sh`: extend the existing daemon fixture/docs if needed so the observed root-repo workspace case is reproducible and can be used for manual verification.

## Dependencies
- No new external dependencies should be required.
- Reuse `internal/lockfile` for daemon-lock inspection instead of inventing a second liveness model.
- Reuse existing daemon state-file helpers and existing command-mock / output-capture patterns in `internal/cli/*_test.go`.
- Coordinate with the existing workspace-mode validation work already on `v2-workspace-guardrails`; the lifecycle fix should not reintroduce assumptions that collapse workspace repos back to unsafe shared cleanup semantics.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling
- Older daemons may have a PID file but no lock metadata. Status/stop must still work via PID fallback instead of regressing compatibility.
- A stale lock file with a dead PID must not be treated as a live daemon. Detection should verify liveness before reporting “running”.
- A live daemon with missing `.loom/daemon.pid` but valid lock/state must still report as running and stop cleanly.
- Workspace mode can target the shared root repo itself. Cleanup must preserve shared runtime state even when the repo path being cleaned is the workspace root.
- Repositories may not ignore `sessions/` or may create `loom.yaml` / `AGENTS.md` as untracked files. Preservation must not rely on `.gitignore` alone.
- Protected-path matching must normalize paths so nested files under `.loom/` or `.beads/` are preserved on both Unix and Windows path styles.
- Cleanup should remain selective: protect only known Loom/Beads/session/control paths so legitimate junk still gets removed and crash recovery does not silently accumulate unrelated files.
- If `daemon stop` cannot derive a trustworthy PID even though partial state exists, it should emit a clear recovery-oriented error instead of incorrectly saying the daemon is not running.

## Testing Strategy
- Add unit tests for daemon runtime detection precedence:
  - valid daemon lock with missing PID file still reports running
  - stale lock / dead PID reports stopped
  - PID-file-only legacy case still reports running
  - inconsistent state file does not override a valid lock-based result
- Add command tests for `runDaemonStatus` and `runDaemonStop` that capture stdout and verify they no longer print false “not running” messages when lock/state show a live supervisor.
- Add cleanup regression tests proving `RecoverWorktree` / `cleanUntrackedFiles` preserve `.beads/`, `.loom/`, `sessions/`, `loom.yaml`, and `AGENTS.md` while still removing ordinary untracked files such as `leftover.txt`.
- Add branch-reset tests proving `discardDirtyState` does not stash/drop protected runtime paths during `EnsureWorktreeBranch`.
- Extend an existing daemon lifecycle integration path (or add a focused regression variant) that reproduces the 2026-03-22 failure mode: start a real daemon in a temp repo/workspace, let an agent exit cleanly, confirm the daemon still reports running before stop, and verify runtime directories survive recovery/restart.
- Manual verification: repeat the disposable repro used during this session and confirm `loom daemon status` reports the live daemon, `loom daemon stop` terminates it successfully, and planner completion no longer deletes `.beads/`, `.loom/`, or `sessions/`.
close_reason: Completed with tests and code review. Daemon runtime detection now uses lockfile → state → PID precedence. Cleanup preserves .beads/, .loom/, sessions/, loom.yaml, AGENTS.md.

title: subscription: GetMutationsSince over-discards connection on Success=false (related to loomcli-67meg)
design:
## Summary

`DaemonSubscriber.GetMutationsSince` in `internal/webui/subscription/subscriber.go:113-132` treats every `err != nil` return from `client.GetMutations()` as a transport failure and routes the pooled connection through `pool.Discard`. But `rpc.Client.Execute` (`internal/rpc/client.go:283-285`) returns `(&resp, fmt.Errorf("operation failed: ..."))` — both non-nil — when the daemon returns `Success=false` on a fully-received response frame. In that case the connection's read buffer is drained, the transport is healthy, and `pool.Put` would be correct. The current code pessimistically discards, quietly churning pooled connections whenever the daemon reports a logical `get_mutations` failure (e.g. `"database locked"`). This is a low-priority efficiency bug only — no correctness impact, no connection corruption — and it is the OVER-discard mirror of the UNDER-discard multi-RPC bug already fixed in `pollDBChanges` (loomcli-67meg on the `nova` branch, not yet merged to `nova-fork`).

## Technical Approach

Distinguish transport error from logical failure by inspecting the returned `resp` pointer, matching the fix pattern literally stated in the bug description:

```go
resp, err := client.GetMutations(&rpc.GetMutationsArgs{Since: since})
if err != nil {
    if resp == nil {
        // Transport error — body not delivered, pipe may hold partial bytes.
        slog.Error("RPC error", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", err)
        return nil   // rpcOK stays false → Discard
    }
    // Success=false — full frame consumed, connection is clean.
    slog.Error("RPC failed", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", resp.Error)
    rpcOK = true
    return nil       // rpcOK=true → Put
}
rpcOK = true
// ... resp.Success must be true here (Execute's contract guarantees err==nil ⇒ resp.Success), but keep the defensive !resp.Success check as a belt-and-braces; fall through to json.Unmarshal.
```

Remove the now-unreachable standalone `!resp.Success` block (lines 120-123) — any `!resp.Success` path now goes through the `err != nil && resp != nil` branch above. Keep `json.Unmarshal` of `resp.Data` intact: a parse error on a fully-delivered `resp.Data` does not taint the connection, so `rpcOK` is already `true` at that point and a parse failure still lets the deferred cleanup call `Put` — which is the correct behavior (matches the convention in `waitForMutations` and the `clientHealthy=true-on-parse-failure` rule established by loomcli-67meg's design).

Why this shape:

- **Minimal**: one helper, no new package-internal API, no signature changes to exported or unexported types outside this function. The contract of `rpc.Client.Execute` ("err != nil with resp != nil means logical failure, err != nil with resp == nil means transport failure") is already stable — lean on it directly.
- **Matches the existing convention for single-RPC paths.** `GetMutationsSince` makes exactly one RPC on `client` before the defer fires, so we do not need the `clientHealthy` threading that loomcli-67meg introduced for the multi-RPC `pollDBChanges`. Introducing that machinery here would be overkill and would drift from the bug's stated scope.
- **Does not rely on string matching** on `err.Error()` to classify the failure. The `resp == nil` check is the load-bearing signal — exactly as `Execute` constructs it.

**Alternatives considered and rejected**:

1. *Also fix `waitForMutations` in the same PR*: same Success=false over-discard exists at `subscriber.go:176-188`. Rejected — the bug ticket explicitly scopes this task to `GetMutationsSince`, and `waitForMutations` has additional nuance (client-side deadline timeouts genuinely taint the pipe, per the in-source comment on line 178-181). Filed as out-of-scope below.
2. *Thread `clientHealthy` through like loomcli-67meg did for pollDBChanges*: unnecessary complexity for a single-RPC path.
3. *Switch to typed error sentinel (`errors.Is(err, rpc.ErrLogical)`)*: would require touching `internal/rpc/client.go`, which is beyond scope and would need coordination with every caller of `Execute`.

## Conventions Established

- **Single-RPC callers of `rpc.Client.Execute` (or `*.<Op>()` wrappers) must classify `err != nil` by `resp == nil`**: transport error iff `resp == nil`; logical failure iff `resp != nil`. Transport error → caller leaves its Discard-gate (`rpcOK`) unset; logical failure → caller sets `rpcOK = true` before returning.
- **Do not rely on `!resp.Success` as a standalone branch downstream of an `err != nil` check**. `Execute` returns `err != nil && !resp.Success` together, so the `!resp.Success` arm after `if err != nil { ... }` was already dead code; treat it as redundant.
- These rules are consistent with — and strictly narrower than — the `clientHealthy` threading convention established by loomcli-67meg for multi-RPC helpers. Multi-RPC paths should continue to use the `clientHealthy` convention; single-RPC paths should use the inline `resp == nil` check.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### `internal/webui/subscription/subscriber.go`

Rewrite the body of `GetMutationsSince` (lines 113-132) to the structure shown in "Technical Approach". Concretely:

- Before (lines 113-132 of nova-fork HEAD):
  ```go
  resp, err := client.GetMutations(&rpc.GetMutationsArgs{Since: since})
  if err != nil {
      slog.Error("RPC error", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", err)
      return nil
  }
  rpcOK = true

  if !resp.Success {
      slog.Error("RPC failed", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", resp.Error)
      return nil
  }

  var mutations []rpc.MutationEvent
  if err := json.Unmarshal(resp.Data, &mutations); err != nil {
      slog.Error("parse error", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", err)
      return nil
  }

  return mutations
  ```
- After:
  ```go
  resp, err := client.GetMutations(&rpc.GetMutationsArgs{Since: since})
  if err != nil {
      if resp == nil {
          slog.Error("RPC transport error", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", err)
          return nil
      }
      slog.Error("RPC failed", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", resp.Error)
      rpcOK = true
      return nil
  }
  rpcOK = true

  var mutations []rpc.MutationEvent
  if err := json.Unmarshal(resp.Data, &mutations); err != nil {
      slog.Error("parse error", "op", "GetMutationsSince", "err", err)
      return nil
  }

  return mutations
  ```

No other functions in this file are modified.

### `internal/webui/subscription/subscriber_test.go`

Two changes:

1. **Extend `subscriptionMockPool` (lines 381-432) with atomic Put/Discard counters** so tests can assert which branch fired. The existing mock indiscriminately closes the client on both Put and Discard, making the current behavior impossible to observe from tests.

   Add fields:
   ```go
   type subscriptionMockPool struct {
       socketPath   string
       clients      []*rpc.Client
       mu           sync.Mutex
       putCount     atomic.Int64
       discardCount atomic.Int64
   }
   ```

   Update `Put` and `Discard` to increment their respective counters before closing the client. Keep `PutAfterError` delegating to `Put` (increments `putCount`, not `discardCount` — that matches the current semantics).

2. **Update `TestDaemonSubscriber_GetMutationsSince_RPCFailure` (lines 697-723)** to assert `pool.putCount.Load() == 1` and `pool.discardCount.Load() == 0` after the call. This is the canonical regression guard for this bug. Today this test only asserts `result == nil`; it passes both before and after the fix, which is why the bug was shipped.

3. **Add `TestDaemonSubscriber_GetMutationsSince_TransportError`**: new test. Use a mock server that `close()`s the accepted connection immediately after reading the `get_mutations` request, without writing any response. The client's `reader.ReadBytes('\n')` returns `io.EOF` (or equivalent), so `client.GetMutations` returns `(nil, err)`. Assert:
   - `result == nil`
   - `pool.putCount.Load() == 0`
   - `pool.discardCount.Load() == 1`

   Implementation hint: add a variant of `startSubscriptionMockServerRaw` — call it `startSubscriptionMockServerDropOp(t, dropOp)` — that serves every request normally except when `req.Operation == dropOp`, in which case the goroutine returns without writing a response, causing `c.Close()` via the `defer`. The existing `startSubscriptionMockServerRaw` performs `c.Write` unconditionally, so it cannot simulate transport error on a specific op.

4. **Add `TestDaemonSubscriber_GetMutationsSince_Success_PutsConn`**: sanity regression guard on the happy path. Assert `pool.putCount.Load() == 1`, `pool.discardCount.Load() == 0`. (Can be folded into the existing `_Success` test rather than a new function — prefer amending in place to keep the test surface tight.)

5. **Add `TestDaemonSubscriber_GetMutationsSince_InvalidJSON_PutsConn`**: amend the existing `_InvalidJSON` test (lines 725-751) to assert `putCount == 1`, `discardCount == 0`. Parse errors on a fully-delivered body must NOT discard the connection — the pipe is clean.

### `internal/webui/subscription/subscriber_test.go` — imports

If `sync/atomic` is not already imported via existing tests, verify. (A quick grep: `sync/atomic` is already in the file's import block at line 12 — no import churn needed.)

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

Repo-wide grep `rg "err != nil" internal/webui/subscription/*.go | grep -v _test` + review of every `client.<Op>()` call preceded by an `rpcOK := false` / deferred `Put`/`Discard` gate surfaced the following sibling patterns with the same OVER-discard shape on logical failure (`Success=false`):

1. **`internal/webui/subscription/subscriber.go:176-188` (`waitForMutations`)** — `err != nil` unconditionally calls `s.pool.Discard(client)`. On `Success=false` from `wait_for_mutations`, this over-discards. But this site also has a load-bearing in-source comment warning that client-side deadline timeouts can leave "a stale response in the pipe", which does legitimately require Discard for transport-level timeouts. Fixing it requires the same `resp == nil` classification AND a careful audit of whether timeout errors surface `(nil, err)` — verify by reading `rpc.Client.Execute`'s timeout path. **Out of scope** — separate bug, file a new ticket referencing loomcli-zbjyl.

2. **`internal/webui/subscription/subscriber.go:287-291` + `fetchTotalCount` at lines 314-331** — `pollDBChanges` sets `rpcOK = true` only after `fetchTotalCount` returns `ok == true`. Inside `fetchTotalCount`, an `err != nil` Count result returns `(0, false)`, so the caller's `rpcOK` stays false and the defer discards — OVER-discarding for `Success=false`. **Out of scope**: this file path is already tracked by loomcli-67meg (closed on `nova` branch, not yet merged to `nova-fork`). When the `nova-fork` branch picks up the `nova` merge, the `clientHealthy` threading from 67meg will replace this `(count, ok)` signature and the bug will go away as a side effect. Do not fix twice.

3. **`internal/webui/subscription/subscriber.go:352-373` (`detectExternalChanges`)** — uses `err == nil && resp.Success` as a combined guard; returns `(false, false, lastPoll)` on any failure. This runs AFTER `pollDBChanges` has already set `rpcOK = true`, so the Discard decision is no longer gated by this helper. The bug here is the UNDER-discard (transport error on the `Count(UpdatedAfter)` call would still Put), which is the multi-RPC failure mode fixed by loomcli-67meg. **Out of scope** — covered by 67meg.

4. **`internal/webui/handlers/issues/ready.go:188-197`** — explicitly annotated in source as an "accepted trade-off" per the loomcli-67meg design. **Deliberately out of scope.**

5. **`internal/webui/service/*.go`, `internal/webui/svcimpl/*.go`, `internal/webui/terminal/*.go`, `internal/webui/fleet/handlers_claim.go:142,176`** — numerous call sites use the same `rpcOK`-gated deferred Put/Discard pattern. Per loomcli-67meg's out-of-scope list, these were already deferred. Repeat the deferral here — this ticket fixes exactly one site (`GetMutationsSince`).

## Dependencies

- No new external packages.
- Internal: unchanged. `github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/rpc` and `github.com/tysonthomas9/loomcli/internal/webui/daemon` continue to be used as-is.
- Task ordering: standalone. Does not depend on loomcli-67meg being merged into `nova-fork` — the fix is scoped to a file region that 67meg does not touch.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **`client.GetMutations` returns `(nil, err)` (transport error)**: `resp == nil` branch fires → `slog.Error("RPC transport error", ...)` → return nil without setting `rpcOK` → deferred `Discard`. Expected behavior.
- **`client.GetMutations` returns `(&resp, err)` with `!resp.Success` (logical failure)**: `resp != nil` branch fires → `slog.Error("RPC failed", ...)` with `resp.Error` → `rpcOK = true` → return nil → deferred `Put`. Expected behavior.
- **`client.GetMutations` returns `(&resp, nil)` with `resp.Success == true`**: fall through to unmarshal; `rpcOK = true` already set. Parse success → return mutations. Parse error → log, return nil, but `rpcOK` stays true → `Put`. Expected behavior (connection is clean — full frame consumed).
- **`client.GetMutations` returns `(&resp, nil)` with `resp.Success == false`**: per `rpc.Client.Execute`'s contract this cannot happen — `Execute` returns `(&resp, fmt.Errorf(...))` in that case. No dedicated branch needed. If defensive paranoia demanded it, we'd fall through to unmarshal `resp.Data` (which would likely parse to an empty slice or fail), then `Put` — safe either way, so no dedicated handling.
- **`s.pool == nil`**: early return at the top of the function is unchanged. No defer registered, no cleanup. Existing `TestDaemonSubscriber_GetMutationsSince_NilPool` continues to pass.
- **`s.pool.Get(ctx)` returns err**: early return before defer is registered. Unchanged.
- **`ctx` deadline expires during `GetMutations`**: the client's per-connection deadline (set by `rpc.Client.SetTimeout`, 5s in the mock pool) may fire instead of the acquire `ctx`. That surfaces as a read error from `reader.ReadBytes('\n')`, which `Execute` maps to `(nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read response: %w", err))`. So `resp == nil` → `Discard`. Correct — a mid-read timeout leaves unread bytes.
- **Concurrent callers**: `GetMutationsSince` is called from the SSE reconnect path (`internal/webui/sse/...` — not audited in this change). Each call acquires its own client from the pool; no shared mutable state on the client itself. No concurrency concern introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After `client.GetMutations` returns a logical failure (`resp != nil`, `!resp.Success`, `err != nil`), the deferred cleanup calls `pool.Put(client)` exactly once and `pool.Discard(client)` zero times.
2. After `client.GetMutations` returns a transport error (`resp == nil`, `err != nil`), the deferred cleanup calls `pool.Discard(client)` exactly once and `pool.Put(client)` zero times.
3. After `client.GetMutations` returns a full successful response, the deferred cleanup calls `pool.Put(client)` exactly once.
4. After `client.GetMutations` returns success but `json.Unmarshal(resp.Data, ...)` fails, the deferred cleanup calls `pool.Put(client)` exactly once — the connection is clean.
5. `GetMutationsSince` must still return `nil` for every non-success path (logical failure, transport error, parse error), preserving the current public contract. No mutations leak to callers on failure paths.
6. The log output on a logical failure path must include `resp.Error` (from the daemon) — not a generic transport error message. This is observably different from the transport-error path and aids debugging.
7. All existing tests in `internal/webui/subscription/...` pass unchanged semantically. The three existing `GetMutationsSince_*` tests (`_Success`, `_RPCFailure`, `_InvalidJSON`, `_EmptyMutations`) continue to return the same `result` as today.
8. The new regression tests assert on `putCount` / `discardCount` counters so the fix is behaviorally observable, not just internal code reshuffling.
9. `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./internal/webui/subscription/...` produce no new findings.
10. No change to exported API of `DaemonSubscriber`. `subscriptionMockPool` is test-only and unexported — extending it is a test-internal refactor.

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests (primary)**:

- Extend `subscriptionMockPool` with `putCount atomic.Int64` and `discardCount atomic.Int64` and increment on each call.
- Add `startSubscriptionMockServerDropOp(t, dropOp string)` helper that serves requests normally but closes the connection without responding when `req.Operation == dropOp`. Required because the existing helper always writes a response, so it cannot simulate a transport-level failure on a specific RPC.
- Test matrix for `GetMutationsSince`:

  | Scenario                                                              | Existing test                              | New/modified assertion         |
  |-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
  | Success path, mutations returned                                      | `_Success` (line 657)                      | `putCount == 1, discardCount == 0` |
  | Success path, empty mutations                                         | `_EmptyMutations` (line 754)               | `putCount == 1, discardCount == 0` |
  | Logical failure (`Success=false`)                                     | `_RPCFailure` (line 698)                   | `putCount == 1, discardCount == 0` ← FIX VERIFIER |
  | Success path but malformed JSON body                                  | `_InvalidJSON` (line 726)                  | `putCount == 1, discardCount == 0` |
  | Transport error (socket closed mid-read of `get_mutations` response)  | **NEW**: `_TransportError`                 | `putCount == 0, discardCount == 1` |
  | Nil pool                                                              | `_NilPool` (line 79)                       | no pool interaction — counters unchanged (implicitly 0) |

- The `_RPCFailure` assertion (row 3) is the canonical regression guard: before the fix, `putCount == 0, discardCount == 1`; after the fix, `putCount == 1, discardCount == 0`. This is the one assertion that will go red on revert and green on fix.

**Manual verification**:

1. `go test ./internal/webui/subscription/... -race -count=5` — all tests pass cleanly, race detector clean.
2. `go build ./...` — compile check for any call-site drift (there are no external callers of `GetMutationsSince` that rely on behavior beyond the `[]rpc.MutationEvent` return, so compile should be trivial).
3. Exercise the SSE reconnect flow manually: start `loom serve`, connect an SSE client, kill the daemon, bring it back, and confirm that on daemon restart the catch-up `get_mutations` call does not now silently churn pool connections. (Low-priority manual check — the fix is purely an efficiency bump, not a correctness change.)

**Regression guard**:

- `go test ./internal/webui/subscription/... -race -count=20` stress-loop to catch any concurrency regression introduced by the counter increments.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/webui/subscription/...` — confirm no new findings (e.g., unused variable from removed dead branch).
